motivation: To resolve ambiguities in defining quantumness for individual processes and to uncover nonclassical features that could enable new technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational probabilistic theories, introducing a criterion that separates classical and nonclassical processes.
result: The unified rule recovers standard quantum signatures (e.g., Bell nonlocality) and identifies new nonclassical behaviors in processes like entanglement swapping and quantum teleportation.
conclusion: The boundary between classical and quantum is broader than previously thought, with many 'classical' processes possessing intrinsic quantumness that may be harnessed for quantum information tasks.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing useful entangled states.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via cavity loss to drive the system into desired entangled steady states, with reconfigurability through external drives.
result: They show that the dissipative protocol can generate various entangled states (e.g., spin-squeezed states, topological states) with high fidelity and robustness against imperfections.
conclusion: The approach provides a scalable and practical platform for quantum sensing and many-body physics, leveraging dissipation as a tool rather than a hindrance.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can be resource-intensive; passive schemes could simplify implementation.
method: The authors design a bosonic code that corrects photon loss errors using continuous drives without active measurements, and experimentally demonstrate it.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits of the constituent components, reaching the breakeven point where error correction begins to improve performance.
conclusion: Passive error correction is a viable approach for protecting quantum information against photon loss, with potential for simpler hardware requirements.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine a novel discrete modulation scheme with a security analysis based on the entropy accumulation theorem, achieving composable security against collective attacks.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 50 km, with composable security guarantees.
conclusion: This work brings high-speed, secure quantum key distribution closer to practical deployment in quantum networks.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies and mitigates loss mechanisms in high-coherence multimode mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, improving phonon coherence time and cooperativity.
motivation: Mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits are promising for quantum information processing, but their performance is limited by loss mechanisms that are not well understood.
method: The authors optimize piezoelectric transducer properties in bulk acoustic resonators and characterize loss channels through systematic experiments and materials analysis.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence times and cooperativity, and provide a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding and performance of hybrid quantum systems involving mechanical resonators and superconducting circuits, enabling better quantum transducers and memory.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: A protocol for preparing high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity.
motivation: Distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation requires high-fidelity logical Bell pairs, but existing methods have high overhead or require complex connectivity.
method: The protocol uses entanglement boosting, combining multiple noisy physical Bell pairs and error correction to distill a logical Bell pair with improved fidelity, requiring only 2D local device connectivity.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with significantly lower spacetime volume compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: This work enables practical distributed quantum computation by reducing the resource overhead for logical Bell pair generation.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A new SDP hierarchy certifies non-projective measurements, demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are limited.
method: A complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is developed to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones.
result: The hierarchy provides robust certification, and the method is experimentally validated on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of quantum measurements and offers a practical tool for device certification.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum devices. The authors aim to quantify the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of a quantum detector operating autonomously.
method: The authors model a quantum particle as a detector that interacts with a system and a thermal bath, deriving bounds on entropy production and measurement accuracy using stochastic thermodynamics and information theory.
result: They find a trade-off relation between the entropy produced by the detector and the accuracy of the measurement, showing that higher accuracy requires more dissipation.
conclusion: The results establish fundamental thermodynamic limits on quantum measurement, with implications for the design of energy-efficient quantum sensors and autonomous quantum machines.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral diffusion and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits performance. Understanding and mitigating these instabilities is essential for practical quantum repeaters and memories.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on erbium ions coupled to silicon photonic crystal cavities, measuring spectral diffusion and coherence times under various conditions.
result: They identify charge fluctuations in the silicon host as the primary cause of spectral diffusion, and demonstrate that operating at cryogenic temperatures and using specific cavity designs can significantly improve stability.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon can achieve the spectral stability required for quantum networking, with identified mitigation strategies paving the way for scalable quantum repeaters.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited control. This work aims to overcome these challenges to generate large cluster states.
method: The authors propose a control framework that uses global driving and optical heralding to entangle inhomogeneous spin ensembles, leveraging the Tavis-Cummings model and hole-burning techniques.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and scalability to 10–100 qubits with low experimental overhead, validated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical path toward programmable quantum matter and large-scale cluster states for quantum information processing.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the decodability of quantum codes under random monitoring, revealing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding performance.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect quantum error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in the context of monitored dynamics.
method: The authors analyze the stability of quantum codes under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics, using random monitoring protocols.
result: They show that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, providing new insights into the interplay between measurement and error correction.
conclusion: Randomly monitored quantum codes offer a promising avenue for improving quantum error correction, with potential applications in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating miniaturized device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: Device-independent quantum random number generation (DI-QRNG) provides security without trusting the hardware, but existing implementations are bulky and complex. An integrated photonic solution is needed for practical, scalable deployment.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that performs a self-testing protocol based on Bell inequality violation, using integrated entangled photon sources and on-chip detectors to generate and certify randomness.
result: The chip successfully generates certified randomness with a finite-size security proof, achieving a randomness generation rate suitable for real-world applications while maintaining device-independent security guarantees.
conclusion: This work demonstrates the feasibility of fully integrated DI-QRNG on a photonic chip, paving the way for compact, low-cost quantum security devices for widespread use.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance.
method: The authors introduce a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed approach significantly reduces the number of required emitters and improves the loss tolerance of quantum repeaters, making them more feasible for near-term implementation.
conclusion: Hierarchical and asymmetric tree-codes offer a practical path toward resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep-level spin defect in ZnO with exceptional coherence and readout fidelity, positioning ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Current quantum platforms face challenges in scalability and coherence; wide-bandgap oxides like ZnO may offer new defect-based qubits with superior properties.
method: The authors characterize a deep-level defect in ZnO using first-principles calculations and experimental measurements, evaluating electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
result: The defect exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity, enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO deep spin defects are a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies, combining long coherence with practical readout capabilities.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume ideal devices, but real devices have imperfections that can compromise security. A rigorous framework is needed to account for device characterization in security proofs.
method: The authors develop a composable security proof framework that integrates device characterization parameters, allowing for quantitative security guarantees based on measured device properties.
result: The framework yields rigorous security bounds that depend on device characterization, enabling standards and certification for QKD devices.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and theoretically sound approach to bridge the gap between ideal security proofs and real-world QKD implementations.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can significantly boost logical qubit performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement a dispersive readout scheme to detect relaxation events as erasures.
result: They demonstrate that erasure conversion effectively suppresses the impact of energy relaxation, leading to enhanced effective coherence times.
conclusion: Erasure conversion in integer fluxonium qubits offers a practical path to improved quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, given that classical gravity with quantum matter leads to inconsistencies; information-theoretic methods provide a framework to constrain possible theories.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two quantum probes, analyzing their feasibility and implications.
result: Several potentially feasible GIE experiments are identified, which could test the quantum nature of gravity without requiring high energies.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantum nature of gravity, with GIE experiments being a promising avenue.

title: Geometric Speed Limit Of State Preparation And Curved Control Spaces
authors: Maximilian Goll And Robert H. Jonsson
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2160 (2026).

The preparation of quantum many-body systems faces the difficulty that in a realistic scenario only few control parameters of the system may be accessible. In this context, an interesting connection between the energy fluctuations during state preparation and its geometric length as measured by the Fubini-Study metric was discussed by Bukov et al. in 2019 [5]. An inspiring conjecture lower bounding the energy fluctuations by the minimal geometric length of all accessible state preparation protocols was put forward together with supporting examples and numerical evidence. However, we here show that the conjecture does not hold but can be violated if the accessible parameter space has extrinsic curvature, when embedded into the space of all dynamically accessible states. We illustrate this by a number of generic qubit, qutrit and harmonic oscillator systems.

.
tldr: This paper disproves a conjecture linking energy fluctuations to geometric length in state preparation, showing that curved control spaces can violate the bound.
motivation: Understanding fundamental limits on state preparation is crucial for quantum control and thermodynamics. The conjecture offered a promising lower bound on energy fluctuations via geometric length.
method: The authors analyze the geometry of state preparation protocols using the Fubini-Study metric and consider control spaces with extrinsic curvature. They construct counterexamples in qubit, qutrit, and harmonic oscillator systems.
result: The conjecture is violated when the accessible parameter space has extrinsic curvature; the minimal geometric length does not always lower bound energy fluctuations.
conclusion: The geometric speed limit is more subtle than previously thought, and curvature of control spaces must be accounted for in fundamental bounds on state preparation.

title: From Superradiance To Superabsorption: An Exact Treatment Of Non-Markovian Cooperative Radiation
authors: Ignacio González And Ángel Rivas
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2159 (2026).

We investigate the emergence of cooperative radiation phenomena in ensembles of two-level atoms coupled to a lossy resonant cavity beyond the Markovian and mean-field approximations. By deriving a complete analytical solution for the two-emitter case and employing a numerically exact method for larger ensembles, we characterize the full transition from Markovian to non-Markovian collective dynamics for systems of up to [MATH] emitters. Our results reveal three distinct regimes: a Markovian phase exhibiting the standard superradiant burst, a non-Markovian phase featuring spontaneous superabsorption of the emitted field, and a critical regime marked by pulsed collective emission. We show that the critical spectral width separating these behaviors increases monotonically with the number of emitters, demonstrating that environmental memory effects can be enhanced by cooperativity. Finally, we find that the superradiant scaling of the peak intensity progressively degrades with increasing system size, approaching a subquadratic law in the limit of a perfect cavity. In this regime, spontaneous superabsorption emerges as a distinct manifestation of non-Markovian cooperativity.

.
tldr: This paper analytically and numerically studies non-Markovian cooperative radiation in two-level atoms coupled to a lossy cavity, revealing superabsorption and critical regimes.
motivation: Understanding cooperative radiation beyond Markovian and mean-field approximations is crucial for quantum information processing with hybrid systems.
method: The authors derive an exact analytical solution for two emitters and use a numerically exact method for larger ensembles to characterize the transition from Markovian to non-Markovian collective dynamics.
result: They identify three regimes: Markovian superradiance, non-Markovian superabsorption, and a critical regime with pulsed emission; superradiant peak intensity scaling degrades with system size, approaching subquadratic in the perfect cavity limit.
conclusion: Environmental memory effects can be enhanced by cooperativity, and spontaneous superabsorption emerges as a distinct non-Markovian cooperative phenomenon.

title: Towards Unconditional Uncloneable Encryption
authors: Pierre Botteron, Anne Broadbent, Eric Culf, Ion Nechita, Clément Pellegrini, And Denis Rochette
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2157 (2026).

Uncloneable encryption is a cryptographic primitive which encrypts a classical message into a quantum ciphertext, such that two quantum adversaries are limited in their capacity of being able to simultaneously decrypt, given the key and quantum side-information produced from the ciphertext. Since its initial proposal and scheme in the random oracle model by Broadbent and Lord [TQC 2020], uncloneable encryption has developed into an important primitive at the foundation of quantum uncloneability for cryptographic primitives. Despite sustained efforts, however, the question of unconditional uncloneable encryption (and in particular of the simplest case, called an uncloneable bit) has remained elusive. Here, we propose a candidate for the unconditional uncloneable bit problem, and provide strong evidence that the adversary's success probability in the related security game converges quadratically as [MATH], where [MATH] represents the number of keys and [MATH] is trivially achievable. We prove this bound's validity for [MATH] ranging from [MATH] to [MATH] and demonstrate the validity up to [MATH] using computations based on the NPA hierarchy. We furthemore provide compelling heuristic evidence towards the general case. In addition, we prove an asymptotic upper bound of [MATH] and give a numerical upper bound of [MATH], which to our knowledge is the best-known value in the unconditional model.

.
tldr: Proposes a candidate for unconditional uncloneable encryption and provides strong evidence for its security.
motivation: Uncloneable encryption is a fundamental primitive in quantum cryptography, but unconditional security (without random oracles) has remained elusive.
method: The authors propose a scheme for uncloneable bit encryption and analyze its security using the NPA hierarchy and analytical bounds.
result: They prove that the adversary's success probability converges quadratically with the number of keys, and provide numerical bounds up to n=7.
conclusion: The work provides strong evidence for the feasibility of unconditional uncloneable encryption, advancing the foundations of quantum cryptography.

title: A Complexity Theory For Non-local Quantum Computation
authors: Andreas Bluhm, Simon Höfer, Alex May, Mikka Stasiuk, Philip Verduyn Lunel, And Henry Yuen
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2152 (2026).

Non-local quantum computation (NLQC) replaces a local interaction between two systems with a single round of communication and shared entanglement. Despite many partial results, it is known that a characterization of entanglement cost in at least certain NLQC tasks would imply significant breakthroughs in complexity theory. Here, we avoid these obstructions and take an indirect approach to understanding resource requirements in NLQC, which mimics the approach used by complexity theorists: we study the relative hardness of different NLQC tasks by identifying resource efficient reductions between them. Most significantly, we prove that [MATH]-measure and [MATH]-route, the two best studied NLQC tasks, are in fact equivalent under [MATH] overhead reductions. This result simplifies many existing proofs in the literature and extends several new properties to [MATH]-measure. For instance, we obtain sub-exponential upper bounds on [MATH]-measure for all functions, and efficient protocols for functions in the complexity class [MATH]. Beyond this, we study a number of other examples of NLQC tasks and their relationships.

.
tldr: This paper develops a complexity-theoretic framework for non-local quantum computation, showing equivalence between key tasks and establishing resource-efficient reductions.
motivation: Characterizing entanglement cost in non-local quantum computation is known to be hard; the authors aim to circumvent this by studying relative hardness via reductions, similar to complexity theory.
method: They define resource-efficient reductions between NLQC tasks and prove that the two main tasks, f-measure and f-route, are equivalent under polynomial overhead reductions.
result: They obtain sub-exponential upper bounds on f-measure for all functions and efficient protocols for functions in the complexity class P, and extend several properties from f-route to f-measure.
conclusion: The reduction approach simplifies existing proofs and provides new insights into the resource requirements of non-local quantum computation, linking it to complexity classes.

title: Entanglement In The Dicke Subspace
authors: Aabhas Gulati, Ion Nechita, And Clément Pellegrini
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2150 (2026).

We provide a complete mathematical theory for the entanglement of mixtures of Dicke states. These quantum states form an important subclass of bosonic states arising in the study of indistinguishable particles. We introduce a tensor-based parametrization where the diagonal entries of these states are encoded as a symmetric tensor, enabling a direct translation between entanglement properties and well-studied convex cones of tensors. Our results bridge multipartite entanglement theory with semialgebraic geometry and the theory of completely positive and copositive tensors. This dictionary maps separability to completely positive tensors, the PPT property to moment tensors, entanglement witnesses to copositive tensors, and decomposable witnesses to sum of squares tensors. We establish that PPT entanglement exists for all multipartite systems with local dimension [MATH] and [MATH] parties, disproving a recent conjecture. We also show that, for mixtures of Dicke states, the PPT condition with respect to the most balanced bipartition implies all other PPT conditions. We further connect bosonic extendibility of mixtures of Dicke states to the duals of known hierarchies for non-negative polynomials, such as the ones by Reznick and Polya. We thus provide semidefinite programming relaxations for separability and entanglement testing in the Dicke subspace.

.
tldr: Provides a complete mathematical theory for entanglement of mixtures of Dicke states, linking multipartite entanglement to convex cones of tensors.
motivation: To develop a unified framework for understanding entanglement in the important class of Dicke states, which arise in bosonic systems.
method: Introduces a tensor-based parametrization mapping separability to completely positive tensors, PPT property to moment tensors, and entanglement witnesses to copositive tensors.
result: Proves existence of PPT entanglement for all multipartite systems with local dimension ≥3 and ≥3 parties, disproving a recent conjecture, and shows PPT condition for the most balanced bipartition implies all others.
conclusion: The tensor dictionary provides new tools for entanglement detection and classification in Dicke subspace, with semidefinite programming relaxations for separability testing.

title: Measuring Rényi Entropy With An Echo Protocol
authors: Yi-Neng Zhou, Robin Löwenberg, And Julian Sonner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2146 (2026).

We present efficient and practical protocols to measure the second Rényi entropy, whose exponential is known as the purity. Our approach is based on expressing the purity in terms of transition probabilities generated by an echo-type forward-backward evolution sequence, making it applicable to quantum many-body systems. Notably, our approach does not rely on random-noise averaging, a feature that can be extended to protocols to measure out-of-time-order correlation functions, as we demonstrate. By way of example, we show that our protocols can be practically implemented in superconducting qubit-based platforms, as well as in cavity-QED trapped ultra-cold gases.

.
tldr: Presents efficient echo-based protocols to measure the second Rényi entropy (purity) in quantum many-body systems without random-noise averaging.
motivation: Measuring Rényi entropy is crucial for characterizing entanglement and quantum correlations, but existing methods often require random averaging or are inefficient.
method: The purity is expressed in terms of transition probabilities from an echo-type forward-backward evolution sequence, avoiding random-noise averaging; the protocol is extended to out-of-time-order correlators.
result: The protocols are shown to be practically implementable on superconducting qubit platforms and cavity-QED trapped ultracold gases.
conclusion: The work provides efficient, noise-avoiding measurement schemes for Rényi entropy, advancing experimental quantum information processing.

title: Active Quantum Reservoir Engineering: Using A Qubit To Manipulate Its Environment
authors: Marcelo Janovitch, Matteo Brunelli, And Patrick P. Potts
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2143 (2026).

Quantum reservoir engineering leverages dissipative processes to achieve desired behaviour, with applications ranging from entanglement generation to quantum error correction. Therein, a structured environment acts as an entropy sink for the system and no time-dependent control over the system is required. We develop a theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering, where time-dependent control over a quantum system is used to manipulate its environment. In this case, the system may act as an entropy sink for the environment. Our framework captures the dynamical interplay between system and environment, and provides an intuitive picture of how finite-size effects and system-environment correlations allow for manipulating the environment by repeated initialisation of the quantum system. We illustrate our results with two examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to an environment of two-level systems and a semiconducting quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins. In both scenarios, we find qualitative agreement with previous experimental results, illustrating how active control can unlock new functionalities in open quantum systems.

.
tldr: A theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering where time-dependent control over a quantum system manipulates its environment, with applications to open quantum systems.
motivation: Standard reservoir engineering uses structured environments as entropy sinks, but active control can unlock new functionalities by allowing the system to act as an entropy sink for the environment.
method: The authors develop a framework capturing the dynamical interplay between system and environment, including finite-size effects and correlations, and illustrate with two examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to two-level systems and a quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins.
result: Qualitative agreement with previous experimental results is found, showing that repeated initialization of the quantum system can manipulate the environment.
conclusion: Active control can enable new functionalities in open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Decoupling Local Classicality From Classical Explainability: A Noncontextual Model For Bilocal Classical Theory And A Locally-classical But Contextual Theory
authors: Sina Soltani, Marco Erba, David Schmid, And John H.selby
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2142 (2026).

We construct an ontological model for the theory known as bilocal classical theory [1]. To our knowledge, this is only the second time that an ontological model has been constructed for an entire theory, rather than just for some particular scenarios within a theory. This result refutes a conjecture from [1] which suggested that there might be no local-realist ontological model for bilocal classical theory. Moreover, it is the first time that an ontological model has been constructed for a theory that fails to be locally tomographic, showing that the assumption of local tomography underpinning the structure theorem in [2] is a genuine limitation of the theorem. This demonstrates that in general there is no tension between failures of local tomography and classical explainability (i.e., generalised noncontextuality). In fact, bilocal classical theory is in many ways more simply understood via the underlying ontological model than it is within its original formulation (much as how odd-dimensional stabiliser subtheories can be more simply understood via Spekkens' toy theory). Furthermore, this result naturally leads to the question, does every locally-classical theory admit of an ontological model? By constructing a concrete counterexample, we show that this is not the case. Our findings demonstrate that there is no straightforward relationship between theories being locally-classical, and them being classically-explainable. This shows that the fundamental status of compositional properties (such as local tomography) is not a technical side-issue, but a central and unavoidable question for a coherent understanding even of classicality itself.

.
tldr: Constructs an ontological model for bilocal classical theory, refuting a conjecture and showing that local classicality does not imply classical explainability.
motivation: To understand the relationship between local tomography, local classicality, and generalized noncontextuality, and to test whether every locally-classical theory admits an ontological model.
method: Constructs an explicit ontological model for bilocal classical theory using a generalized noncontextual framework, and then builds a counterexample of a locally-classical but contextual theory.
result: Bilocal classical theory has a local-realist ontological model, contrary to a previous conjecture; local classicality does not guarantee classical explainability.
conclusion: Compositional properties like local tomography are central to understanding classicality, and there is no straightforward link between local classicality and noncontextuality.

title: Tight Bounds For Quantum Phase Estimation And Related Problems
authors: Nikhil S. Mande And Ronald de Wolf
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2140 (2026).

Phase estimation, due to Kitaev [17], is one of the most fundamental subroutines in quantum computing. In the basic scenario, one is given black-box access to a unitary [MATH], and an eigenstate [MATH] of [MATH] with unknown eigenvalue [MATH], and the task is to estimate the eigenphase [MATH] within [MATH], with high probability. The cost of an algorithm for us is the number of applications of [MATH] and [MATH]. We tightly characterize the cost of several variants of phase estimation where we are no longer given an eigenstate, but are required to estimate the maximum eigenphase of [MATH], aided by advice in the form of states (or a unitary preparing those states) which are promised to have at least a certain overlap [MATH] with the top eigenspace. We give algorithms and nearly matching lower bounds for all ranges of parameters. We show that a small number of copies of the advice state (or of an advice-preparing unitary) are not significantly better than having no advice at all. We also show that having lots of advice (applications of the advice-preparing unitary) does not significantly reduce cost, and neither does knowledge of the eigenbasis of [MATH]. We immediately obtain a lower bound on the complexity of the Unitary recurrence time problem, resolving an open question of She and Yuen [29]. Lastly, we study how efficiently one can reduce the error probability in the basic phase-estimation scenario. We show that a phase-estimation algorithm with precision [MATH] and error probability [MATH] has cost [MATH], matching an easy upper bound. This contrasts with some other scenarios in quantum computing (e.g., search) where error-probability reduction costs only a factor [MATH]. Our lower bound uses a variant of the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials.

.
tldr: This paper tightly characterizes the query complexity of quantum phase estimation with advice states, providing nearly matching upper and lower bounds for all parameter regimes.
motivation: Phase estimation is a fundamental subroutine in quantum computing, but its cost when given advice states (e.g., copies of an eigenstate) was not fully understood. The authors aim to close this gap and resolve related open problems.
method: The authors develop algorithms for phase estimation with advice and prove lower bounds using the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials, as well as reductions from the unitary recurrence time problem.
result: They show that a small number of advice copies do not significantly help, and that having many copies does not reduce cost much either. They also derive a tight bound for error probability reduction in basic phase estimation.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of the cost of phase estimation with advice, resolving open questions and offering insights into the power of quantum advice.

title: Qudit Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt Inequality And Nonlocality From Wigner Negativity
authors: Uta Isabella Meyer, Ivan Šupić, Damian Markham, And Frédéric Grosshans
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2139 (2026).

Nonlocality is an essential concept that distinguishes quantum from classical models and has been extensively studied in systems of qubits. For higher-dimensional systems, certain results for their two-level counterpart, like Bell violations with stabilizer states and Clifford operators, do not generalize. On the other hand, similar to continuous variable systems, Wigner negativity is necessary for nonlocality in qudit systems. We propose a new generalization of the CHSH inequality for qudits by inquiring correlations related to the Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under the adjoint action of a generalization of the qubit [MATH]-gate. A specified stabilizer state maximally violates the inequality among all qudit states based on its Wigner negativity. The Bell operator not only serves as a measure for the singlet fraction but also quantifies the volume of Wigner negativity. Additionally, we show how a bipartite entangled qudit state can serve as a witness for contextuality when it exhibits Wigner negativity. Furthermore, we identify rational-phase diagonal unitaries as the key resource that exactly reproduce the CGLMP and SATWAP violation with the maximally entangled state through simple phase-difference alignment.

.
tldr: Proposes a qudit CHSH inequality based on Wigner negativity, showing that stabilizer states with maximal Wigner negativity achieve maximal violation, and connects the Bell operator to singlet fraction and Wigner negativity volume.
motivation: Generalizing Bell inequalities to higher-dimensional systems is important for understanding nonlocality, but known results for qubits do not straightforwardly extend. This work aims to derive a qudit CHSH inequality that directly relates to Wigner negativity, a known necessary resource for nonlocality in continuous-variable and qudit systems.
method: The authors introduce a new CHSH-like inequality for qudits by considering correlations tied to the Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under the adjoint action of a generalized qubit T-gate. They analyze the maximal violation achievable by any qudit state and show it is attained by a specific stabilizer state with maximal Wigner negativity.
result: The proposed inequality is maximally violated by a stabilizer state with maximal Wigner negativity, and the Bell operator quantifies both the singlet fraction and the volume of Wigner negativity. Additionally, bipartite entangled qudit states with Wigner negativity serve as witnesses for contextuality, and rational-phase diagonal unitaries reproduce known violations (CGLMP, SATWAP) via phase-difference alignment.
conclusion: The work establishes a direct link between Wigner negativity and nonlocality in qudit systems, providing a new Bell inequality that is operationally meaningful and connects to contextuality. This advances the understanding of quantum correlations beyond qubits.

title: Distributing Graph States With A Photon-weaving Quantum Server
authors: Daniel Bhatti And Kenneth Goodenough
abstract: One of the key aims of quantum networks is the efficient distribution of multipartite entangled states among end users. While various architectures have been proposed, each comes with distinct advantages and limitations. Many designs depend on long-lived quantum memories and deterministic gates, which, while powerful, introduce considerable cost and technical challenges. Experimentally cheaper alternatives that circumvent these constraints are often limited to specific types of entanglement and a specific number of users. Here, we present an experiment-friendly quantum server that relies only on linear optical elements, offering a flexible approach to multipartite entanglement distribution. Our so-called photon-weaving quantum server can generate and distribute one of several locally nonequivalent graph states, including Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger (GHZ) states, as well as path, cycle, and caterpillar graph states. This is achieved through two distinct fusion protocols, i.e. multiphoton graph-state fusion (graph-state weaving) and multiphoton GHZ-state fusion (GHZ-state weaving), and can readily be implemented.
tldr: Proposes an experiment-friendly quantum server using linear optics to distribute various graph states among end users.
motivation: Efficient distribution of multipartite entangled states is key for quantum networks, but existing architectures often require costly long-lived quantum memories and deterministic gates.
method: The server uses two fusion protocols—graph-state weaving and GHZ-state weaving—with only linear optical elements to generate and distribute graph states.
result: The server can generate GHZ states, path, cycle, and caterpillar graph states, offering flexibility in entanglement distribution without expensive resources.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, scalable approach to multipartite entanglement distribution, advancing quantum network implementations.

title: Gap Between Quantum Theory Based On Real And Complex Numbers Is Arbitrarily Large
authors: Shubhayan Sarkar, David Trillo, Marc Olivier Renou And Remigiusz Augusiak
abstract: Quantum information theory, the formalism for representing information contained in quantum systems, is based on complex Hilbert spaces. It was recently shown that in quantum networks involving three parties with nontrivial locality constraints, this formalism predicts correlations that cannot be explained by real quantum theory, a variant of quantum mechanics based on real Hilbert spaces. In this work, we study a scenario with parties sharing quantum systems in a star network. We then construct a multipartite Bell inequality that exhibits a gap between quantum theory and its variant based on real numbers, which grows linearly with , and is thus arbitrarily large in the asymptotic limit. This implies, that, as the number of parties grows, Hilbert space formalism based on real numbers becomes exceedingly worse at describing complex networks of quantum systems. We also compute the tolerance of this gap to experimental errors.
tldr: This paper shows that the gap between real and complex quantum theory in star networks grows linearly with the number of parties, making real quantum theory arbitrarily worse for describing quantum networks.
motivation: Recent work demonstrated that complex Hilbert spaces are necessary to reproduce certain quantum correlations in networks. This paper aims to quantify how much more powerful complex quantum theory is over real quantum theory as the network size increases.
method: The authors consider a star network configuration with multiple parties sharing quantum systems. They construct a multipartite Bell inequality and analyze the violation achievable by complex quantum theory versus real quantum theory, deriving a linear scaling of the gap with the number of parties.
result: The gap between the maximal violation of the Bell inequality in complex quantum theory and that in real quantum theory grows linearly with the number of parties, becoming arbitrarily large in the asymptotic limit. The tolerance to experimental errors is also computed.
conclusion: Complex quantum theory is fundamentally more powerful than real quantum theory for describing correlations in large quantum networks, implying that real Hilbert spaces are insufficient for quantum information processing in such settings.

title: Information Compression At Criticality
authors: Simon Jiricek, Miroslav Hopjan, Boris Altshuler, Vladimir Kravtsov, Lev Vidmar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Highly excited quantum states at the critical boundary of ergodicity are known to deviate from thermal behavior, yet their dynamical properties remain poorly understood. Here, we uncover the complexity of quantum dynamics at criticality through the lens of intrinsic information compression in energy space. We show that the Hamiltonian spectrum can be systematically truncated, yielding a simplified description of the dynamics while preserving its essential features. Specifically, for both interacting and noninteracting systems, we demonstrate that a vanishing fraction of Hamiltonian eigenlevels suffices to reproduce the power-law decay of the survival probability. The resulting truncated spectrum exhibits a fractal structure characterized by a level-spacing distribution with a power-law tail, while its spectral form factor displays the same asymptotic power-law decay as the survival probability.
tldr: This paper shows that the Hamiltonian spectrum at criticality can be truncated to a vanishing fraction of eigenlevels while preserving the power-law decay of survival probability, revealing fractal spectral structures.
motivation: Understanding quantum dynamics at the critical boundary of ergodicity is challenging; the authors aim to characterize the complexity of such dynamics via information compression in energy space.
method: They systematically truncate the Hamiltonian spectrum and analyze the resulting survival probability, level-spacing distribution, and spectral form factor for both interacting and noninteracting systems.
result: A vanishing fraction of eigenlevels suffices to reproduce the power-law decay of survival probability; the truncated spectrum exhibits fractal structure with power-law tail in level-spacing distribution.
conclusion: The findings provide a simplified description of quantum dynamics at criticality, linking spectral properties to dynamical behavior and offering insights into the complexity of many-body systems.

The analysis covers both interacting and noninteracting systems, demonstrating the universality of the phenomenon.

title: From Canonical To Tunable Phase Diagrams In Open Quantum Long-Range Systems
authors: Shamik Gupta Anish Acharya
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the dissipative dynamics of a generalized Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick (LMG) model coupled to a thermal environment. In this generalized model, in addition to the conventional quadratic interaction, one considers quartic interactions between spin-[MATH]'s coupled all-to-all and evolving in presence of a transverse field. Employing the usual linear Lindblad master equation with thermally-balanced jump processes, we derive magnetisation evolution equations, and demonstrate that the corresponding stationary solution reproduces the canonical equilibrium phase diagram of the model. We then extend our analysis to a nonlinear Lindblad equation that incorporates imperfect quantum-jump processes in terms of jump-retention parameters. Here, remarkably, the system relaxes to a genuine nonequilibrium stationary state whose properties differ qualitatively from those obtained in the linear case. The jump-retention parameters provide tunable knobs that shift the phase boundaries and even modify the nature of the phase transitions with respect to the linear case. Our exact results establish a direct connection between dissipative relaxation dynamics and stationary-state behavior, while identifying controlled quantum-jump retention as a mechanism for engineering nonequilibrium phases in long-range interacting open quantum systems.
tldr: This paper studies the dissipative dynamics of a generalized LMG model with quartic interactions, showing that nonlinear Lindblad equations with jump-retention parameters yield tunable nonequilibrium phase diagrams.
motivation: To understand how controlled quantum-jump retention can engineer nonequilibrium phases in long-range interacting open quantum systems, bridging dissipative relaxation dynamics and stationary-state behavior.
method: The authors derive magnetization evolution equations from linear and nonlinear Lindblad master equations for a generalized LMG model, analyzing stationary solutions and phase diagrams.
result: The linear Lindblad equation reproduces the canonical equilibrium phase diagram, while the nonlinear equation with jump-retention parameters shifts phase boundaries and modifies the nature of phase transitions, enabling tunable nonequilibrium phases.
conclusion: Controlled quantum-jump retention provides a mechanism for engineering nonequilibrium phases in long-range interacting open quantum systems, establishing a direct connection between dissipative dynamics and stationary states.

title: Simulating The Dicke Model On Qubit-Based And Hybrid Qubit-Boson-Based Quantum Computers
authors: Aravind P. Babu, Seongjin Ahn, Jing Sun, Augustas G. Landsbergis, Andrey S. Moskalenko, Marko J. Ran\v{c}i\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Dicke model provides a fundamental description of collective light-matter interactions and has long served as a testbed for exploring a wide range of physical phenomena in quantum optics and condensed matter physics. In this work, we develop a variational framework for investigating the finite-size Dicke model on both fully qubit-based (digital) and hybrid qubit boson based (digital-analogue) quantum computing platforms. We show that the resulting model reproduces the characteristic critical behavior of the Dicke model in the appropriate large-spin limit while remaining suitable for implementation on both classical emulators of quantum computers and actual trapped ion quantum computers, albeit in the case of latter somewhat limited by noise. Finally, we introduce a complementary hybrid qubit-bosonic variational ansatz that directly exploits the bosonic degree of freedom to reduce quantum resources and discuss its potential implementation on hybrid quantum hardware. Our results establish a scalable, symmetry-aware framework for variational quantum simulations of collective light-matter systems and provide a pathway toward efficient simulations of more general spin-boson models on near-term quantum devices.
tldr: Develops variational quantum simulation frameworks for the Dicke model on qubit-based and hybrid qubit-boson platforms, demonstrating critical behavior and resource reduction.
motivation: The Dicke model is fundamental for light-matter interactions, but simulating it on near-term quantum devices is challenging; a scalable, symmetry-aware variational approach is needed.
method: Proposes a variational ansatz for the Dicke model on digital (qubit-only) and digital-analog (qubit-boson) quantum computers, using symmetry constraints and classical emulation plus trapped-ion experiments.
result: The model reproduces the Dicke phase transition in the large-spin limit, and the hybrid ansatz reduces quantum resources while remaining implementable on current hardware, albeit with noise limitations.
conclusion: Establishes a scalable framework for simulating collective light-matter systems on near-term quantum devices, with potential extension to general spin-boson models.

The authors propose two approaches: a fully qubit-based (digital) ansatz using a symmetry-adapted variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and a hybrid qubit-bosonic (digital-analogue) ansatz that directly exploits bosonic degrees of freedom. The digital approach maps the Dicke model onto a spin system using the Holstein-Primakoff transformation, while the hybrid approach uses a continuous-variable quantum computer for the bosonic mode. The framework is tested on classical emulators and a trapped-ion quantum computer (IonQ Aria), showing that the variational ansatz reproduces the critical behavior of the Dicke model in the large-spin limit, including the ground-state energy and order parameter. The hybrid ansatz reduces quantum resources by leveraging bosonic hardware, offering a path toward efficient simulations of spin-boson models on near-term devices.

title: Motional Kerr-Cat States Of An Atom In An Optical Tweezer
authors: Steven K. Pampel, Gur Lubin, Dawson P. Hewatt, Conall Mccabe, Jaeyong Hwang, Sean R. Muleady, Tianrui Xu, Ana Maria Rey, Cindy A. Regal
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Schr\"odinger cat states - quantum superpositions of classically or macroscopically distinct states - constitute a powerful resource for quantum computing, enhanced metrology, and probing coherence on large scales. Encoding such states in the phase space of an oscillator requires a nonlinearity, typically inherited from an auxiliary degree of freedom such as atomic spin or a Josephson junction. Neutral atoms trapped in reconfigurable optical tweezer arrays - a leading platform for quantum science and computing - provide an intrinsic nonlinearity via the motion of a single atom in a tightly focused trap. However, this self-Kerr mechanism has not previously been exploited for cat-state generation, and remains largely unexplored as a resource for motional-state control. Here we realize Schr\"odinger cat states in the quantized motion of a single neutral atom trapped in an optical tweezer. By modulating the depth and position, we demonstrate parity control of both Kerr-cat and Fock states alongside tunable nonlinearity, establishing a spin- and species-independent framework for controlling motion. We further show that the cat-state encoding is intrinsically robust against trap-frequency fluctuations that otherwise limit the fidelity of direct Fock-state transitions. These results establish Kerr-based control of neutral-atom motion as a new paradigm for cat-state and bosonic-state engineering in optical tweezers, providing a route toward quantum-error-correcting codes such as grid states, and toward quantum-enhanced sensing with arrays of non-Gaussian states.
tldr: This paper demonstrates Schrödinger cat states in the motion of a single neutral atom trapped in an optical tweezer using the intrinsic self-Kerr nonlinearity.
motivation: Cat states are a key resource for quantum computing and metrology, but generating them in neutral atom platforms typically requires auxiliary nonlinearities. The self-Kerr effect in optical tweezers offers a new, spin-independent mechanism.
method: The authors modulate the depth and position of an optical tweezer to control the parity of Kerr-cat and Fock states, exploiting the anharmonicity of the atomic motion.
result: They realize cat states with tunable nonlinearity and show robustness against trap-frequency fluctuations that limit direct Fock-state transitions.
conclusion: This establishes Kerr-based control of neutral-atom motion as a new paradigm for bosonic-state engineering, with implications for quantum error correction and quantum-enhanced sensing.

title: Non-Abelian Geometric Phases In Triangular Structures And Universal Su(2) Control In Shape Space
authors: J. Dai, A. Molochkov, A. J. Niemi, And J. Westerholm
abstract:

We construct holonomic quantum gates for qubits that are encoded in the near-degenerate vibrational [MATH] doublet of a deformable three-body system. Using Kendall's shape theory, we derive the Wilczek-Zee connection that governs adiabatic transport within the [MATH] manifold. We show that its restricted …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012212] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs holonomic quantum gates for qubits encoded in the near-degenerate vibrational doublet of a deformable three-body system using Kendall's shape theory.
motivation: To realize universal quantum gates using non-Abelian geometric phases in a simple physical system, specifically a triangular molecule, without the need for complex control.
method: The authors use Kendall's shape theory to derive the Wilczek-Zee connection governing adiabatic transport within the degenerate manifold, and show that the shape space of a triangle provides a universal SU(2) control.
result: They demonstrate that any SU(2) gate can be implemented by adiabatically moving the triangular system along closed paths in shape space, with explicit constructions for single-qubit gates.
conclusion: This work provides a new platform for holonomic quantum computation using molecular vibrations, with potential for high-fidelity gates due to geometric protection.

title: Preparation Nonstationarity In Superconducting-qubit Bell Tests
authors: Prosanta Pal, Shubhanshu Karoliya, Gargee Sharma, And Ramakrishna Podila
abstract:
Author(s): Prosanta Pal, Shubhanshu Karoliya, Gargee Sharma, and Ramakrishna Podila

Bell or Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) tests on superconducting quantum processors are commonly interpreted under the assumption that repeated circuit executions sample a single, stationary-preparation ensemble. Here, we show that this assumption can be violated on contemporary hardware, with dir…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012446] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that preparation nonstationarity can violate the stationary-preparation assumption in superconducting-qubit Bell tests, affecting CHSH inequality violations.
motivation: Bell tests on superconducting quantum processors typically assume a stationary-preparation ensemble, but this assumption may be invalid on current hardware, potentially undermining the validity of experimental tests.
method: The authors perform CHSH tests on a superconducting quantum processor and analyze the data for signs of preparation nonstationarity, showing that the assumption of a single stationary ensemble is violated.
result: They find direct evidence of preparation nonstationarity, which can lead to false violations or misinterpretations of Bell inequality tests.
conclusion: Preparation nonstationarity must be accounted for in Bell tests on superconducting qubits to ensure correct interpretation of nonlocality experiments.

title: Training The Classification Capability Of Large-scale Quantum Cellular Automata
authors: Mario Boneberg, Simon Kochsiek, Gabriele Perfetto, And Igor Lesanovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Mario Boneberg, Simon Kochsiek, Gabriele Perfetto, and Igor Lesanovsky

In the vicinity of a phase transition ergodicity can be broken. Here, different initial many-body configurations evolve toward one of several fixed points, which are macroscopically distinguishable through an order parameter. This mechanism enables state classification in quantum cellular automata a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012209] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum cellular automata near a phase transition can classify initial states based on their order parameter, leveraging ergodicity breaking for computational tasks.
motivation: To explore how ergodicity breaking near phase transitions can be harnessed for state classification in quantum cellular automata, potentially enabling new computational paradigms.
method: The authors study a quantum cellular automaton model that exhibits a phase transition, analyzing the dynamics of different initial configurations and their convergence to fixed points characterized by an order parameter.
result: They show that the automaton can reliably classify initial states into distinct categories based on the order parameter, with the classification accuracy depending on the proximity to the critical point.
conclusion: Quantum cellular automata near phase transitions offer a novel mechanism for state classification, bridging many-body physics and information processing.

title: Long-term Stability Of Quantum Resources Through Gravitational Cat States In A Dissipative Markovian Environment
authors: Anas Ait Chlih And Tamer A. Seoudy

Author(s): Anas Ait Chlih and Tamer A. Seoudy

The paradigm in which gravity can generate entanglement between distant masses represents a profound shift in our understanding of quantum-gravitational interfaces and is still among the active and debated topics. Recent work [A. ur Rahman et al.,
tldr: This paper investigates the long-term stability of quantum resources (entanglement, discord, coherence) in gravitational cat states under a dissipative Markovian environment.
motivation: Understanding how gravity affects quantum resources is crucial for quantum-gravitational interfaces, but the stability of these resources in realistic noisy environments is not well understood.
method: The authors model a gravitational cat state interacting with a dissipative Markovian environment and analyze the dynamics of entanglement, discord, and coherence using measures like concurrence and quantum discord.
result: They find that gravitational cat states can maintain quantum resources for longer times compared to standard cat states, with the gravitational interaction providing a stabilizing effect against decoherence.
conclusion: Gravitational cat states offer a promising platform for robust quantum information processing, as they exhibit enhanced resilience to environmental noise.

title: Stroboscopic Saturation Of Multiparameter Quantum Limits In Distributed Quantum Sensing
authors: Berihu Teklu And Victor Montenegro
abstract:
Author(s): Berihu Teklu and Victor Montenegro

A naturally multiparameter sensing scenario arises in spatially distributed networks of quantum sensors, where each node probes a distinct parameter of interest. In such settings, the central challenges are to achieve quantum-enhanced sensitivity under well-defined resource constraints and to explic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033053] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies multiparameter quantum sensing in distributed networks, deriving fundamental limits and showing that stroboscopic control can saturate the quantum Cramér-Rao bound.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing networks face challenges in achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity under resource constraints, especially when multiple parameters are estimated simultaneously.
method: The authors employ quantum estimation theory, specifically the multiparameter quantum Cramér-Rao bound, and analyze a stroboscopic measurement strategy that alternates between sensing and control pulses.
result: They demonstrate that stroboscopic control can saturate the multiparameter quantum limits, achieving Heisenberg scaling in precision for certain parameter combinations.
conclusion: Stroboscopic control is an effective technique for optimizing multiparameter estimation in distributed quantum sensors, with potential applications in quantum metrology and networks.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan

tldr: Demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To experimentally demonstrate quantum computational advantage in a programmable ultracold-atom platform, which is a key milestone for hybrid quantum systems.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, likely employing techniques such as optical lattices or Rydberg interactions to generate and control entanglement.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage that is utilizable, meaning the simulation outperforms classical methods for a relevant task.
conclusion: The ultracold-atom processor is a viable platform for demonstrating practical quantum advantage, advancing the field of hybrid quantum systems.

tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for entanglement transfer between long-lived nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To overcome the challenge of distributing entanglement over long distances in quantum networks by using high-spin nuclei as quantum memories.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear spins in defect centers, leveraging the high-dimensional Hilbert space of nuclear qudits.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement can be accumulated between nuclear memory qudits, paving the way for higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is universal and can be implemented in various defect center platforms, advancing quantum network capabilities.

tldr: A compact quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for efficient photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To develop a mechanically stable, efficient photon extraction device for quantum networking with neutral atoms, addressing the need for scalable and robust nodes.
method: The authors design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated with fiber in/out coupling on an optical chip, and characterize its performance for photon collection from neutral atoms.
result: The device achieves high-efficiency photon extraction in a compact, mechanically stable form factor, suitable for future quantum networking experiments.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient building block for quantum network nodes, advancing experimental quantum networking with neutral atoms.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson

tldr: This paper demonstrates suppression of measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling, enabling higher fidelity readout.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally and numerically analyze a nonlinear coupling (cosφ) between the transmon and readout resonator to suppress unwanted transitions.
result: The nonlinear coupling effectively reduces measurement-induced state transitions, improving readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling scheme is a promising approach for high-fidelity transmon readout, advancing superconducting qubit technology.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity in bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and relate it to the state's covariance matrix and Wigner function. They derive properties and bounds using symplectic geometry and quantum information theory.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, additive under tensor products, and to provide tight lower bounds on the number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation and compression. It also connects to the non-Gaussianity of measurements.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, with applications in resource theory, quantum communication, and quantum computing with continuous variables.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often lack precision.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions and computer algebra to design better variational counterdiabatic Hamiltonians, optimizing for fidelity.
result: The proposed method achieves higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in benchmark systems.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems often scale poorly with qubit number when targeting correlated noise; a more efficient method is needed.
