tldr: This paper proposes a Floquet-engineering approach to realize the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model in ultracold atoms in an optical lattice, linking to black holes and high-temperature superconductors.
motivation: The Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model is a prominent model of quantum matter with connections to black holes and high-temperature superconductors, but its experimental realization is challenging. The authors aim to emulate it using ultracold atoms in an optical lattice via Floquet engineering.
method: The authors design a Floquet-engineering scheme to generate the necessary interactions in a Hubbard model with ultracold atoms, using periodic driving to simulate the SYK model's random all-to-all interactions.
result: They show that the Floquet-engineered system reproduces key features of the SYK model, such as maximal chaos and a non-Fermi liquid state, as evidenced by out-of-time-order correlators and spectral functions.
conclusion: This work provides a feasible experimental platform to study SYK physics, offering insights into quantum chaos and holography, but it is not directly aligned with the user's core interests in quantum information or thermodynamics.

conclusion: The proposed method provides a useful tool for characterizing phases in dipolar BECs.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong electronic correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel quantum phases and functionalities.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory, time-resolved spectroscopy, and pump-probe techniques.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable states, and nonthermal orders such as superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation in Mott insulators provides a rich playground for exploring nonequilibrium physics and designing new material properties.

title: Machine Learning Decoding Of Circuit-Level Noise For Bivariate Bicycle Codes
authors: John Blue, Harshil Avlani, Zhiyang He, Liu Ziyin, And Isaac L. Chuang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2149 (2026).

Fault-tolerant quantum computers will depend crucially on the performance of the classical decoding algorithm which takes in the results of measurements and outputs corrections to the errors inferred to have occurred. Machine learning models have shown great promise as decoders for the surface code; however, this promise has not yet been substantiated for the more challenging task of decoding quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes. In this paper, we present a recurrent, transformer-based neural network designed to decode circuit-level noise on Bivariate Bicycle (BB) codes. For the [MATH] BB code, at a physical error rate of [MATH], our model achieves logical error rates almost [MATH] times lower than belief propagation with ordered statistics decoding (BP-OSD), and roughly [MATH] times larger than a most-likely error decoder. Moreover, while BP-OSD has a wide distribution of runtimes with significant outliers, our model has a consistent runtime and is an order-of-magnitude faster than the worst-case times from a benchmark BP-OSD implementation. On the [MATH] BB code, our model obtains worse logical error rates but maintains the speed advantage. These results provide initial evidence that machine learning decoders can out-perform conventional decoders on small QLDPC codes, but suggest more complex architectures and/or training procedures are necessary to scale to larger code sizes.

.
tldr: This paper applies machine learning decoding to bivariate bicycle codes, a type of quantum LDPC code, achieving lower logical error rates and faster runtime than BP-OSD on small codes.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires efficient decoders for quantum error-correcting codes; machine learning decoders have shown promise for surface codes but not yet for QLDPC codes.
method: A recurrent, transformer-based neural network is trained to decode circuit-level noise on bivariate bicycle codes, using syndrome measurement data to predict error corrections.
result: On the [[144,12,12]] BB code, the ML decoder achieves logical error rates nearly 10 times lower than BP-OSD and is an order of magnitude faster, though performance degrades on larger codes.
conclusion: Machine learning decoders can outperform conventional decoders on small QLDPC codes, but scaling to larger codes requires more complex architectures or training procedures.

title: High-gain Effects In Broadband Continuous-wave Parametric Down Conversion Sources And Measurements With Undetected Photons
authors: Martin Houde, Franz Roeder, Christine Silberhorn, Benjamin Brecht And Nicolás Quesada
abstract: We study theoretically how high-gain effects affect the measurement outcome of visible signal spectra in undetected photon measurement schemes. We consider two interferometric configurations: firstly, the SU(1,1) interferometer where the idler incurs loss and additional dispersion in between two identical, lossless, squeezers; secondly, the induced coherence interferometer where the idler incurs loss and additional dispersion in between two identical, lossless, squeezers and where the second squeezer is seeded by the idler and a vacuum ancilla mode. Furthermore, we consider a distributed loss configuration where the idler incurs loss as it propagates in the nonlinear medium. Motivated by experimental evidence and due to the fact that broadband sources are ideal for these measurement schemes, we use the dispersive data of a third-order dispersion engineered integrated waveguide parametric down conversion (PDC) source presented in Roeder et al (2024 New J. Phys. 26 123025) to model the PDC spectra in the three configurations. For each configuration we consider the case of idler-only (i) absorption, (ii) additional dispersion, and (iii) the combined effects. We obtain results which outline the strength and weaknesses of the different configurations at different operation points.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies high-gain effects in broadband continuous-wave parametric down conversion sources for undetected photon measurements, focusing on SU(1,1) and induced coherence interferometers.
motivation: To understand how high-gain effects impact measurement outcomes in undetected photon schemes, which are relevant for quantum imaging and sensing.
method: The authors model parametric down conversion spectra using dispersive data from an integrated waveguide source, considering loss and dispersion in two interferometric configurations.
result: They outline strengths and weaknesses of different configurations at various operation points, showing how high-gain alters spectra.
conclusion: High-gain effects must be accounted for in broadband continuous-wave sources for accurate undetected photon measurements.

title: Transient Localization From Fractionalization: Vanishingly Small Energy Transport In Gapless Quantum Magnets
authors: Shi Feng, Penghao Zhu, Johannes Knolle, And Michael Knap
abstract:
Author(s): Shi Feng, Penghao Zhu, Johannes Knolle, and Michael Knap

Disorder-free localization is usually associated with dynamics far from equilibrium. Here, the authors uncover a new mechanism in the low-energy sector of clean, gapless quantum magnets: transient localization from mass-imbalanced fractionalization. Studying the dynamical response in the gapless phase of a translation-invariant Kitaev ladder model, they show that fractionalization creates a coherent superposition of quasistatic flux-disorder configurations in the ground state, preserving translation symmetry while strongly suppressing correlation spreading and energy transport.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034423] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers a new mechanism of transient localization from fractionalization in clean, gapless quantum magnets, leading to vanishingly small energy transport.
motivation: Understanding energy transport in low-dimensional quantum magnets is important for fundamental physics and potential applications, but disorder-free localization typically requires far-from-equilibrium dynamics.
method: The authors study a translation-invariant Kitaev ladder model in its gapless phase, analyzing the dynamical response and showing that fractionalization creates a coherent superposition of quasistatic flux-disorder configurations.
result: They find that despite preserving translation symmetry, the fractionalization strongly suppresses correlation spreading and energy transport, leading to transient localization.
conclusion: This work reveals a new mechanism for localization in clean systems, which may have implications for understanding thermalization and transport in quantum materials.

title: Adlam's Frame: Comment On "Wigner's Frame"
authors: Anne-Catherine de la Hamette Andrea Di Biagio
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent no-go theorems based on extended Wigner's Friend scenarios (EWFS) reveal a deep tension between the universal validity of quantum theory and local friendliness (LF), the conjunction of three natural assumptions: the absoluteness of observed events, locality, and no-superdeterminism. In a recent work, Adlam argues that this tension can be dissolved by appealing to quantum reference frames (QRFs). We present and critically assess her proposal. We show that her proposed resolution does not arise from QRFs, but instead relies on three independent modifications: certain degrees of freedom are always definite, observers can flip upon measuring spins, and the outcomes the superobservers record and use to test the inequalities are not their friends' observed results. The proposal and the arguments for the plausibility of these modifications rest on several misconceptions about QRFs and EWFS, which we rectify. We conclude that, within standard quantum theory, quantum reference frames do not evade the EWFS no-go theorems.
tldr: This paper critically assesses Adlam's proposal to resolve extended Wigner's Friend no-go theorems using quantum reference frames, arguing that the proposal relies on misconceptions and does not evade the theorems.
motivation: Recent no-go theorems in extended Wigner's Friend scenarios challenge the universal validity of quantum theory. Adlam proposed a resolution using quantum reference frames, which this paper evaluates and finds flawed.
method: The authors analyze Adlam's argument, identifying three independent modifications she introduces and showing they are not inherent to quantum reference frames. They clarify misconceptions about QRFs and EWFS.
result: Adlam's proposed resolution does not arise from QRFs but from additional assumptions; the paper concludes that QRFs do not evade the EWFS no-go theorems within standard quantum theory.
conclusion: Quantum reference frames do not resolve the tension highlighted by extended Wigner's Friend no-go theorems; the proposed resolution is based on misunderstandings.

We propose a microscopic, weak-coupling mechanism by which generic Chern bands asymptotically relax toward ideal bands. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046601] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.

motivation: Ideal Chern bands are important for fractional Chern insulators, but realistic systems often deviate from ideal conditions; the authors aim to show that coupling to a bath can drive relaxation toward ideal bands.
method: They consider interacting electrons in a Chern band coupled to an Ohmic bosonic bath, derive a master equation using the Born-Markov approximation, and analyze the steady state.
result: Under weak coupling and leading order, the system relaxes to a state that approximates an ideal Chern band, with corrections that can be controlled.
conclusion: The proposed mechanism provides a practical route to realize ideal Chern bands in experiments, potentially enabling fractional Chern insulator physics.

motivation: To find exact solutions for spin-1 chains with Kitaev-like couplings, inspired by the AKLT model.

abstract:

It is found that increasing the persistence of the active particle motion increases the total insertion volume and its surface area: the averaged space available to place another particle without overlaps. tldr: This paper studies the statistical geometry of active repulsive rods and disks, finding that activity increases insertion volume and connectivity.
motivation: To understand how active motion affects the geometry of available space in repulsive particle systems, which is relevant to active matter physics.
method: Combines theoretical analysis with simulations of active repulsive rods and disks, measuring insertion volume and surface area as functions of persistence.
result: Increasing persistence of active motion increases the total insertion volume and its surface area, making the insertion space more connected.
conclusion: Activity significantly alters the statistical geometry of repulsive active matter, with implications for packing and transport in such systems.

tldr: A quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis is proposed, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a classical machine learning technique; quantum speedups could enable analysis of larger datasets.
method: The paper designs a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and sampling to compute persistent homology.
result: The algorithm achieves provable exponential speedup over classical methods for certain input classes.
conclusion: While theoretically interesting, the result is not directly aligned with the researcher's core interests in quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant that is hard to compute classically, making it a candidate for quantum advantage. The authors aim to provide an end-to-end quantum algorithm that can be implemented on near-term devices.
method: The paper describes a complete pipeline including state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, using a Hadamard test and controlled unitary operations based on a braid representation of the knot.
result: The algorithm is implemented on a trapped-ion quantum processor, and the results show good agreement with exact values for small knots, demonstrating the feasibility of the approach.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical benchmark for quantum computers and suggests that the Jones polynomial approximation may be a viable candidate for early quantum advantage.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified approach.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding quantum dynamics, with connections to quantum computation.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity is crucial for explaining perception, thought, and action.
method: The authors review recent progress in connecting maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to experimental recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible behaviors and demonstrate that abstract theoretical principles can have predictive power in neuroscience.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a quantitative bridge between neural data and theoretical models, advancing our understanding of brain function.

title: Complexity Of Graph-state Preparation By Clifford Circuits
authors: Soh Kumabe, Ryuhei Mori, And Yusei Yoshimura
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2165 (2026).

In this work, we study the complexity of graph-state preparation in a general model of quantum algorithms that allows measurements in the computational basis, single-qubit Clifford operations, and two-qubit Clifford operations. We define the CZ-complexity of a graph state [MATH] as the minimum number of two-qubit Clifford operations required to generate [MATH] from [MATH] for some [MATH]. Equivalently, every optimal algorithm can be taken to use only controlled-Z (CZ) gates as its two-qubit Clifford operations. We then give a combinatorial characterization of graph-state transformations. Specifically, [MATH] can be generated from another graph state [MATH] by an algorithm of CZ-complexity at most [MATH] if and only if [MATH] can be obtained from [MATH] by vertex deletions, local complementations and at most [MATH] elementary edge-complementations. Here, an elementary edge-complementation toggles either a single edge, all edges between one vertex and the neighborhood of another, or all edges between the neighborhoods of two non-adjacent vertices. Using this characterization, we relate CZ-complexity to rank-width. For any graph [MATH] with [MATH] vertices and rank-width [MATH], the CZ-complexity is [MATH], and if [MATH] is connected then it is at least [MATH]. We also show that these bounds are close to optimal. Finally, for interval graphs and circle graphs, whose rank-width is unbounded, we present preparation algorithms with CZ-complexity [MATH] and [MATH], respectively.

.
tldr: This paper studies the minimum number of two-qubit Clifford operations (CZ-complexity) needed to prepare graph states, providing a combinatorial characterization and bounds based on rank-width.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of graph-state preparation is important for quantum computing and communication, as graph states are a key resource for measurement-based quantum computing and quantum error correction.
method: The authors define CZ-complexity and prove a combinatorial characterization of graph-state transformations using vertex deletions, local complementations, and elementary edge-complementations. They then relate CZ-complexity to rank-width and provide algorithms for interval and circle graphs.
result: For any graph with n vertices and rank-width r, the CZ-complexity is O(r n), and at least Ω(r) for connected graphs. Interval and circle graphs have O(n) and O(n log n) CZ-complexity, respectively.
conclusion: The paper establishes a connection between graph-state preparation complexity and graph-theoretic parameters like rank-width, offering efficient algorithms for certain graph classes.

title: Exact Quantum Many-Body Scars In 2d Quantum Gauge Models
authors: Yuan Miao, Linhao Li, Hosho Katsura, And Masahito Yamazaki
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2164 (2026).

Quantum many-body scars (QMBS) serve as important examples of ergodicity-breaking phenomena in quantum many-body systems. Despite recent extensive studies, exact QMBS are rare in dimensions higher than one. In this paper, we study a two-dimensional quantum [MATH] gauge model that is dual to a two-dimensional spin-[MATH] XY model defined on bipartite graphs. We identify the exact eigenstates of the XY model with a tower structure as exact QMBS. Exploiting the duality transformation, we show that the exact QMBS of the XY model (and XXZ model) after the transformation are the exact QMBS of the dual [MATH] gauge model. This construction is versatile and has potential applications for finding new QMBS in other higher-dimensional models.

.
tldr: This paper constructs exact quantum many-body scars in a 2D quantum gauge model via duality to an XY model.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars are rare in higher dimensions; the authors aim to provide exact examples in 2D.
method: They study a 2D quantum Z2 gauge model dual to a spin-1/2 XY model on bipartite graphs, identifying exact eigenstates with a tower structure as QMBS.
result: Exact QMBS are found in the XY model and, via duality, in the gauge model, demonstrating a versatile construction.
conclusion: This construction may be generalized to find new QMBS in other higher-dimensional models.

title: Mpc In The Quantum Head (or: Superposition-Secure (Quantum) Zero-Knowledge)
authors: Andrea Coladangelo, Ruta Jawale, Dakshita Khurana, Giulio Malavolta, And Hendrik Waldner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2161 (2026).

The MPC-in-the-head technique (Ishai et al., STOC 2007) is a celebrated method to build zero-knowledge protocols with desirable theoretical properties and high practical efficiency. This technique has generated a large body of research and has influenced the design of real-world post-quantum cryptographic signatures. In this work, we present a generalization of the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting, where the MPC is running a quantum computation. As an application of our framework, we propose a new approach to build zero-knowledge protocols where security holds even against a verifier that can obtain a superposition of transcripts. This notion was pioneered by Damgard et al., who built a zero-knowledge protocol for NP (in the common reference string model) secure against superposition attacks, by relying on perfectly hiding and unconditionally binding dual-mode commitments. Unfortunately, no such commitments are known from standard cryptographic assumptions. In this work we revisit this problem, and present two new three-round protocols in the common reference string model: (i) A zero-knowledge argument for NP, whose security reduces to the standard learning with errors (LWE) problem. (ii) A zero-knowledge argument for QMA from the same assumption.

.
tldr: This paper generalizes the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting to build zero-knowledge protocols secure against superposition attacks, with applications to NP and QMA.
motivation: Existing zero-knowledge protocols are not secure against quantum verifiers who can obtain superposition of transcripts, and previous constructions relied on commitments not known from standard assumptions.
method: The authors develop a quantum generalization of the MPC-in-the-head technique, where the MPC runs a quantum computation, and use it to construct three-round zero-knowledge arguments in the common reference string model.
result: They obtain a zero-knowledge argument for NP and one for QMA, both secure against superposition attacks, with security based on the standard learning with errors (LWE) assumption.
conclusion: This work provides the first zero-knowledge protocols for NP and QMA secure against superposition attacks from standard cryptographic assumptions, advancing quantum cryptography.

title: Near-Optimal Parameter Tuning Of Level-1 Qaoa For Ising Models
authors: V Vijendran, Dax Enshan Koh, Eunok Bae, Hyukjoon Kwon, Ping Koy Lam, And Syed M Assad
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2158 (2026).

The Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA) tackles combinatorial optimisation problems by encoding their solutions into the ground state of an Ising Hamiltonian prepared by a [MATH]-level parameterised circuit, with the angles tuned classically. Parameter optimisation is widely regarded as a central bottleneck, even for the shallowest circuits. Focusing on QAOA at [MATH] (QAOA[MATH]), we show that tuning the two angles [MATH] for weighted Ising models is not a black-box search but a structured signal-processing problem. We prove that the QAOA[MATH] expectation value is a partial Fourier series in [MATH] whose frequencies are determined explicitly by the problem's couplings and fields, giving instance-wise bandwidth bounds and, via the Nyquist–Shannon theorem, the sampling resolution needed to avoid the aliasing that causes coarse-grid searches to return spurious optima. We then eliminate the mixer angle analytically, computing [MATH] in closed form to reduce the search to one dimension, and apply a subdivision algorithm that locates the globally optimal [MATH] in polynomial time with a certificate of optimality when the weights are commensurable and bounded. For regular weighted graphs, we further prove the conventional wisdom that the globally optimal [MATH] concentrates near zero and coincides with the first local optimum, giving a rigorous account of the empirical success of small-angle initialisation and allowing gradient descent to replace exhaustive line searches. Validated within Recursive QAOA (RQAOA) on weighted instances of 128 and 256 qubits, our method consistently outperforms both coarsely optimised RQAOA and semidefinite programming.

.
tldr: This paper presents a near-optimal parameter tuning method for level-1 QAOA on Ising models, reducing the optimization to a structured signal-processing problem.
motivation: Parameter optimization is a central bottleneck in QAOA, even for shallow circuits; the authors aim to show that tuning is not a black-box search but a structured problem.
method: They prove the QAOA1 expectation is a partial Fourier series, derive instance-wise bandwidth bounds, eliminate the mixer angle analytically, and apply a subdivision algorithm for global optimization.
result: The method achieves polynomial-time global optimality certification for commensurable weights and shows that for regular graphs the optimal angle concentrates near zero, validating small-angle initialization.
conclusion: The proposed tuning method consistently outperforms coarse optimization and semidefinite programming in Recursive QAOA on weighted instances up to 256 qubits.

title: Cavity-induced Multispin Interactions And Phase Transitions In Ultracold Fermi Gases
authors: Shi-Liang Zhu And Z D Wang Zhen Zheng
abstract: The many-body physics of higher-spin systems is expected to host qualitatively new matter phases, but realizing them requires the controllable interactions between multispin components that can be tuned independently for each component. Here we propose a scheme that meets this demand in ultracold Fermi gases. By engineering the atom-cavity coupling, we generate cavity-induced effective interactions between pseudo-spin states via multiple Raman and cavity paths. Focusing on the simplest spin-1 case, we obtain two independent scattering channels whose relative strengths and signs are determined by the Clebsch–Gordan coefficients and optical-field parameters. The resulting Hamiltonian combines the on-site Cooper pairing with the off-site repulsion, and drives a continuous transition from the superfluid to the spin-density-wave phase. The coexistence region is reminiscent of a supersolid, yet the self-organized modulation appears in the spin density profile of a higher-spin representation, rather than in the number density profile. The proposal can be implemented with the existing techniques in ultracold atoms. Therefore it offers a versatile platform for quantum simulation of higher-spin many-body physics.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to generate cavity-induced multispin interactions in ultracold Fermi gases, leading to a superfluid to spin-density-wave phase transition.
motivation: Higher-spin systems can host novel quantum phases, but controllable multispin interactions are challenging to realize.
method: By engineering atom-cavity coupling via multiple Raman and cavity paths, effective interactions between pseudo-spin states are generated, with independent control over scattering channels.
result: For spin-1 fermions, the Hamiltonian combines on-site Cooper pairing and off-site repulsion, driving a continuous transition from superfluid to spin-density-wave phase, with a coexistence region reminiscent of supersolid.
conclusion: The scheme is experimentally feasible with existing ultracold atom techniques and provides a platform for quantum simulation of higher-spin many-body physics.

title: Boundary Free Energies In Disordered Ising Models
authors: Hexiang Wang, Keheng Zhu, Mauris Chueng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The boundary correction to the free energy of a disordered Ising model depends on the boundary condition, the normalization, and the finite-volume sequence. We give a one-dimensional i.i.d. counterexample showing that the surface free-energy density need not be independent of the van Hove sequence and that the corresponding random correction need not converge in probability. For bounded couplings in the Dobrushin uniqueness regime on cubic boxes in dimensions [MATH], we prove convergence of the normalized free-to-fixed boundary free-energy difference in expectation, almost surely, and in every [MATH], [MATH]. For Gaussian boundary couplings, we derive an exact finite-volume interpolation identity and explain why it does not by itself imply a low-temperature surface limit. For a seam-flip free-energy difference [MATH] across a set [MATH] of independent symmetric bonds of variance [MATH], we prove [MATH]; one-dimensional examples show that symmetry and finite moments alone do not determine a stiffness exponent, and the low-temperature Gaussian Edwards--Anderson problem remains open.
tldr: This paper studies boundary free energies in disordered Ising models, focusing on convergence properties and counterexamples.
motivation: Understanding boundary corrections to free energy in disordered systems is important for statistical mechanics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors provide a one-dimensional i.i.d. counterexample and prove convergence results for bounded couplings in the Dobrushin uniqueness regime using finite-volume interpolation.
result: They show that surface free-energy density may depend on the van Hove sequence and that the random correction may not converge in probability; for Gaussian couplings, they derive an exact identity.
conclusion: The results clarify limitations of boundary free energy limits but do not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A First Bound On The Moffat Energy And Thorium--229 Clock As A Probe Of The Nonlocal Time-Energy Structure
authors: J. W. Moffat Arvin Kouroshnia
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The new Thorium--229 nuclear clocks give us a new laboratory system in which to test if modification of the Time-Energy uncertainty principle is correct. In this paper we derive the nonlocal Time-Energy uncertainty principle and then apply the published [MATH]Th nuclear clock data as a first probe of the nonlocality scale \(E_M\). We note that since these experiments were not designed to test nonlocal quantum field theory the constraints are interpreted as motivating bounds and not definitive exclusions. By using the direct clock-energy channel, we find conservative lower bounds on \(E_M\) at the tens of MeV scale, with optimistic present-data estimates reaching the hundred MeV scale. Including the known nuclear sensitivity enhancement of the [MATH]Th transition gives us stronger model dependent bounds in the GeV range, while nuclear-scale reference-energy scenarios can reach the TeV range. The conclusion we draw from this is that nuclear clocks already provide an experimental route from nonlocal time--energy uncertainty to measurable laboratory bounds on non-Planckian nonlocality.
tldr: This paper derives a nonlocal time-energy uncertainty principle and uses Thorium-229 nuclear clock data to place bounds on the Moffat energy scale, testing nonlocal quantum field theory.
motivation: To test modifications to the time-energy uncertainty principle using a new laboratory system (Thorium-229 nuclear clock) and constrain the nonlocality scale.
method: Derives a nonlocal time-energy uncertainty relation and applies published Thorium-229 nuclear clock data to extract lower bounds on the Moffat energy scale, considering nuclear sensitivity enhancement.
result: Conservative lower bounds on the Moffat energy scale are at tens of MeV, with optimistic estimates reaching hundreds of MeV; model-dependent bounds can reach GeV to TeV range.
conclusion: Nuclear clocks provide an experimental route to bound non-Planckian nonlocality, but current constraints are preliminary and not definitive.

title: Phase-Selective Amplitude Amplification For Constrained Optimization
authors: Massimiliano Cutugno
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work introduces a variant of Grover amplitude amplification using stabilizer and blade qubits to improve boosting robustness across objective distributions. We give geometric intuition, example simulations, and discuss limitations. Formal performance bounds and larger-scale validation are left for future research.
tldr: This paper introduces a variant of Grover's amplitude amplification using stabilizer and blade qubits for constrained optimization, but lacks formal performance bounds and large-scale validation.
motivation: The authors aim to improve the robustness of amplitude amplification across different objective distributions, addressing limitations of standard Grover's algorithm.
method: They propose a phase-selective amplitude amplification technique that incorporates stabilizer and blade qubits, and provide geometric intuition and example simulations.
result: The work presents preliminary simulations showing potential benefits, but no formal performance bounds or large-scale validation are provided.
conclusion: The approach is a conceptual contribution with limited immediate applicability; further research is needed to establish its effectiveness.

title: Control Of Eigenmode Localization And Coupling Anisotropy By Multiscan Femtosecond Laser Writing
authors: S. A. Zhuravitskii (quantum Technology Centre, Faculty Of Physics, M.V. Lomonosov Moscow State University, Moscow, Russia), N. S. Kostyuchenko (quantum Technology Centre, Faculty Of Physics, M.V. Lomonosov Moscow State University, Moscow, Russia), N. N. Skryabin (quantum Technology Centre, Faculty Of Physics, M.V. Lomonosov Moscow State University, Moscow, Russia, Russian Quantum Center, Moscow, Russia), I. V. Dyakonov (quantum Technology Centre, Faculty Of Physics, M.V. Lomonosov Moscow State University, Moscow, Russia, Russian Quantum Center, Moscow, Russia), A. A. Korneev (quantum Technology Centre, Faculty Of Physics, M.V. Lomonosov Moscow State University, Moscow, Russia), A. A. Kalinkin (quantum Technology Centre, Faculty Of Physics, M.V. Lomonosov Moscow State University, Moscow, Russia), S. S. Straupe (quantum Technology Centre, Faculty Of Physics, M.V. Lomonosov Moscow State University, Moscow, Russia, Russian Quantum Center, Moscow, Russia), S. P. Kulik
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The multiscan method is widely used in femtosecond laser writing of waveguide systems to increase the refractive index contrast and to control the eigenmode shape. Here, we investigate multiscan writing with a constant effective writing speed and show that the displacement between adjacent scans provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling eigenmode confinement. By optimizing the multiscan parameters, the effective mode area can be reduced, enabling an up to eightfold increase in fabrication speed compared to conventional single-scan writing. We further demonstrate that careful tuning of the multiscan geometry substantially reduces the anisotropy of inter-waveguide coupling. These findings are applied to the fabrication of three-dimensional waveguide arrays operating at wavelengths of 808 nm and 1450 nm, where reduced coupling anisotropy is achieved. The proposed approach may be useful for three-dimensional waveguide arrays employed in topological photonics experiments, where low coupling anisotropy is desired.
tldr: This paper presents a method to control eigenmode localization and reduce coupling anisotropy in waveguide arrays fabricated by multiscan femtosecond laser writing.
motivation: To improve fabrication speed and control over waveguide properties for applications in topological photonics.
method: The authors investigate multiscan writing with constant effective speed and vary the displacement between adjacent scans to optimize mode confinement and coupling anisotropy.
result: They achieve up to eightfold increase in fabrication speed and reduced coupling anisotropy in 3D waveguide arrays at 808 nm and 1450 nm.
conclusion: The proposed multiscan approach is useful for fabricating waveguide arrays with low coupling anisotropy, beneficial for topological photonics experiments.

title: Equivariant Continuous Normalizing Flows With Offline Sampling For Fermionic Ground State Estimation
authors: Sam Cochran, James B. Larsen, Andrew Wray, Michael J. Keiser, Chad Rigetti, Shravan Veerapaneni
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a framework for fermionic variational Monte Carlo (VMC) in which a continuous normalizing flow (CNF) refines a fixed antisymmetric base wavefunction. The flow is implemented as a permutation-equivariant neural ODE, a smooth, topology-preserving map that learns correlations not captured by the base; equivariance preserves the antisymmetry of the base, so the flow can in principle improve any antisymmetric ansatz that can be sampled efficiently. We demonstrate this using Slater and Jastrow-Slater bases, though more expressive choices are admissible. Exact samples from the flow's Born distribution are obtained by pushing pre-cached base samples through the forward ODE, requiring no Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) at training time. The base samples are generated offline and reused across training batches and runs, decoupling sample generation from parameter optimization and enabling embarrassingly parallel training across multiple GPUs. We introduce three novel permutation-equivariant vector field architectures: Pairwise Deep Sets (PDS), FermiNet Vector Fields (FVF), and Pairwise Deep Sets Gradient (PDSG), each offering a different balance of expressivity and computational cost. We further introduce an augmented dynamics formulation for kinetic energy computation that co-evolves the required derivative quantities as ODE state variables, eliminating differentiation through the ODE trajectory and yielding significant reductions in wall-clock time and memory. Training runs on systems of harmonically trapped spinless electrons demonstrate ground-state energies below CISD reference values. Scaling experiments demonstrate near-ideal strong scaling from 1 to 128 NVIDIA A100s using 32 GPU nodes of NERSC's Perlmutter supercomputer for systems of up to [MATH] particles in three dimensions.
tldr: This paper introduces a variational Monte Carlo method using equivariant continuous normalizing flows for fermionic ground state estimation, achieving high parallel efficiency.
motivation: Accurate estimation of fermionic ground states is computationally challenging; existing methods often rely on Markov chain Monte Carlo which is slow and hard to parallelize.
method: A permutation-equivariant neural ODE (continuous normalizing flow) refines a fixed antisymmetric base wavefunction; base samples are generated offline and reused, enabling embarrassingly parallel training.
result: Ground-state energies below CISD reference values are achieved for harmonically trapped spinless electrons, with near-ideal strong scaling up to 128 GPUs.
conclusion: The framework provides a scalable, MCMC-free approach to fermionic VMC, but its focus is on computational chemistry and machine learning rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Isochoric Thermodynamic Preconditioning For Resolving Mechanically Induced Phase Change In Fractured Porous Media
authors: Veljko Lipovac, Eirik Keilegavlen, Inga Berre
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rapid pore-volume changes can trigger phase change on timescales shorter than characteristic transport times and may therefore be skipped by conventional nonlinear solves and adaptive time stepping. We present a persistent-variable framework for transport in fractured porous media, introducing specific volume as an independent variable. Starting from a fully coupled system, we derive volume-based models and recover classical pressure-based formulations by eliminating local thermodynamic variables. To resolve abrupt fracture opening, we introduce a nonlinear preconditioner that assumes instantaneous free expansion and resolves the fluid state through an isochoric equilibrium calculation before advancing the transport problem. The preconditioner applies to both volume- and pressure-based models. In the studied fracture-opening cases, unpreconditioned simulations miss transient vaporization, whereas the preconditioned models do not. Across the investigated aperture range, larger openings produce monotonic increases in gas content, expansion-induced cooling, and durations of transients. Thermal effects alter the phase evolution but have otherwise minor influence on the overall transient duration. Within the proof-of-concept setting, fracture opening generates substantial transient pressure reductions, indicating that geomechanical feedback may become important in fully coupled applications. Pressure-enthalpy and volume-temperature formulations recover identical physical solutions but exhibit different nonlinear robustness, with the pressure-enthalpy formulation proving more robust in some recompression-dominated cases. These results show that equilibrium specifications control the numerical properties of the nonlinear problem rather than recovered physical responses, while isochoric preconditioning connects the nonlinear initialization directly to the underlying thermodynamics.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical framework for modeling phase change in fractured porous media using isochoric thermodynamic preconditioning.
motivation: Rapid pore-volume changes can cause phase transitions that are missed by conventional solvers; a robust numerical method is needed to capture these transients.
method: The authors introduce specific volume as an independent variable, derive volume-based models, and develop a nonlinear preconditioner that assumes instantaneous free expansion with isochoric equilibrium calculation.
result: Preconditioned simulations capture transient vaporization that unpreconditioned ones miss; thermal effects have minor influence on transient duration.
conclusion: Isochoric preconditioning improves numerical robustness for fracture-induced phase change, but the physical solutions are identical to pressure-based formulations.

title: Spontaneous Optical Emission Of A Randomly Oriented Chiral Quantum Source
authors: Mikael P. Backlund
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive the form of the one-photon state of the electromagnetic field resulting from spontaneous optical emission of a randomly oriented chiral quantum source, including electric dipole, magnetic dipole, and electric quadrupole contributions to the radiation. We describe how spatial coherence in the emission can be exploited to reveal hidden information about the emitter. This work serves as a prelude and companion piece to our concurrently submitted work in which we present the classical and quantum error bounds associated with assigning the handedness of such an emitter.
tldr: Derives the one-photon state from a chiral quantum source, focusing on spatial coherence to infer emitter handedness.
motivation: To understand spontaneous emission from chiral sources and use spatial coherence to extract hidden information about the emitter's chirality.
method: Analytical derivation of the electromagnetic field's one-photon state including electric dipole, magnetic dipole, and electric quadrupole contributions.
result: The form of the one-photon state is obtained, showing how spatial coherence can reveal information about the emitter's handedness.
conclusion: This work provides a theoretical foundation for determining chirality via optical emission, with implications for quantum sensing.

title: Raman-Assisted Multiband Nonlinear Frequency-Conversion Network In A High-Q Ltoi Microdisk
authors: Zhifan Fang, Yuxuan He, Zhangning Pan, Xianfeng Chen, Yuping Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-chip nonlinear frequency conversion offers a key route to broadband coherent light sources, but spanning telecom, visible, and ultraviolet wavelengths within a single resonator remains challenging. Lithium tantalate-on-insulator (LTOI), which has recently emerged as a promising material platform for integrated photonics, combines strong Raman activity, a large second-order nonlinearity, broad optical transparency and high resistance to photorefractive damage, thereby attracting increasing attention for on-chip nonlinear frequency conversion. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a Raman-assisted multiband frequency-conversion network in a high-Q LTOI microdisk with a loaded quality factor of 2.48x10^6. The resonant pumping produced high-purity single-mode Raman lasing with a 3.14 mW threshold, 32.44% slope efficiency, and an excellent side-mode suppression ratio (SMSR) of 29.5 dB. Under a nearby pump condition, we also observe multiple Stokes components together with an anti-Stokes line on the short-wavelength side of the pump. The resulting multiple intracavity Stokes fields subsequently acted as frequency seeds for cascaded chi^(2) processes, producing near-infrared and visible signals and extending the emission to 312.6 nm in the ultraviolet. These findings establish the cooperative action of Raman gain and second-order nonlinearity across widely separated spectral bands within a single microcavity. The device therefore offers a route toward integrated multiband light sources and a platform for studying coupled nonlinear dynamics.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a Raman-assisted multiband nonlinear frequency conversion network in a high-Q LTOI microdisk, achieving broadband light generation from telecom to ultraviolet.
motivation: On-chip nonlinear frequency conversion is key for broadband coherent light sources, but spanning telecom, visible, and UV within a single resonator remains challenging.
method: The authors use a high-Q LTOI microdisk resonator to achieve Raman lasing and cascaded second-order nonlinear processes, generating multiple Stokes and anti-Stokes components.
result: They achieve single-mode Raman lasing with 3.14 mW threshold and 32.44% slope efficiency, and extend emission to 312.6 nm in the ultraviolet via cascaded chi^(2) processes.
conclusion: The cooperative action of Raman gain and second-order nonlinearity in a single microcavity offers a route toward integrated multiband light sources and studies of coupled nonlinear dynamics.

title: Simulating Majorana Fermions In Black Hole With Ising Models
authors: Kristian Hauser A. Villegas John Vienn A. Estremadura
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum field theory (QFT) in curved spacetime has led to profound predictions, including the Unruh effect and Hawking radiation, yet their direct observation remains extraordinarily challenging because of their extremely weak signatures. Here, we show that the transverse-field Ising model provides a quantum simulator for Majorana fermions in a Schwarzschild black hole background. Remarkably, different coordinate representations of the same spacetime-Schwarzschild, tortoise, Kruskal, and conformally flat-map onto distinct microscopic Ising spin models. Despite their microscopic differences, these models converge in the continuum limit to the same Majorana field theory, exhibiting an emergent form of general covariance. This provides a rare example of a fundamental symmetry of general relativity arising as an emergent property of a condensed matter system. We further demonstrate how black hole particle production can be simulated and detected through spin correlation measurements, and discuss experimental platforms capable of realizing these models. Our work establishes a practical route for investigating fermionic QFT in curved spacetime using controllable quantum many-body systems and tabletop experiments.
tags: quantum field theory in curved spacetime
tldr: This paper proposes simulating Majorana fermions in a black hole background using transverse-field Ising models, showing emergent general covariance and black hole particle production.
motivation: Direct observation of QFT in curved spacetime phenomena like Hawking radiation is extremely challenging; the authors aim to provide a tabletop quantum simulation route.
method: They map different coordinate representations of Schwarzschild spacetime onto distinct Ising spin models and show convergence to the same Majorana field theory in the continuum limit.
result: The models exhibit emergent general covariance and allow simulation of black hole particle production detectable via spin correlations.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical path for investigating fermionic QFT in curved spacetime using condensed matter systems.
keywords: quantum field theory in curved spacetime

title: In Situ Coherence Measurements Of Scattered Light In Magnetically Trapped Cold Atomic Clouds: Probe-Driven Atomic Dynamics
authors: Amilson R. Fritsch (ifsc-Usp), Hector Letellier (INPHYNI), Leonardo Lima Da Silva (ifsc-Usp), Pierre Azam (INPHYNI), Vanderlei Salvador Bagnato (ifsc-Usp), Robin Kaiser (INPHYNI), Mathilde Hugbart
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The use of temporal correlations in scattered photons to probe the microscopic dynamics of ultracold quantum gases has emerged as a powerful, minimally destructive approach for in situ analysis. Here, we demonstrate that temporal coherence spectroscopy can quantitatively characterize atomic motion in a magnetic trap, despite the perturbative effects of the probing light. By measuring the first-order correlation function g (1) ([MATH] ) of light scattered by a 87 Rb cloud confined in a quadrupole trap, we identify radiation-pressure-induced acceleration and heating as the origin of the apparent discrepancy between coherence spectra and temperatures inferred from time-of-flight measurements. A simple dynamical model incorporating these effects restores agreement between theory and experiment, establishing coherence spectroscopy as a reliable in situ probe of velocity distributions in trapped atomic ensembles. Our results pave the way for time-resolved studies of nonequilibrium dynamics and thermalization processes in confined cold gases, complementing conventional destructive imaging techniques.
tldr: This paper uses temporal coherence spectroscopy to measure atomic motion in a magnetic trap, focusing on probe-driven dynamics and heating effects.
motivation: To develop a minimally destructive in situ probe for velocity distributions in cold atomic clouds, overcoming limitations of conventional time-of-flight measurements.
method: Experimental measurement of the first-order correlation function g(1) of light scattered by 87Rb atoms in a quadrupole magnetic trap, combined with a dynamical model incorporating radiation-pressure effects.
result: The coherence spectra initially disagreed with temperature estimates from time-of-flight, but a model including radiation-pressure-induced acceleration and heating restored agreement.
conclusion: Coherence spectroscopy is a reliable in situ probe for velocity distributions in trapped cold gases, enabling time-resolved studies of nonequilibrium dynamics.

title: Coupled Van Der Pol Networks
authors: O. Viatchaninov O. Pokytnyi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18337v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we provide a complete analytical characterization of amplitude modes in a nonlinear Van der Pol network. The phase condition presented in the paper fully classifies all possible configurations, leading to a finite set of discrete solutions. This result provides a complete description of the limit cycles, including all stable oscillatory states for arbitrary network size, without relying on approximate or iterative numerical schemes. In addition, we provide a constructive theorem that yields an iterative scheme for approximating solutions of the corresponding boundary-value problem.
tldr: This paper provides a complete analytical characterization of amplitude modes in nonlinear Van der Pol networks, classifying all possible configurations and limit cycles.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of coupled nonlinear oscillators is important for many physical systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors derive a phase condition that fully classifies configurations and provide a constructive theorem for approximating solutions of the boundary-value problem.
result: They obtain a finite set of discrete solutions and a complete description of limit cycles for arbitrary network size without numerical schemes.
conclusion: The work offers a rigorous analytical framework for Van der Pol networks, but its relevance to the specified research interests is minimal.

title: Mutual Information Second Order Expansion Is The Pearson's Chi-square Statistic
authors: Marius Marinescu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that MI connects subtly and elegantly the two best-known state-of-the-art independence test statistics: the [MATH] and the Pearson's chi-square statistic [MATH]. Furthermore, we show that the MI connects directly those statistics by an elegant formula arising from a stochastic Taylor expansion of MI ([MATH]-method). MI second order term is precisely [MATH] up to a scale factor. As a consequence, by this connection, the difference between [MATH] and [MATH] can be explicitly quantified.
tldr: This paper shows that the second-order expansion of mutual information equals Pearson's chi-square statistic, connecting two independence test statistics.
motivation: To understand the relationship between mutual information and classical independence tests, and to quantify the difference between two widely used statistics.
method: The authors use a stochastic Taylor expansion (delta-method) to derive the second-order term of mutual information.
result: The second-order term of mutual information is precisely proportional to Pearson's chi-square statistic, providing an explicit connection.
conclusion: Mutual information and Pearson's chi-square are intimately linked, with the difference between them explicitly quantified via higher-order terms.

title: Cyclic And Constacyclic Codes Over Z4+iZ4
authors: Miguel Mart\'in (faculty Of Science,engineering - Bernoulli Institute, University Of Groningen), Ekin \"ozman
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study cyclic and constacyclic codes over the finite chain ring R=Z4+iZ4, where i^2=-1. We prove that all constacyclic codes over R are equivalent to cyclic codes. An algorithm to obtain generators for all simple root constacyclic codes over R is presented. Using a Gray map we then obtain linear Z4 codes from constacyclic codes over R. We present new best linear Z4 codes found using this method.
tldr: This paper studies cyclic and constacyclic codes over the finite chain ring Z4+iZ4, presenting an algorithm for generator computation and obtaining new linear Z4 codes via a Gray map.
motivation: To extend coding theory over finite rings, specifically Z4+iZ4, and to find new best linear Z4 codes.
method: Proves equivalence of constacyclic codes to cyclic codes over R, provides an algorithm for simple root constacyclic codes, and uses a Gray map to obtain Z4 codes.
result: Presents new best linear Z4 codes found using the proposed method.
conclusion: The study contributes to algebraic coding theory over finite chain rings, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Distribution Of $k$-th Maximum Order Statistics Of Independent, & Non-Identical Snr Random Variables In $\kappa-\mu$ Fading And Its Applications In $6g$
authors: Srinivas Sagar, Athira Subhash, Sheetal Kalyani
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper employs extreme value theory to establish the asymptotic distribution of the [MATH]-th maximum order statistics of signal to noise ratio (SNR) for a [MATH] fading channel with independent and non-identically distributed (i.n.i.d.) parameters. Since [MATH] encompasses well-known distributions such as Rice, Rayleigh, and Nakagami-m, the order statistics for these are also derived as special cases. We demonstrate the practical significance of our results by showcasing their applicability in several applications, including antenna selection in MIMO systems, backscatter systems, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, and UAV-assisted relay selection systems. Furthermore, by utilizing the [MATH]-th maximum order statistics, we derive expressions for outage probability and average throughput of [MATH]-th maximum order statistics. Comprehensive Monte Carlo simulations are carried out to verify the accuracy of the proposed results.
tldr: This paper derives asymptotic distributions of k-th maximum order statistics for SNR in κ-μ fading channels and applies them to various wireless communication systems.
motivation: Understanding the distribution of maximum order statistics of SNR is important for performance analysis of wireless systems like antenna selection and relay selection.
method: The authors use extreme value theory to derive the asymptotic distribution of the k-th maximum order statistic for i.n.i.d. κ-μ fading random variables, and validate with Monte Carlo simulations.
result: Closed-form expressions for outage probability and average throughput based on k-th maximum order statistics are obtained.
conclusion: The derived results are useful for analyzing and optimizing wireless communication systems in 6G contexts.

title: Function-Correcting Rt Codes: A Coding Framework For Parallel Channels
authors: Huiying Liu, Hongwei Liu, Sihem Mesnager
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Function-correcting codes have recently emerged as an effective approach to reducing coding redundancy when the objective is to reliably recover only the prescribed function values of the transmitted information, rather than the complete message itself. As a natural generalization of the Hamming metric, the Rosenbloom--Tsfasman metric (RT-metric) has attracted considerable attention due to its relevance to communication over parallel channels. Motivated by these two research directions, we introduce in this paper function-correcting RT codes (FCRTCs), which extend the framework of function-correcting codes from the Hamming metric to the more general RT metric. To investigate the fundamental problem of optimal redundancy, we introduce a new class of matrix codes, called irregular RT-distance codes, and establish a direct correspondence between the redundancy optimization problem for FCRTCs and the construction of such codes. This connection provides a unified framework for deriving redundancy bounds under the RT metric. For arbitrary functions, we establish general upper and lower bounds on the optimal redundancy of FCRTCs. We then specialize our analysis to several important classes of functions, namely RT-weight functions, RT-weight distribution functions, and RT-locally-two-valued binary functions, for which substantially sharper bounds are obtained by exploiting their specific structural properties. Furthermore, we present explicit constructions of FCRTCs for RT-weight distribution functions and prove that these constructions attain the optimal redundancy bounds in several cases. The proposed framework considerably extends the theory of function-correcting codes to the RT metric, provides new theoretical tools for studying reliable communication over parallel channels, and opens new perspectives for redundancy-efficient coding beyond the classical Hamming setting.
tldr: This paper introduces function-correcting codes under the Rosenbloom–Tsfasman metric for parallel channels, focusing on optimal redundancy bounds.
motivation: To reduce coding redundancy when only function values of transmitted information need recovery, and to extend function-correcting codes from Hamming metric to RT metric for parallel channel communication.
method: Introduces irregular RT-distance codes and establishes a correspondence between redundancy optimization and construction of such codes; derives general bounds and specializes to specific function classes.
result: Provides general upper and lower bounds on optimal redundancy for arbitrary functions, and sharper bounds for RT-weight, RT-weight distribution, and RT-locally-two-valued binary functions; explicit constructions achieve optimal bounds in several cases.
conclusion: The framework extends function-correcting codes to RT metric, offering new tools for reliable communication over parallel channels and redundancy-efficient coding beyond Hamming setting.

title: Quantum Logistic Map Considered As Discrete-time Heisenberg Equation
authors: Arkadiusz Or{\l}owski Maciej Janowicz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We represent scalar logistic iterates as multiplication operators on [MATH] and study their fixed matrix elements in the normalized shifted-Legendre basis. Three parameter regimes permit analytical control. At [MATH], every fixed matrix element converges to [MATH], where [MATH] is the Kronecker delta. At [MATH], the attracting period-two orbit yields phase-resolved limits for the even and odd subsequences. At [MATH], an exact Chebyshev-moment representation gives an [MATH] approach of every fixed matrix element at iteration [MATH] to [MATH]. The case [MATH] is treated only by a controlled finite numerical refinement study. Complementary finite diagnostics comprise matrix-element time dependence, a bifurcation-style plot, a time-averaged mean intensity, a normalized second-order intensity moment, and normalized scalar OTOC-type commutator correlation matrices. We also examine the separate finite-dimensional recursion [MATH], with fixed matrix [MATH], using diagonal and tridiagonal amplitude profiles. These operator-valued calculations are exploratory finite-time numerics. The analytical statements concern fixed matrix elements for the specified basis indices; they are distinct from the finite-resolution observations and do not imply operator-norm convergence. A regularized phase-space lift is included as a controlled visualization.
tldr: The paper studies the quantum logistic map as a discrete-time Heisenberg equation, focusing on matrix elements in a shifted-Legendre basis and finite-time numerics.

result: Analytical results for fixed matrix elements at specific parameter values; finite-resolution numerics show time dependence and bifurcation-like behavior.
conclusion: The work is exploratory and does not provide operator-norm convergence; it is a mathematical study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Shared Vulnerabilities In Robustness-Optimized Defenses: One Breach Exposes The Family
authors: Hanrui Wang, Ruihao Zheng, Shuo Wang, Isao Echizen, Xingbo Dong, Zhe Jin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adversarial robustness optimization aims to preserve correct prediction under adversarial perturbations, and has produced substantial robustness gains through methods such as adversarial training and adversarial purification. However, we identify a new security risk: these gains can create shared vulnerabilities across defenses. Once one representative robustness-optimized defense is effectively breached, the broader family may become exposed. Studying this risk requires separating genuine transferability from distortion-induced degradation and from the algorithmic gains of sophisticated attacks. We therefore introduce stricter transfer-only protocols and a deliberately simple adaptive attack, PGDTransfer, to test whether robustness-optimized defenses share transfer-only vulnerability under controlled conditions. We further introduce Adversarial Sensitivity Maps (AdvSMs) to visualize and quantify shared alignment beyond differentiable classifiers, including stochastic and non-differentiable defenses. Across adversarially trained classifiers, purification-based defenses, and LVLMs with robust visual encoders, we identify natural transferability within each robustness family, i.e., transfer that arises even with simple PGD-style optimization rather than specialized transferable-attack design. The risk is already severe for purification: PGDTransfer reaches an average transfer attack success rate of [MATH] across filtering-, compression-, and diffusion-based purifiers under [MATH], suggesting that purifier defenses may no longer provide reliable protection. As attacks improve, currently stronger robustness families may face the same risk. Future defenses should therefore treat vulnerability diversity and transfer-only isolation as security objectives, rather than optimizing only individual robustness.
tldr: This paper studies shared vulnerabilities in robustness-optimized adversarial defenses, showing that breaching one defense can expose the entire family.
motivation: Adversarial robustness optimization has produced substantial gains, but the paper identifies a new security risk: these gains may create shared vulnerabilities across defenses.
method: The authors introduce stricter transfer-only protocols and a simple adaptive attack, PGDTransfer, to test transfer-only vulnerability. They also propose Adversarial Sensitivity Maps (AdvSMs) to visualize shared alignment.
result: PGDTransfer achieves high average transfer attack success rates across purification-based defenses, indicating that purifier defenses may no longer provide reliable protection.
conclusion: Future defenses should treat vulnerability diversity and transfer-only isolation as security objectives rather than optimizing only individual robustness.

title: Value Iteration For Stochastic Parity Games
authors: Ichiro Hasuo Kittiphon Phalakarn
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the first (bounded) value iteration algorithm for the quantitative analysis of stochastic parity games, a fundamental model for probabilistic verification with [MATH]-regular objectives. Existing algorithms are based on strategy iteration, which repeatedly computes optimal strategies for one player while fixing the other, leading to high computational cost. Our algorithm instead operates directly on a lattice-theoretic characterization of winning probabilities, exploiting structural properties of (almost-sure qualitative) winning states under parity objectives. We prove correctness and convergence of the proposed algorithm.
tldr: This paper presents a value iteration algorithm for stochastic parity games, which are used in probabilistic verification with omega-regular objectives.
motivation: Existing strategy iteration algorithms for stochastic parity games are computationally expensive; the authors aim to develop a more efficient algorithm.
method: The algorithm operates on a lattice-theoretic characterization of winning probabilities and exploits structural properties of almost-sure qualitative winning states under parity objectives.
result: The proposed algorithm is the first bounded value iteration algorithm for stochastic parity games, with proven correctness and convergence.
conclusion: Value iteration offers a more efficient alternative to strategy iteration for quantitative analysis of stochastic parity games.

title: CryptanalysisBench: Can LLMs Do Cryptanalysis?
authors: Lukas Fluri, Avital Shafran, Nicholas Carlini, Matthew Jagielski, Milad Nasr, Orr Dunkelman, Eyal Ronen, Florian Tram\`er
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cryptanalysis - the task of finding attacks against cryptographic schemes - sits at the intersection of mathematical reasoning and cybersecurity, two areas where LLMs have advanced fastest. Cryptanalysis represents both a clean testbed for frontier reasoning (as practical attacks can be automatically verified) and a domain with unusually high stakes, since the primitives under study underpin our digital security. In this paper we ask whether LLMs can do cryptanalysis, and find that the answer is increasingly yes. We introduce CryptanalysisBench, 191 tasks across six families of cryptographic primitives (block ciphers, hash functions, etc.) drawn primarily from four NIST standardization competitions. Our benchmark consists of three tiers: (i) primitives with known practical breaks; (ii) primitives with no known practical break, evaluated both at full strength and as scaled-down variants; and (iii) a challenge set of production primitives at the frontier of cryptanalysis. Five frontier models (Claude Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Mythos 5, GPT 5.5, and the open-weights GLM 5.2) break 65%-86% of Tier 1 schemes, 6-12 Tier-2 schemes at full strength, and 24-61 across all scaled-down variants. Beyond deriving known results, models produce novel cryptanalysis, such as a key-recovery attack that exploits a design flaw in the SpoC AEAD and an error in KINDI's published CCA-security proof, both to the best of our knowledge not previously known. We release CryptanalysisBench as a tool to help track if (or when) AI cryptanalysis becomes a serious factor and as a scaffold for stress-testing candidate schemes before deployment. The attacks that the benchmark already surfaces are an early snapshot of a fast-moving frontier that may soon match, and in places exceed, the published state of the art.
tldr: This paper evaluates the ability of large language models to perform cryptanalysis on various cryptographic primitives.
motivation: To assess whether LLMs can contribute to cryptanalysis, a domain requiring mathematical reasoning and cybersecurity expertise, and to benchmark their performance.
method: The authors introduce CryptanalysisBench, a benchmark of 191 tasks across six families of cryptographic primitives, and test five frontier LLMs on these tasks.
result: The LLMs break 65%-86% of Tier 1 schemes, 6-12 Tier-2 schemes at full strength, and produce novel cryptanalysis including a key-recovery attack on SpoC and an error in KINDI's security proof.
conclusion: LLMs are increasingly capable of cryptanalysis, and the benchmark can track progress and stress-test candidate schemes.
