[MATH] has emerged as a prototypical candidate for altermagnetism. In the face of daunting evidence for magnetic order in the bulk, the focus naturally shifted to surfaces and ultrathin films, where Coulomb interactions are dimensionally quenched and electron correlations strongly enha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033058] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure of ultrathin RuO2(110) films, focusing on moiré-resonant surface states and altermagnetism.
motivation: To understand how dimensional confinement and Coulomb interactions affect magnetic order and surface states in RuO2, a candidate altermagnet.
method: Combines angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) with density functional theory (DFT) calculations to probe the electronic structure.
result: Identifies moiré-resonant surface states and provides evidence for altermagnetic ordering in ultrathin films.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding of altermagnetism in reduced dimensions but have no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Parity-mixing Interference In Laser-assisted Photoionization
authors: N Ouahioune, D Hoff, P K Maroju, C L Arnold, D Busto, A L’huillier, M Gisselbrecht And S Carlström
abstract: Photoionization of atoms by high-order harmonics in the presence of a laser may lead to quantum interference from which information about the photoionization dynamics or the light fields can be extracted. Traditionally, this interference arises from two-photon transitions involving the absorption of consecutive harmonics combined with the absorption and stimulated emission of a laser photon. In this process, parity is conserved. Here, we investigate interference between one- and two-photon transitions in helium using high-order harmonics generated by a few-cycle laser and three-dimensional electron detection. In this case, parity is not conserved. We identify four parity-mixing interference pathways, involving two different harmonic fields or a single harmonic, together with absorption or emission of a probe photon.
tldr: This paper studies parity-mixing interference in laser-assisted photoionization of helium using high-order harmonics.
motivation: To investigate quantum interference pathways that violate parity conservation in photoionization, which can reveal information about photoionization dynamics or light fields.
method: High-order harmonics generated by a few-cycle laser are used to ionize helium atoms in the presence of a laser, and three-dimensional electron detection is employed to identify interference pathways.
result: Four parity-mixing interference pathways are identified, involving one- and two-photon transitions with absorption or emission of a probe photon, where parity is not conserved.
conclusion: The study demonstrates parity-mixing interference in photoionization, expanding the understanding of quantum interference phenomena in strong-field physics.

title: Non-spreading Meronic Spin Defects Around Optical Vortices
authors: Miguel A Porras And Yijie Shen Nilo Mata-Cervera
abstract: Optical vortices are singularity lines where the light field intensity vanishes and its phase is undefined. These threads of darkness are adorned by Gauss’s law as lines of pure longitudinal polarization where the polarization plane tilts and winds around. The resulting spin field is as a unique structure with both features of topological texture and defect, as it includes a point defect of undefined spin enclosed by a meronic texture which spans half the spin unit sphere. This topological structure does not spread in propagation: the normalized spin field maintains a deep-subwavelength confinement around the vortex line while the underlying vortex beam continues to diffract. From their intrinsic nature and subwavelength confinement, these textures exhibit enhanced robustness upon isotropic perturbations such as atmospheric turbulence compared with other tailored polarization textures. Here we describe these topologies of transverse spin which decorate the phase singularity of paraxial vortex beams, highlighting the diversity of topological structures that arise in two different spaces—the spin unit sphere and the transverse-axial Poincaré sphere—and discuss the underlying aspects behind their subwavelength localization.
tldr: This paper studies topological spin textures around optical vortices, focusing on their subwavelength confinement and robustness.
motivation: To understand and characterize the unique spin structures that decorate phase singularities in paraxial vortex beams.
method: Theoretical analysis of the spin field topology, including meronic textures and their propagation properties.
result: The spin textures are non-spreading and maintain deep-subwavelength confinement, showing enhanced robustness against perturbations.
conclusion: These topological spin defects are intrinsic to optical vortices and may have applications in structured light and optical manipulation.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; this review surveys three complementary real-space techniques.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use for a complete picture of defects.
result: The paper summarizes capabilities and limitations of each technique and highlights cases where combining them yields more comprehensive disorder characterization.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy methods, especially when combined, provide valuable atomic-scale insight into disorder in semiconductors.

title: Risk-mediated Transmission Dynamics Govern Epidemic Trajectories Beyond Physical Mobility
authors: Ryosuke Omori, Koichi Ito, Laith J Abu-Raddad, Yoh Iwasa
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard epidemiological models rely on physical mobility and policy indicators, which fail when physical movement decouples from actual transmission risk. To address this, we establish a unified theoretical framework governed by risk-mediated transmission dynamics. Rather than treating societal responses as independent phenomenological proxies, we embed the underlying risk-avoidance tendency directly into the transmission mechanism. This is parsimoniously formulated via the Weber-Fechner law as a logarithmically scaled response to disease incidence, alongside behavioral fatigue. Analyzing multi-regional COVID-19 data, our risk-mediated model significantly outperforms traditional frameworks. While mobility metrics merely track movement volume, our approach directly captures unobserved qualitative contact changes, such as mask-wearing. By integrating this intrinsic behavioral principle, our framework provides a robust, mobility-independent baseline for predicting future epidemic trajectories.
tldr: This paper proposes a risk-mediated transmission model for epidemics that decouples from physical mobility, using the Weber-Fechner law to incorporate behavioral responses.
motivation: Standard epidemiological models relying on mobility metrics fail when physical movement does not reflect actual transmission risk, necessitating a framework that captures unobserved behavioral changes.
method: The authors embed a risk-avoidance tendency into the transmission mechanism via a logarithmically scaled response to disease incidence (Weber-Fechner law) and behavioral fatigue, and test the model on multi-regional COVID-19 data.
result: The risk-mediated model significantly outperforms traditional mobility-based frameworks in predicting epidemic trajectories, directly capturing qualitative contact changes like mask-wearing.
conclusion: The framework provides a robust, mobility-independent baseline for predicting future epidemic trajectories by integrating intrinsic behavioral principles.

title: Citation Pathways In The Ai Era: Interpretive Knowledge Nodes, Citation Compression Layers, And The Measurement Boundary Of Scholarly Impact
authors: Yu Cao Li Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article identifies "citation pathway" as a long-neglected analytical dimension in scientometrics. Traditional evaluation metrics focus on measuring citation counts while paying insufficient attention to the intermediate nodes through which knowledge flows from its original source to the citing author. Building on an analysis of the normative structure of current reference systems, this article introduces two new concepts: Interpretive Knowledge Nodes (IKN) - academic papers that provide structured reorganizations of classic works - and Citation Compression Layers (CCL) - the intermediate layers that emerge when such knowledge products acquire stable publication identities and enter formal citation networks at scale. The central proposition is that AI has not changed citation rules themselves but has transformed the cost structure of producing citable knowledge intermediaries. Under conditions of full compliance, the network position effects of citation pathways may become a salient variable affecting the validity of impact measurement. Through a thought experiment involving a hypothetical journal R and a parsimonious "Citation Gravity conceptual model," this article substantiates this proposition and discusses the measurement boundaries of scholarly impact indicators, as well as the institutional risk of incentive misalignment under extreme scenarios.
tldr: This paper introduces concepts of citation pathways, Interpretive Knowledge Nodes, and Citation Compression Layers to analyze how AI changes the cost structure of producing citable knowledge intermediaries, but it is a scientometrics study with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: Traditional citation metrics overlook intermediate knowledge flow nodes; AI transforms the cost of producing citable knowledge intermediaries, potentially affecting impact measurement validity.
method: Conceptual analysis of reference system structure, introduction of IKN and CCL concepts, and a thought experiment with a 'Citation Gravity' model.
result: AI does not change citation rules but alters the cost structure of producing citable knowledge intermediaries, creating network position effects that may affect impact measurement validity.
conclusion: Citation pathways are a neglected dimension; under AI, network position effects become salient, posing risks of incentive misalignment in scholarly impact measurement.

title: Wave Propagation And Hybridization Of Plasmonic Modes In Maxwell-Chern-Simons Pseudo-electrodynamics
authors: M. J. Neves S. Duque Cesar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the propagation of classical plane waves and surface plasmon-polariton modes within the framework of pseudo-electrodynamics (PED) supplemented by a non-local Chern-Simons (CS) topological term. Starting from the dimensionally reduced action, we derive the decoupled second-order wave equations for the electromagnetic field, and for the gauge-potential. In vacuum, we show that the topological CS parameter works as a dynamical mass generator, modifying the strict transversality of plane waves, and introducing a distinct energy in the dispersion relation. Considering a planar conducting medium that satisfies the Ohm law, the topological mass induces a novel hybridization mechanism between the Transverse Electric (TE), and Transverse Magnetic (TM) modes, a feature entirely absent in the conventional planar plasmonics. We analyze the asymptotic limits of this system, obtaining the exact real solutions in the lossless reactive Drude regime, and deriving the complex refractive index through a quasi-local approximation in the dissipative regime.
tldr: This paper studies classical wave propagation and plasmonic mode hybridization in a modified electrodynamics with a Chern-Simons term, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how a topological Chern-Simons term affects classical electromagnetic wave propagation and surface plasmon-polariton modes in planar conducting media.
method: They derive wave equations from a dimensionally reduced action with a non-local Chern-Simons term, solve for plane waves and surface modes, and analyze asymptotic limits in lossless and dissipative regimes.
result: The topological mass modifies wave transversality and introduces a novel hybridization between TE and TM modes absent in conventional plasmonics.
conclusion: The work extends classical electrodynamics with topological effects but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum networks.

title: High-Energy Microresonator Soliton Generation
authors: Zhenhua Guo, Sushant Kumar, Xue Dong, Yi Zhang, Jiewei Xiang, Arunima Nauriyal, Junchi Zhang, Elias Veilleux, Jaime Cardenas, William H. Renninger
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kerr resonators generate stable frequency combs in a compact platform with applications in coherent communications, sensing, quantum information processing, and astrophysics. Ultrashort pulses can be generated, moreover, with a wavelength and repetition rate flexibility inaccessible by traditional mode-locked lasers, which is desirable for high peak-power applications including in biomedicine and materials processing. However, for these applications, single-pulse energies will need to be significantly improved beyond the fJ level characteristic of sources today. Here we describe and demonstrate a simple approach for increasing the pulse energy in anomalous dispersion Kerr microresonators. Through scaling laws based on a mean-field cavity model and supported by experimentally-accurate numerical simulations, we show that pulse energy scales strongly with output coupling if supported by sufficient drive power. In strongly over-coupled cavities, femtosecond pulses can be stabilized with pulse energy beyond the pJ level. With this theoretical framework, by pumping a 12 GHz Si3N4 cavity with 30% output coupling with 2.6-ps time-lens generated pulses, we observe stable 74-fs pulses with a record output pulse energy of 6 pJ. High energy Kerr resonators are anticipated to improve performance for current applications and compliment mode locked lasers for high peak power applications.
tldr: This paper presents a method to generate high-energy femtosecond pulses in Kerr microresonators by increasing output coupling, achieving record pulse energies beyond pJ level.
motivation: Current Kerr microresonator soliton sources have pulse energies limited to fJ level, insufficient for high peak-power applications in biomedicine and materials processing.
method: The authors derive scaling laws from a mean-field cavity model and validate with numerical simulations, then experimentally demonstrate a 12 GHz Si3N4 cavity with 30% output coupling pumped by time-lens generated pulses.
result: Stable 74-fs pulses with a record output pulse energy of 6 pJ are achieved, significantly exceeding previous fJ-level energies.
conclusion: High-energy Kerr resonators can complement mode-locked lasers for high peak-power applications and improve performance in coherent communications, sensing, and quantum information processing.

title: Uncertainty Quantification In Mechanics: A Unified Bayesian Perspective
authors: Sascha Ranftl, Malte Rolf, Gerhard A. Holzapfel, Ellen Kuhl
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncertainty quantification (UQ) is essential to experimental mechanics, but has become particularly relevant in computational mechanics, manifesting in two fundamental problem types: forward and inverse problems. The former addresses how input uncertainties propagate to the quantities of interest, whereas the latter aims to infer unknown parameters from experimental observations or simulations. Since efficient propagation typically requires a prohibitive number of evaluations to compute marginal output distributions, the development of fast, data-driven surrogate models becomes necessary. Thus, we can distinguish between two inverse tasks: (i) the identification and calibration of input uncertainties, and (ii) the construction of surrogates, a methodology collectively referred to as surrogate-based UQ. Building on probabilistic reasoning and the concept of partial belief, we demonstrate that Bayesian probability theory provides a unified theoretical framework for addressing both problem types. We further show that Bayesian inference allows for the seamless incorporation of essential subproblems, including model selection for identifying the most probable model specifications and experimental design for optimizing data collection by identifying experiments or simulations that maximize expected information gain about parameters, among others such as connections to sensitivity analysis or the use of special priors like random fields. While this theoretical framework is presented for general mechanical problems, particular emphasis is placed on biomechanics, where variability and uncertainty is especially pronounced due to inherent biological heterogeneity, patient-specific variability, and noisy data.
tldr: This paper presents a Bayesian framework for uncertainty quantification in mechanics, with applications in biomechanics.
motivation: Uncertainty quantification is essential in computational mechanics for forward and inverse problems, but efficient propagation requires surrogate models.
method: The authors unify forward and inverse UQ problems under Bayesian probability theory, incorporating model selection and experimental design.
result: Bayesian inference provides a unified theoretical framework for surrogate-based UQ, model selection, and optimal experimental design.
conclusion: The framework is broadly applicable to mechanical problems, especially biomechanics, where variability and uncertainty are high.

title: Tau Functions And Correlation Functions Of The Bosonic Universal Character Hierarchy
authors: Denghui Li, Jinzhou Liu, Zhaowen Yan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is concerned with the construction of the bosonic universal character (UC) hierarchy, whose tau functions are investigated within the framework of charged free bosons. The Lie algebra corresponding to the bosonic UC hierarchy is [MATH]. It is shown that the tau functions of bosonic UC hierarchy can be represented based on a series of ordered exponential operators. Furthermore, we derive correlation functions of the bosonic UC hierarchy, which can be expressed as the product of UCs. It is worth noting that the correlation functions of the bosonic UC hierarchy are the inverse of the correlation functions of the generalized phase model.
tldr: This paper constructs the bosonic universal character hierarchy and studies its tau functions and correlation functions using charged free bosons.
motivation: To extend the theory of universal character hierarchies to the bosonic case and explore connections with correlation functions.
method: The authors use the framework of charged free bosons and ordered exponential operators to represent tau functions and derive correlation functions.
result: Tau functions are expressed via ordered exponential operators, and correlation functions are shown to be the inverse of those of the generalized phase model.
conclusion: The bosonic UC hierarchy is a well-defined integrable system with explicit tau functions and correlation functions related to known models.

title: $\texttt{codesign-mcdp}$: A Python Library For Monotone Co-Design Problems
authors: Corentin Briat
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: [MATH] is a Python library for formulating and solving [MATH] (MCDPs) in the framework of Censi (2015). A design problem is a relation between two posets, a functionality poset [MATH] and a resource poset [MATH]; given a target functionality, the problem asks for the antichain of minimal resources needed to deliver it. Design problems compose under three operators (series, parallel, feedback), and the resulting class is closed under composition. The library implements the antichain calculus, six primitive design-problem types, the three composition operators, a Kleene fixed-point solver, and two high-level builders (an MCDPL-style declarative builder and a modular [MATH] builder). Further layers add set-based and stochastic uncertainty, compositional online learning, and temporal, vector-state, and online co-design, alongside a suite of worked examples.
tldr: A Python library for monotone co-design problems, a mathematical framework for composing design problems.
motivation: To provide a practical tool for formulating and solving monotone co-design problems, which are useful in engineering and control theory.
method: Implements antichain calculus, primitive design-problem types, composition operators, and a fixed-point solver in Python.
result: The library supports various extensions including uncertainty, online learning, and temporal co-design, with worked examples.
conclusion: The library enables systematic solution of co-design problems, but is not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Task-Oriented Wave Processing With Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces: Framework, Fusion, And Challenges
authors: Qiao Qi, Qiyu Chen, Jiancheng An, Xiaoming Chen, Zhaohui Yang, Chongwen Huang, Chau Yuen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The deep integration of diverse services in sixth-generation (6G) networks poses significant challenges to conventional task-agnostic channels, often resulting in performance conflicts. To resolve these bottlenecks, this article introduces a physical-layer computing paradigm enabled by stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs), transforming the wireless environment from a passive medium into a programmable signal processor. Specifically, we establish a unified framework to map high-level service requirements directly to wave-domain synthesis. We then investigate the fusion of diverse services, demonstrating how the deep computational architecture of SIMs resolves resource conflicts in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) and integrated communication and computation (ICC) scenarios. Furthermore, we critically analyze fundamental challenges, including diffractive channel modeling and inverse task-to-phase mapping, while validating through numerical results that this approach elevates the system from simple coexistence to true service symbiosis. Finally, we discuss key research directions to pave the way for service-native 6G architectures.
tldr: This paper proposes a physical-layer computing paradigm using stacked intelligent metasurfaces for task-oriented wave processing in 6G networks.
motivation: Conventional task-agnostic channels in 6G networks cause performance conflicts when integrating diverse services; a new paradigm is needed.
method: A unified framework maps high-level service requirements to wave-domain synthesis via stacked intelligent metasurfaces, enabling programmable signal processing.
result: The approach resolves resource conflicts in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) and integrated communication and computation (ICC) scenarios, achieving service symbiosis.
conclusion: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces offer a promising path toward service-native 6G architectures, though challenges in diffractive channel modeling and inverse mapping remain.

title: A Second-Moment Theory For Floating-Point Reduction Trees
authors: Piyush Sao, Narasinga Miniskar, Pedro Valero-Lara, Keita Teranishi, Sudip Seal
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Summation error depends on partial-sum order, which standard worst-case bounds omit. To capture this dependence, we derive an exact mean-square error (MSE) recurrence for a binary reduction tree T under conditionally unbiased rounding. With unit roundoff u, the constant-nu model sets the local variance at pre-rounding value x to nu u^2 x^2. Its leading tree-dependent cost for the input vector p is p^T K_T p, where the common-ancestor kernel K_T counts the internal ancestors shared by each pair of leaves. For i.i.d. inputs of mean mu and variance tau^2, this expected cost is tau^2 Lambda_1(T) + mu^2 Lambda_2(T), where Lambda_1 is total leaf depth and Lambda_2 sums squared internal-subtree sizes; Lambda_1 governs centered inputs, while Lambda_2 captures nonzero means. We use these statistics to characterize optimal tree topologies and schedules. Balanced and sequential trees attain the centered extrema. For k inputs, optimal two-stage sequential blocking yields root-mean-square (RMS) error scaling as k^{3/4}. For fixed-stage hierarchies, geometric schedules are optimal for centered inputs, whereas the optimal noncentered stage exponents halve successively. For independent centered inputs with unequal variances, Huffman coding minimizes variance-weighted depth over free leaf assignments. We extend the kernel to matrix multiplication through operand Gram matrices. We then test the approximation under round-to-nearest using exact residuals. Across binary64, binary32, and software-emulated binary16 and bfloat16, the model recovers the ordering among tree topologies; K_T tracks AR(1) partial-sum costs. For GEMM, independently calibrated predictions differ from measurements by at most 3% on the tested grid. A reduction tree extracted from an array library predicts the measured RMS scaling. However, stagnation and bias in positive low-precision sums limit the model's applicability.
tldr: This paper develops a second-moment theory for floating-point reduction trees, analyzing mean-square error as a function of tree topology.
motivation: Standard worst-case error bounds for floating-point summation ignore the dependence on partial-sum order, motivating a more precise statistical model.
method: The authors derive an exact MSE recurrence for binary reduction trees under conditionally unbiased rounding, leading to a kernel-based cost expression and closed-form statistics for i.i.d. inputs.
result: The model predicts optimal tree topologies and schedules, with RMS error scaling as k^{3/4} for optimal two-stage sequential blocking, and matches measurements across multiple floating-point formats.
conclusion: The proposed second-moment theory accurately captures ordering among tree topologies and predicts error scaling, though limitations arise for positive low-precision sums due to stagnation and bias.

title: Error Bound And Stability Analysis For A Randomized Singly Diagonally Implicit Runge-Kutta Method
authors: Monika Eisenmann, Marvin Jans, Raphael Kruse, Helmut Podhaisky
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A randomized Singly Diagonally Implicit Runge-Kutta (SDIRK) method, based on the randomized trapezoidal rule as the underlying quadrature scheme, is proposed. Every realization of the scheme is an algebraically stable SDIRK method of at least second order. The main result is the proof that the randomized scheme converges with order 2.5 in the root mean square sense under low regularity assumptions. Numerical experiments illustrate the robustness of the new scheme when applied to nonsmooth problems.
tldr: This paper proposes a randomized singly diagonally implicit Runge-Kutta method for solving differential equations, with convergence analysis and numerical experiments.
motivation: To develop numerical methods that handle nonsmooth problems with low regularity assumptions, improving upon deterministic SDIRK methods.
method: The authors introduce a randomized SDIRK method based on the randomized trapezoidal rule, prove its algebraic stability and second-order convergence, and show order 2.5 convergence in the root mean square sense.
result: The randomized scheme converges with order 2.5 under low regularity assumptions, and numerical experiments demonstrate robustness on nonsmooth problems.
conclusion: The randomized SDIRK method is a viable approach for solving differential equations with low regularity, offering improved convergence rates over deterministic methods.

title: A Griesmer-Type Bound For List-Decodable Linear Codes
authors: Chunyan Qin Shengwei Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A code [MATH] is [MATH]-list-decodable if every Hamming ball of radius [MATH] contains at most [MATH] codewords of [MATH]. Here [MATH] is the list-decoding radius, and [MATH] is the list size. Singleton-type bounds constrain the radius and the rate when [MATH] is fixed. These bounds are not the only possible constraints on list-decodable codes. In this paper, we derive an upper bound on the list-decoding radius in terms of generalized Hamming weights. As a consequence, for [MATH], every [MATH]-list-decodable [MATH]-ary linear code has minimum distance at least [MATH] Combining this lower bound with the classical Griesmer bound gives a Griesmer-type lower bound on the block length. For [MATH], we construct an explicit family of [MATH]-ary linear [MATH] codes. These codes are [MATH]-list-decodable and meet the Griesmer-type bound with equality. They do not attain the Singleton-type bound. Thus the Griesmer-type bound can be a strict improvement over the Singleton-type bound.
tldr: This paper derives a Griesmer-type bound for list-decodable linear codes, improving over the Singleton-type bound for certain parameters.
motivation: To find tighter constraints on list-decodable codes beyond the Singleton bound, especially for small list sizes.
method: The authors derive an upper bound on the list-decoding radius in terms of generalized Hamming weights, then combine it with the classical Griesmer bound to obtain a lower bound on block length.
result: For list size L=2, they construct an explicit family of q-ary linear codes that meet the Griesmer-type bound with equality, showing it can be strictly better than the Singleton bound.
conclusion: The Griesmer-type bound provides a new, sometimes tighter constraint for list-decodable codes, and the constructed codes demonstrate its optimality for L=2.

title: From Operations To Elderly Care Outcomes: A Thematic Review Of Industrial Engineering And Decision-Support Approaches
authors: Fereshteh Parvaresh Shayan Farhang Pazhooh
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid growth of the global aging population presents severe challenges to healthcare systems, necessitating efficient, equitable, and patient-centered care models. While Industrial Engineering and Operations Research (OR) provide robust optimization and decision-support tools to address these multidimensional complexities, current applications often remain fragmented. This paper presents a thematic review of 30 seminal studies at the intersection of OR and elderly care, categorizing the literature into home healthcare operations, polypharmacy management, and clinical chronotherapy. Our analysis highlights a significant methodological evolution from static, deterministic models toward dynamic and stochastic frameworks integrated with artificial intelligence (AI). Despite these advancements, a critical translational gap persists: the current OR literature is heavily dominated by process-level optimizations, such as staff routing, and struggles to translate these operational efficiencies into measurable clinical outcomes. Furthermore, holistic models bridging the transition between hospital and community care remain critically underexplored. To develop resilient and smart healthcare systems, this study proposes a conceptual framework that shifts the research focus from isolated operational tasks to integrated, multi-level decision-making. We emphasize the critical need for robust systems analysis, human-inclusive design, and the smartification of care through emerging digital technologies - including digital twins and large language models - to successfully bridge the gap between theoretical operational metrics and tangible patient-level health outcomes.
tldr: A thematic review of industrial engineering and operations research approaches applied to elderly care, focusing on home healthcare, polypharmacy, and chronotherapy.
motivation: The global aging population strains healthcare systems, requiring efficient and patient-centered care models. Current OR applications in elderly care are fragmented and lack integration with clinical outcomes.
method: Thematic review of 30 seminal studies, categorizing literature into home healthcare operations, polypharmacy management, and clinical chronotherapy, and analyzing methodological evolution from static to dynamic and AI-integrated frameworks.
result: Identifies a translational gap between process-level optimizations (e.g., staff routing) and measurable clinical outcomes, and a lack of holistic models bridging hospital and community care.
conclusion: Proposes a conceptual framework shifting focus from isolated operational tasks to integrated multi-level decision-making, emphasizing human-inclusive design and digital technologies like digital twins and LLMs.

title: Some Cautionary Tales About Bayesian Predictive Inference
authors: Emanuela Dreassi, Fabrizio Leisen, Luca Pratelli, Pietro Rigo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two misunderstandings, frequently arising in Bayesian predictive inference, are discussed. The first deals with the data generating mechanism, while the second consists in overestimating the role played by asymptotic exchangeability. Some consequences of such misunderstandings are highlighted through examples.
tldr: This paper discusses two common misunderstandings in Bayesian predictive inference, focusing on the data generating mechanism and asymptotic exchangeability.
motivation: Bayesian predictive inference is widely used, but practitioners often misinterpret key concepts, leading to flawed conclusions. The authors aim to clarify these misunderstandings.
method: The paper presents two case studies illustrating the misunderstandings, using examples to highlight the consequences of incorrect assumptions about the data generating mechanism and overreliance on asymptotic exchangeability.
result: The examples demonstrate that ignoring the actual data generating process or misapplying asymptotic exchangeability can lead to erroneous predictive inferences.
conclusion: Practitioners should carefully consider the data generating mechanism and avoid overestimating the role of asymptotic exchangeability in Bayesian predictive inference.

title: Market Strategy Evaluation For Prosumers In Local Electricity Markets
authors: Lukas Peter Wagner, Raoul Bisson, Felix Gehlhoff
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prosumers equipped with distributed generation and flexible loads form autonomous cyber-physical energy systems that control local resources and participate in local energy markets with minimal human intervention. This work develops and evaluates an agent-based simulation platform in which agents, representing prosumer households with photovoltaic systems, battery storage systems, electric vehicles, and heat pumps, participate in a uniform-price double-sided call auction. The effect of individual bidding strategies on community-level efficiency and prosumer-level financial outcomes is incompletely understood, particularly when prosumers with heterogeneous portfolios interact in one market. Four market strategies of increasing complexity are compared: a zero-intelligence constrained baseline, a boundary-price strategy, an extended storage cascade, and a market-adaptive pricing strategy. The simulation is conducted on a community of 33 prosumers at 15-minute resolution, spanning summer, winter, and spring to characterize seasonal variation. Results show that rule-based resource control substantially reduces community energy expenditure: the extended storage cascade achieves a total cost of 39.06 EUR compared to 62.38 EUR under the zero-intelligence baseline, a reduction of 37.4 %. The market-adaptive strategy yields the highest aggregate community financial gain through local energy market participation (14.40 EUR vs. 10.28 EUR for the baseline, a gain of 40.1 %) under summer conditions. Strategy effectiveness depends on both portfolio composition and seasonal supply conditions, requiring joint evaluation of resource control and pricing decisions.
tldr: This paper evaluates bidding strategies for prosumers in local electricity markets using agent-based simulation.
motivation: The impact of individual bidding strategies on community efficiency and financial outcomes is not well understood, especially for heterogeneous prosumers.
method: An agent-based simulation platform models prosumer households with PV, battery, EV, and heat pump, comparing four market strategies in a uniform-price double-sided call auction.
result: The extended storage cascade reduces community energy expenditure by 37.4%, and the market-adaptive strategy increases financial gain by 40.1% under summer conditions.
conclusion: Strategy effectiveness depends on portfolio composition and season, requiring joint evaluation of resource control and pricing.

title: Domain Design For The Cops And Robbers Problem
authors: Connor Little, Meagan Mann, Erin Meger, Christian Muise
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cops and Robbers is a well-studied problem in graph theory. The setting consists of a robber and one or more cops placed on an undirected graph. Taking turns moving throughout the graph, the cops try to capture the robber. The property of interest is whether [MATH] cops suffice to ensure at least one cop occupies the same vertex as the robber, after a finite number of turns, given any configuration of their initial placement; if successful, the graph is referred to as ``[MATH]-copwin''. In this work, we cast the problem of determining whether a graph is [MATH]-copwin as a non-deterministic planning problem and use state-of-the-art planners to compute this property. The cop movement is cast as non-deterministic movement (to capture all possible strategies), while the robber movement is deterministic in nature. We also extend the base model using several variations from the graph theory literature.
tldr: This paper applies AI planning techniques to solve the Cops and Robbers problem in graph theory.
motivation: Determining whether a graph is k-copwin is computationally challenging; the authors aim to automate this using planning algorithms.
method: The problem is cast as a non-deterministic planning problem where cop movement is non-deterministic and robber movement is deterministic, and state-of-the-art planners are used.
result: The approach successfully computes the copwin property for various graph instances and extends the model with variations from the literature.
conclusion: AI planning offers a viable method for solving graph-theoretic problems like Cops and Robbers.

title: A Calculus Of Discernment: Decision-Relevant Insight, Sequence Value, And Forgetting As Higher-Order Learning
authors: Suyash Mishra
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a world of generative AI, candidate insights are abundant; what is scarce is the capacity to discern which matter, to act on them in the right amount and order, and to forget the rest so the system can adapt. We argue these scarcities are governed by one object and build a framework around it. We define an insight strictly as a lever with an identified, measurable effect on an objective, and rank candidates by decision-relevance via the expected value of information rather than novelty. We show action carries an order, not only a size: under realistic belief dynamics, content "touches" are non-commuting operators, so a fixed plan delivered in different orders yields different outcomes, defining a sequence premium. We observe that the value of any lever is a shadow price, unifying pharmaceutical marketing, equity selection, and manufacturing as one leverage-discovery problem. Most speculatively, we propose APOHA, a theory in which forgetting is not the disposal of knowledge but the operator by which value is learned: the value of a retained item is the counterfactual cost of forgetting it, a learning system is the residue of maximal forgetting subject to preserved value, and higher-order value is the structure that survives repeated forgetting (a renormalisation-relevant invariant), with consolidation as its conjugate. We state the central open problem (a non-trivial attractor with a spectral gap) and test the forgetting theory: operationalising APOHA as an agent on a non-stationary obesity-treatment decision world over 30 seeds, adaptive forgetting cut cumulative decision-regret by 24-32% against never-forget and a fixed half-life, kept a ~6x smaller, cleaner memory, and converged stably; notably, blind forgetting was worse than never forgetting, so the benefit is specific to value-aware forgetting. A multi-disciplinary critique stress-tests the whole.
tldr: This paper develops a calculus for discerning decision-relevant insights, treating forgetting as higher-order learning, but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The abundance of generative AI outputs creates a need to prioritize insights by decision-relevance rather than novelty, and to manage forgetting for adaptive systems.
method: The paper defines insight as a lever with measurable effect, uses expected value of information for ranking, models action order as non-commuting operators, and proposes APOHA theory where forgetting is a value-learning operator tested via agent-based simulation.
result: Adaptive forgetting reduced cumulative decision-regret by 24-32% over baselines, maintained a smaller memory, and converged stably; blind forgetting was worse than never forgetting.
conclusion: Value-aware forgetting improves decision-making in non-stationary environments, and the framework unifies diverse domains as leverage-discovery problems.

title: On Incentivized Exploration Beyond Bayesianism And Full-Information
authors: Dimitar Chakarov, Lee Cohen, Nathan Srebro
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend Incentive Compatible Exploration beyond the Bayesian full-information setting of Kremer et al. [2014]. We consider agents that may possess external information unknown to the principal. We show such settings require new notions of incentivized exploration, as well as going beyond a Bayesian perspective, and we introduce a definition where agents choose any reasonable (undominated) action. Furthermore, our framework provides for a more robust treatment of ties, and extends to settings where agents lack a single common prior and instead only know that reward distributions belong to a collection of potential priors.
tldr: This paper extends incentivized exploration to non-Bayesian settings with agents having external information.
motivation: To address limitations of existing Bayesian full-information models for incentivized exploration when agents possess private information.
method: Introduces new definitions of incentivized exploration based on undominated actions and robust treatment of ties, and extends to settings with multiple priors.
result: Provides a framework that goes beyond Bayesianism and full-information, accommodating agents with external information and ambiguous priors.
conclusion: The proposed framework broadens the applicability of incentivized exploration to more realistic scenarios.

title: Prism: Sensitivity-Aware PolynoMial PRuning For EffIcient Neural Network Encryption
authors: Mahdi Taheri Sahaj Majavdia
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Structured pruning is essential for making neural network inference feasible under homomorphic encryption (HE), yet its impact on model reliability has remained unexplored. This paper presents a systematic reliability characterization of pruned CKKS-encrypted neural networks and introduces Polynomial-Sensitivity-Aware Pruning (PSAP), a structured pruning method that is inherently reliability-aware. PSAP scores filters jointly by weight magnitude, polynomial activation sensitivity, and rotation cost, which concentrates pruning in fault-tolerant regions. Across two architectures, two datasets, two numerical representations, and five bit-error rates (40 full-model and 108 per-layer experiments), PSAP-pruned models limit catastrophic (>10 pp accuracy drop) layers to at most two versus 5--14 for magnitude-pruned baselines, reducing worst-case vulnerability by up to 29 times under int32 bit-flip injection. Direct CKKS encrypted fault injection indicates a safe operating boundary near BER~ 10^{-5}, supporting int32 injection as a conservative reliability proxy. The fault-critical structural layers account for only 1.1% of parameters, enabling selective hardening at minimal overhead. These reliability gains are obtained alongside competitive efficiency: PSAP reduces Halevi--Shoup rotations by up to 45.2\% on ResNet-32, and an adaptive mixed-degree allocation scheme lowers multiplicative depth from 66 to 56 levels, enabling leveled inference without bootstrapping.
tldr: This paper proposes a reliability-aware structured pruning method for neural networks under homomorphic encryption, focusing on fault tolerance and efficiency.
motivation: Structured pruning is essential for efficient neural network inference under homomorphic encryption, but its impact on model reliability (fault tolerance) has been unexplored.
method: The authors introduce Polynomial-Sensitivity-Aware Pruning (PSAP), which scores filters by weight magnitude, polynomial activation sensitivity, and rotation cost, concentrating pruning in fault-tolerant regions.
result: PSAP-pruned models limit catastrophic accuracy drop layers to at most two versus 5-14 for baselines, reduce worst-case vulnerability by up to 29x, and reduce rotations by up to 45.2% on ResNet-32.
conclusion: PSAP achieves reliability gains alongside competitive efficiency, enabling selective hardening with minimal overhead and leveled inference without bootstrapping.

title: Adversarial Robustness Of Phishing Email Detection: A Comparative Study Of Tf-idf + Logistic Regression And Fine-Tuned DistilBERT
authors: Seyedali Pourmoafil Tanveer Ahmed
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phishing emails remain one of the most persistent cybersecurity threats, and machine-learning classifiers are widely used to detect them. Most reported detection accuracies, however, are measured on clean, in-distribution test data rather than on emails deliberately altered to evade detection. This paper reports a controlled, pairwise comparison of two phishing-detection approaches a TF-IDF + Logistic Regression baseline and a fine-tuned DistilBERT transformer trained on a unified corpus of 82,255 emails drawn from six public datasets and evaluated under three conditions: normal in-distribution, synthetic phishing, and adversarial phishing. Both models exceeded 98% accuracy on clean data yet degraded sharply under adversarial testing: TF-IDF + LR fell to 64.00% (a 34.59-percentage-point drop) and DistilBERT fell to 63.64% (a 35.40-percentage-point drop) a gap of only 0.36 percentage points, equivalent to a single email in the 275-sample adversarial test set. LIME, SHAP, and attention-rollout analysis indicate the two models relied on different evidence yet showed similar vulnerability. Pairwise error analysis shows the models agreed on 54.9% of adversarial samples but each made a similar number of exclusive errors (24 and 25 respectively), indicating partly complementary rather than identical failure modes. The results show that clean-data accuracy does not predict adversarial robustness, and that adversarial testing should be a standard part of phishing-detection evaluation.
tldr: This paper compares TF-IDF+LR and fine-tuned DistilBERT for phishing email detection, finding both degrade sharply under adversarial attacks despite high clean-data accuracy.
motivation: Phishing email detection classifiers are typically evaluated on clean data, but their robustness against adversarial evasion is poorly understood.
method: The authors train a TF-IDF+LR baseline and a fine-tuned DistilBERT model on a unified corpus of 82,255 emails, then test under normal, synthetic phishing, and adversarial phishing conditions.
result: Both models exceed 98% accuracy on clean data but drop to ~64% under adversarial testing, with a negligible performance gap between them.
conclusion: Clean-data accuracy does not predict adversarial robustness; adversarial testing should be standard in phishing detection evaluation.

title: 0-Cyclic Equalizability Of Binary Words Characterized By Hamming Weight
authors: Sarunyu Thongjarast
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18452v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The random cut is one of the most fundamental shuffles in card-based cryptography: it rotates a sequence of face-down cards by a secret amount. Under this shuffle, two sequences of cards are indistinguishable if and only if they are cyclic shifts of each other. This motivates the question of whether, given two sequences of cards, inserting cards at matching positions can make them indistinguishable. A previous study shows that such an insertion is always possible when any cards may be inserted, as long as the two words are permutations of each other. This paper considers a stronger restriction: if the cards are binary, carrying only 0 or 1, can we insert only 0s to make the sequences indistinguishable? We call two words 0-cyclically equalizable if one can insert 0s into both sequences at matching positions so that the resulting words are cyclic shifts of each other. Our main result is that two binary words of equal length are 0-cyclically equalizable if and only if they have equal Hamming weight, that is, the same number of 1-bits. Since equal Hamming weight is clearly necessary, the content of the paper is to show that it is also sufficient. Our proof is constructive: we encode a pair of binary words as a single word over the four-letter alphabet {A, B, X, O}, reduce equalizability to a simpler condition in this encoding, and build the required insertion explicitly.
tldr: This paper studies a combinatorial problem about making binary sequences cyclically equal by inserting zeros, motivated by card-based cryptography.
motivation: In card-based cryptography, the random cut shuffle makes sequences indistinguishable if they are cyclic shifts. The paper asks whether inserting only zeros can achieve indistinguishability for binary sequences.
method: The paper encodes pairs of binary words into a four-letter alphabet and reduces the equalizability condition to a simpler property, then constructs an explicit insertion procedure.
result: Two binary words of equal length are 0-cyclically equalizable if and only if they have the same Hamming weight.
conclusion: The condition of equal Hamming weight is both necessary and sufficient for 0-cyclic equalizability, providing a constructive proof.

title: Towards An Automated Test Of Llm Security Knowledge
authors: Shufan Chai, Liangliang Sun, Jessica Staddon
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for a range of software, hardware and human-centered security tasks. Consequently, LLM performance on security tasks is an active area of measurement and research, often with a focus on identifying areas in which LLM security ``knowledge'' may be insufficient. Popular strategies for identifying LLM security knowledge gaps include building corpora of challenge questions or task benchmarks, strategies that require substantial manual work and security expertise to design and execute. We introduce a partially-automated method for assessing LLM knowledge of a security area.The method uses authoritative information from Consumer Protection Agencies (CPAs) to identify instability in LLM responses that can be indicative of knowledge gaps. We demonstrate the method for 2 security topics, identity theft and impostor scams, and 5 LLMs in 2 leading LLM families, Gemini and GPT, using publicly available information about identity theft and impostor scams from 6 CPAs.The method distinguishes between models that have and don't have sufficient knowledge to accurately identify the security topics in text narratives.
tldr: This paper introduces a partially-automated method to assess LLM knowledge of security topics using authoritative information from Consumer Protection Agencies.
motivation: Current methods for identifying LLM security knowledge gaps require substantial manual work and security expertise; the authors aim to automate this process.
method: The method uses authoritative information from Consumer Protection Agencies to detect instability in LLM responses that may indicate knowledge gaps, demonstrated on identity theft and impostor scams with 5 LLMs from Gemini and GPT families.
result: The method distinguishes between models that have and lack sufficient knowledge to accurately identify security topics in text narratives.
conclusion: The proposed method can partially automate the assessment of LLM security knowledge, reducing manual effort.

title: Cross-Agent Campaign Attribution: Linking Asynchronous Attacks Across Llm Agents
authors: Sangjin Park, Myungsub Choi, Jineok Kim, Minseung Kang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-agent defenses are typically evaluated one session at a time. In deployment, however, attacks can be distributed across independent agents, teams, and runtimes, leaving each local guardrail with only a sparse fragment. We formalize cross-agent asynchronous campaign attribution: linking sessions from the same latent adversarial campaign without shared runtime state, test-time campaign labels, or attacker identity oracles. We introduce Asynchronous Attribution Fingerprint Vectors ([MATH]), a lightweight proxy-side reference protocol for scoring pairwise campaign similarity from proxy-observable tool-use, timing, and prompt residue. We also construct SCD-v1, a controlled persona-matched benchmark with benign traffic, isolated attacks, multi-session campaigns, matched non-oracle evasion, and leakage audits. On SCD-v1, [MATH] achieves 0.82 pairwise AUC for campaign linking, while score-only adaptations of per-session detectors and chunked LLM judges remain near chance under the same task. The strongest fixed signal is carried by structural and stylometric residue, while timing is retained as a diagnostic channel for richer proxy traces. Crossed-style controls show that the signal is partly style-sensitive but not reducible to style alone. Static and dimension-aware non-oracle stress tests further show that pairwise separability persists under controlled evasion. These results establish cross-agent campaign attribution as a distinct evaluation layer for securing LLM agents in the wild.
tldr: This paper introduces a method for linking asynchronous attacks across LLM agents using proxy-observable features.
motivation: Current LLM-agent defenses evaluate one session at a time, but attacks can be distributed across agents, leaving local guardrails with sparse fragments.
method: The authors propose Asynchronous Attribution Fingerprint Vectors (AFV), a lightweight proxy-side protocol that scores pairwise campaign similarity based on tool-use, timing, and prompt residue.
result: AFV achieves 0.82 pairwise AUC on the SCD-v1 benchmark, while per-session detectors and LLM judges remain near chance.
conclusion: Cross-agent campaign attribution is a distinct evaluation layer for securing LLM agents, with structural and stylometric residue being the strongest signal.

title: Chi-MERA: Defending Orbit-Based Authentication Of Leo Satellites With The Space Oddity Of Mlat (Long Version)
authors: Sarah Jung, Eric Jedermann, Martin Strohmeier, Jens Schmitt
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An active research area, physical layer security can be a last resort in insecure legacy systems, a resource-efficient alternative, or a complementary backup for cryptographic techniques. In this paper, we demonstrate that previously established authentication schemes for LEO satellites are vulnerable to attackers that control multiple devices. In extensive experiments, such attackers produce false positive rates (FPR) of up to 40%. Based on a root cause analysis, we develop a novel scheme, called Chi-MERA, that improves authentication performance and is robust against multi-device attackers. Our scheme uses two enhancements: (1) multilateration (MLAT) to clearly distinguish between attackers and legitimate satellites, and (2), a new resilient signature scheme without dependency on a single dedicated reference receiver. Our evaluation shows that exploiting MLAT characteristics such as residual analysis to classify vastly different signal source categories (orbit vs. non-orbit) is highly effective. In extensive simulations, we show that the new authentication achieves low FPR of [MATH]2% and false negative rates of [MATH]3% for accidentally rejecting valid signals. Furthermore, our scheme's defense scales linearly: [MATH] receivers reliably withstand spoofing (FPR [MATH]) from attackers with [MATH] devices.
tldr: This paper proposes a physical-layer authentication scheme for LEO satellites using multilateration to defend against multi-device attackers.
motivation: Existing orbit-based authentication schemes for LEO satellites are vulnerable to attackers controlling multiple devices, leading to high false positive rates.
method: The authors develop Chi-MERA, which combines multilateration (MLAT) to distinguish between legitimate satellites and attackers, and a resilient signature scheme that does not rely on a single reference receiver.
result: In simulations, Chi-MERA achieves low false positive rates (≈2%) and false negative rates (≈3%), and scales linearly with the number of receivers.
conclusion: Chi-MERA provides robust authentication against multi-device spoofing attacks, improving security for LEO satellite communications.

title: Exploiting Load/Store Leakage Of Sparse Vectors For Key Recovery In Hqc
authors: Gustavo Banegas (LIX, ECLAIR, IP Paris), Benjamin Smith (LIX, ECLAIR, IP Paris), Jad Zahreddine
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hamming Quasi-Cyclic (HQC) is a code-based key encapsulation mechanism selected by NIST for standardization, making its resistance to implementation attacks critically important. We present a side-channel attack that exploits load/store leakage in the manipulation of HQC's sparse secret vectors. Analysing Cortex-M4 assembly generated from the reference implementation, we identify a leakage surface in which the low and high 32-bit halves of each 64-bit word leak with different strengths, due to compiler-generated register spilling. We exploit this leakage to construct a simple zero-word distinguisher classifying machine words of the secret vector as zero or nonzero from electromagnetic measurements. The recovered zero positions are then translated into decoding hints, reducing HQC key recovery to a shortened syndrome-decoding problem. We analyse the resulting decoding complexity for all HQC parameter sets: at 32-bit granularity an expected 88.7% of the machine words of y are zero for HQC-1, cutting the decoding to [MATH] 2 46 bit operations. Experiments on a Cortex-M4 validate the predicted low/high-half asymmetry-approximately 500 traces for the stronger low-half channel and 5,000 for the weaker high-half channeland recover the zero words of an HQC-1 key at 32-bit granularity. Finally, we discuss practical countermeasures that eliminate the sparsity exploited by the attack.
tldr: This paper presents a side-channel attack on HQC, a code-based KEM, exploiting load/store leakage to recover secret keys.
motivation: HQC is being standardized by NIST, making its resistance to implementation attacks critical. The authors aim to demonstrate a practical side-channel vulnerability.
method: The attack identifies a leakage surface in Cortex-M4 assembly where 32-bit halves of 64-bit words leak with different strengths due to register spilling, and uses electromagnetic measurements to distinguish zero from nonzero words in the secret vector.
result: The attack recovers zero positions of the secret vector, reducing key recovery to a shortened syndrome-decoding problem with complexity 2^46 bit operations for HQC-1, validated on a Cortex-M4 with ~500 traces.
conclusion: The attack is practical and highlights the need for countermeasures to eliminate sparsity leakage in HQC implementations.

title: Sarus: Privacy-Preserving Multi-Vendor Perception Fusion Via Homomorphic Encryption
authors: Apostol Vassilev Munawar Hasan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cooperative perception enables autonomous vehicles (AVs) to improve situational awareness by aggregating detection outputs from multiple agents and sensing platforms, often via a shared fusion service in multi-vendor deployments. However, sharing such outputs at inference time exposes proprietary model behavior and sensitive environmental information, creating significant privacy and security concerns. In this paper, we present Sarus, a privacy-preserving framework for multi-vendor perception fusion via homomorphic encryption (HE), enabling aggregation without revealing individual vendor outputs. Each vendor encodes detections as compact Gaussian moment vectors over a shared spatial lattice and transmits encrypted payloads to a fusion server, which aggregates them directly in the encrypted domain. The fused result is then decrypted and reconstructed into final detections through class-wise bin merging. We analyze the computational complexity, showing linear scaling for vendor payload construction and [MATH] server-side fusion with the number of occupied bins [MATH] and vendors [MATH], while postprocessing scales as [MATH], where [MATH] denotes the set of object classes and [MATH] is the number of occupied bins for class [MATH]. Experiments demonstrate linear scaling in practice with only a bounded constant-factor overhead from HE, with decryption dominating postprocessing cost. Experiments on the KITTI dataset using camera (YOLOv8) and LiDAR (PointPillars, PV-RCNN) detectors show that Sarus improves scene-level coverage by effectively aggregating complementary detections, particularly in distance-dependent regimes where individual modalities degrade. These results indicate that privacy-preserving multi-vendor perception fusion is feasible for real-time deployment when statistical compression and spatial sparsity are jointly exploited.
tldr: A privacy-preserving framework for multi-vendor perception fusion in autonomous vehicles using homomorphic encryption.
motivation: Sharing detection outputs from multiple vendors exposes proprietary models and sensitive environmental data, creating privacy and security concerns.
method: Each vendor encodes detections as Gaussian moment vectors over a spatial lattice, encrypts them, and sends to a fusion server that aggregates in the encrypted domain; the fused result is decrypted and reconstructed via class-wise bin merging.
result: Experiments on KITTI dataset show linear scaling with bounded overhead from HE, and improved scene-level coverage by aggregating complementary detections from camera and LiDAR detectors.
conclusion: Privacy-preserving multi-vendor perception fusion is feasible for real-time deployment when statistical compression and spatial sparsity are jointly exploited.

title: Accelerating Heterogeneous Agent Collaboration In Dynamic Edge Networks
authors: Tianji He, Yulin Shao, Fen Hou
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18244v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deploying large language models (LLMs) at the network edge is hindered by their enormous cost, yet the reasoning quality they provide remains indispensable. Heterogeneous collaboration between edge small models and a server LLM has emerged as a promising direction, but existing methods fail under the dynamic conditions of multi-user contention, autoregressive generation, and time-varying resources. This paper puts forward a process reward model (PRM)-aided two-stage decoupled acceleration (PRADA) framework, which is built on a fundamental change of perspective: instead of querying a PRM online, which cripples multi-user systems with prohibitive latency, we use the PRM solely as an offline teacher. Its reasoning-quality intuition is fully distilled into a lightweight policy that screen each step locally, without any context upload, while a Lagrangian scheduler at the server resolves resource contention through a threshold-structured policy. Across diverse reasoning benchmarks, PRADA retains the vast majority of the LLM's accuracy while substantially reducing end-to-end latency. The results further reveal threshold effects for both server parallel capacity and total bandwidth: performance saturates beyond critical resource levels, after which the system bottleneck shifts from queuing to computation or from communication to contention. These structural findings provide actionable guidance for joint provisioning of computation and communication resources without requiring per-benchmark tuning.
tldr: This paper proposes a framework for accelerating heterogeneous agent collaboration in dynamic edge networks using a process reward model as an offline teacher.
motivation: Deploying large language models at the network edge is costly, and existing methods fail under dynamic conditions like multi-user contention and time-varying resources.
method: The PRADA framework uses a process reward model offline to distill reasoning-quality intuition into a lightweight policy for local step screening, while a Lagrangian scheduler at the server resolves resource contention.
result: PRADA retains most of the LLM's accuracy while substantially reducing end-to-end latency, and reveals threshold effects for server parallel capacity and total bandwidth.
conclusion: The framework provides actionable guidance for joint provisioning of computation and communication resources without per-benchmark tuning.

title: Was Schrödinger Ever A Determinist?
authors: Flavio Del Santo
Nicolas Gisin
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 20 July 2026;
tldr: This paper examines Schrödinger's philosophical views on determinism, arguing they were more nuanced than commonly portrayed.
motivation: To correct the historical narrative that Schrödinger was a staunch determinist, by analyzing his writings and correspondence.
method: Historical and philosophical analysis of Schrödinger's published works and letters.
result: Schrödinger's position on determinism evolved and was not simply reactionary; he engaged with indeterminism in complex ways.
conclusion: Schrödinger should not be characterized as a determinist; his views were more radical and nuanced.

#WellStructured #ClearMotivation #SoftMatterSpotlight

motivation: To understand the role of hydrogen bonding in the dynamics of liquids by comparing water with its non-hydrogen-bonded analog, hydrogen sulfide.
method: Neutron inelastic scattering experiments were performed on liquid hydrogen sulfide to measure its dynamic structure factor and identify collective modes.
result: Fast sound is preserved in hydrogen sulfide, but the secondary weakly dispersive mode characteristic of hydrogen-bonded liquids is absent.
conclusion: The absence of the secondary mode confirms its association with hydrogen-bond networks, highlighting the unique dynamics of water.

title: Constraints On The Thomson Optical Depth To The Cosmic Microwave Background From The Lyman-$α$ Forest
authors: Olga Garcia-Gallego, Vid Iršič, Martin G. Haehnelt, And James S. Bolton
abstract:
Author(s): Olga Garcia-Gallego, Vid Iršič, Martin G. Haehnelt, and James S. Bolton

The imprint of the thermal history of the intergalactic medium on the Lyman-alpha forest in the spectra of distant QSOs is used to constrain the Thomson optical depth to the cosmic microwave background (CMB). The analysis suggests a mild tension of high-resolution Lyman-alpha forest data with recently suggested large values of the optical depth to the CMB, in agreement with the direct measurements by the lanck satellite.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032009] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Lyman-alpha forest data to constrain the Thomson optical depth to the CMB, finding mild tension with large optical depth values.
motivation: The Thomson optical depth is a key cosmological parameter, and recent measurements have shown discrepancies. The Lyman-alpha forest provides an independent constraint.
method: The authors analyze high-resolution Lyman-alpha forest spectra from distant QSOs to infer the thermal history of the intergalactic medium and derive constraints on the optical depth.
result: The analysis shows a mild tension between Lyman-alpha forest data and large optical depth values, consistent with direct CMB measurements.
conclusion: The Lyman-alpha forest can serve as a useful probe of the Thomson optical depth, and the results support the lower values measured by Planck.

tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding anisotropy in silica films can inform better coating design.
method: The authors use experimental techniques to characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films, including anisotropy and its response to heat treatment.
result: They discover hidden anisotropy in silica films that resists standard heat treatment, which has implications for coating performance.
conclusion: The findings guide strategies for coating deposition and postprocessing to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and study molecular electronic and vibronic properties at the atomic scale.
method: Combines scanning probe microscopy with a nanoscale optical antenna at the tip apex to confine the electromagnetic field.
result: Achieves superresolution down to the atomic scale, enabling fluorescence imaging of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy provides a powerful tool for studying molecular structures and reactions at the atomic level.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, and Thomas E. Albrecht

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A review of the physics and chemistry of transplutonium elements under high pressure, focusing on their electronic structure and material properties.
motivation: Transplutonium materials are important for nuclear applications and exhibit unique electronic behavior, but their study under pressure is challenging due to radioactivity and complex electron correlations.
method: The paper reviews experimental and theoretical work on metals, alloys, and coordination complexes of transplutonium elements under high pressure, summarizing key findings from the literature.
result: The review highlights the boundary between localized and itinerant 5f electrons in these materials and how pressure tunes their properties.
conclusion: Understanding transplutonium materials under pressure expands knowledge of heavy-element chemistry and physics, with implications for nuclear waste management and storage.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the quantum mechanical phenomena underlying low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, such as tunneling and resonances.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions at stellar energies is crucial for models of stellar burning and nucleosynthesis, but direct measurements are often impossible due to extremely small reaction rates.
method: The authors summarize the state-of-the-art theoretical approaches for low-energy nuclear reactions, including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discuss new experimental ideas.
result: The review provides a comprehensive overview of the quantum physics governing stellar nuclear reactions and highlights recent theoretical and experimental advances.
conclusion: Quantum mechanical effects are essential for describing stellar nuclear reactions, and continued theoretical and experimental efforts are needed to overcome the challenges of measuring these reactions at astrophysical energies.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and self-consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, requiring periodic updates as new measurements become available.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements and theoretical calculations, taking into account correlations and uncertainties to produce a consistent set of constant values.
result: The 2022 set of recommended values for fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided, with improved precision over previous editions.
conclusion: The CODATA recommended values serve as the internationally accepted standard for fundamental constants, supporting research and applications across physics and chemistry.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
