tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering single-particle and collective behaviors.
motivation: To unify the understanding of self-alignment in active systems and its implications for biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: Review of existing models and experimental observations, presenting a unified mathematical and conceptual framework.
result: Self-alignment enables novel behaviors such as orbiting in harmonic traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a fundamental property that reshapes motion in active systems, with potential for groundbreaking applications.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser pulses to generate ultrasound waves for deep-tissue imaging.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review discusses the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy enables imaging of optical contrast at millimeter-to-centimeter depths with high resolution, and multimodal approaches enhance its capabilities.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical imaging, with ongoing developments in multimodal systems.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nonlinear elasticity theory applied to buckling, creases, and cusps in growing soft matter, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding morphological instabilities in soft materials is important for materials science and biology, but the paper does not address quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: The review integrates techniques from nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory and conformal mapping.
result: It provides a modern treatment of the Biot instability and related phenomena.
conclusion: The paper is a valuable resource for soft matter physics but falls outside the scope of the user's research interests.

title: Machine-learning-enabled Solvent Engineering For Uniform Quantum Dot Packing In Efficient And Stable Quantum-dot Light-emitting Diodes
authors: Beomsoo Chun, Byong Jae Kim, Hyeongjin Kim, Jeong Han Song, Yeongsik Kim, Jaehoon Lim And Jeonghun Kwak
abstract: Colloidal quantum dots (QDs) offer size-tunable optoelectronic properties and solution processability, yet achieving uniformly packed emissive layers remains a bottleneck for high-performance quantum-dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs). Here, we report a machine learning -guided solvent optimization strategy to produce homogeneous QD films. Five representative solvent parameters are evaluated, and multiple regression models are trained against film uniformity derived from atomic force microscopy. Among them, support vector regression provides the highest predictive accuracy for film homogeneity. Guided by these predictions, we formulate a mixed solvent that closely matches the target profile, yielding superior packing homogeneity, which is confirmed by grazing-incidence small-angle x-ray scattering. QLEDs fabricated with this formulation exhibit an external quantum efficiency of 20.6% and an operational lifetime of 468.5 h at 20 000 cd m−2, surpassing all single-solvent controls. These findings establish packing homogeneity as a decisive factor for device performance and introduce a generalizable and scalable framework for data-driven design of solution-processed devices, holding strong potential for next-generation optoelectronic systems.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to optimize solvent mixtures for uniform quantum dot packing in QLEDs, achieving high efficiency and long lifetime.
motivation: Achieving uniformly packed emissive layers is a bottleneck for high-performance quantum-dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs).
method: Five solvent parameters were evaluated, and multiple regression models (including support vector regression) were trained to predict film uniformity from atomic force microscopy data; a mixed solvent was formulated based on predictions.
result: The optimized solvent yielded superior packing homogeneity, and QLEDs achieved 20.6% external quantum efficiency and 468.5 h operational lifetime at 20,000 cd/m².
conclusion: Packing homogeneity is a decisive factor for device performance, and the data-driven framework is generalizable for solution-processed devices.

title: Improving Punching "Power": Reconsidering The Roles Of Initial Strike Velocity And Effective Mass
authors: Joseph L. Natale
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We review the principal features of one-dimensional, elastic collisions pertinent to modeling strike-mediated impacts in martial arts and combat sports contexts. Arguing for the post-collision velocity of a stationary, target mass as a useful proxy for determining overall punch efficacy, we demonstrate that pre-collision velocities for real strikes are bounded, such that speed prior to impact has a more limited effect on the impulse experienced by said target than suggested by supporting literature. We find that the value of incoming, "effective" mass -- despite eluding uniform establishment criteria or measurement protocols across the same body of literature -- exerts an independent influence on the target velocity which can, in principle, match or exceed that of the strike speed. We perform explicit numerical analyses to supplement these theoretical considerations, in dynamical regimes relevant to real human combat, and then briefly discuss the potential for a given fighter to attain a fold-increase in effective mass (from a reasonable baseline value based on bodyweight, and supported by previous work) sufficient to realize limits for upper-limb strikes to the body, in practice, as a trainable goal.
tldr: This paper analyzes the physics of punching in martial arts, focusing on the roles of initial strike velocity and effective mass in determining punch efficacy.
motivation: The authors aim to clarify the relative importance of speed versus effective mass in generating impact force, challenging the common emphasis on speed.
method: They use one-dimensional elastic collision models and numerical simulations to analyze post-collision target velocity as a proxy for punch efficacy.
result: They find that pre-collision velocity has a limited effect on impulse due to bounded speeds, while effective mass can independently match or exceed the influence of speed.
conclusion: Training to increase effective mass may be as important as improving speed for enhancing punch power in combat sports.

title: Long-term Coexistence Of Epidemics And Risk Awareness: Impacts Of Adaptive Human Response And Fatigue
authors: Abdallah Alsammani Mozzamil Mohammed
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive human behavior is widely recognized as a key determinant of epidemic dynamics, yet remains elusive to incorporate into epidemic models in a mechanistically transparent and analytically tractable manner. Here, we introduce a modeling framework in which population-level awareness is represented explicitly as a dynamic behavioral state that governs individual accessibility for interaction, rather than modifying intrinsic transmission probabilities. Awareness emerges endogenously in response to infection prevalence and decays through behavioral fatigue, generating a closed feedback loop between disease dynamics and social accessibility. This framework reveals that awareness-driven accessibility alone can produce transient epidemic waves, while epidemic trajectories ultimately converge to a long-term coexistence of infection and risk awareness. By separating behavioral accessibility from biological transmission processes, we show that awareness responsiveness and behavioral fatigue jointly regulate both transient epidemic structure and long-term endemic burden without altering the epidemic invasion threshold. These results identify awareness-driven accessibility as a fundamental and previously underrepresented component of epidemic dynamics, providing a mechanistic basis for explicitly integrating adaptive human behavior into epidemic modeling and informing public health preparedness for emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases.
tldr: This paper models epidemic dynamics with adaptive human awareness and fatigue, showing that awareness-driven accessibility can lead to long-term coexistence of infection and risk awareness.
motivation: Adaptive human behavior is a key determinant of epidemic dynamics but is often poorly incorporated into models; the authors aim to provide a mechanistically transparent and analytically tractable framework.
method: The authors introduce a modeling framework where population-level awareness is a dynamic behavioral state that governs individual accessibility for interaction, forming a feedback loop with infection prevalence.
result: Awareness-driven accessibility alone can produce transient epidemic waves, and trajectories converge to a long-term coexistence of infection and risk awareness without altering the epidemic invasion threshold.
conclusion: Awareness-driven accessibility is a fundamental component of epidemic dynamics, and the framework provides a mechanistic basis for integrating adaptive human behavior into epidemic modeling.

title: Distribution-First Population Simulation: Collapse, Calibration, And Recall In Non-WEIRD Llm Persona Modeling
authors: Gurkan Ozkan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synthetic-population tools increasingly run every individual as an independent large language model (LLM) agent. Using real survey microdata, we show that this paradigm has a basic failure mode, and we set a distribution-first corrective against it, all measured with a deterministic, construct-validated verifier on non-WEIRD (Turkey-first) data. First, N independent LLM agents grounded on 2,414 real World Values Survey respondents fail to reproduce the population's response distribution: they pile onto a modal default (four scenarios x five seeds: concentration 0.36->0.69, entropy 1.46->0.77, 85% collapse, TVD=0.44), and the collapse is a predictable function of scenario structure (r=0.55 with a single-answer structure). Second, Verbalized Sampling (VS) fixes the field's chronic under-dispersion without training in three model families (fidelity +7 to +10; significant on Qwen, p=0.002, d=6.2), yet the same move universally overshoots into over-dispersion (SD-ratio 0.4-0.56 -> 1.26-1.37), a structural property of VS. Third, survey fidelity transfers only weakly to agentic behavior: in a single-model, single-domain booking task, a persona is dominated by a cheapest-default (~80%) that income modulates but does not override (comfort choice 0%->7%->32% across income bands). Fourth, a placebo-controlled memorization attack and an election backtest show VS keeps aggregate strength while subgroup and individual claims are contaminated by recall and underdetermination. We close with the corrective: model the distribution once (VS) and assign it to grounded characters at O(1) cost, with a budget-aware router whose honest AUC is 0.805, not the tautological 1.0 of a code-derived oracle. The central contribution needs no realism claim: it measures the internal inconsistency of the independent-agent route and the conditions under which the distribution-first route calibrates.
tldr: This paper studies distribution collapse in LLM-based population simulations and proposes a distribution-first corrective, but is unrelated to quantum information theory or quantum networks.
motivation: LLM agents used for synthetic populations fail to reproduce real survey distributions, collapsing to a modal default. The authors aim to diagnose and fix this under-dispersion.
method: They run independent LLM agents on World Values Survey data, measure collapse via concentration and entropy, and propose Verbalized Sampling (VS) to calibrate distributions. They also test agentic behavior in a booking task and conduct memorization attacks.
result: VS fixes under-dispersion but overshoots into over-dispersion; survey fidelity does not transfer to agentic tasks; distribution-first approach with a budget-aware router achieves honest AUC 0.805.
conclusion: The independent-agent route is internally inconsistent; a distribution-first approach calibrates better at low cost, but claims about subgroups and individuals are contaminated by recall.

title: Mapping The Narrow Corridor With Large Language Models
authors: Ebrahim M Songhori
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Acemoglu and Robinson (2024 Nobel laureates in Economics) trace national histories in The Narrow Corridor as paths through a two-dimensional (state power, society power) space but plot none: quantifying the two axes at each moment is the labor-intensive, judgment-laden task that has kept the framework qualitative. We ask whether large language models (LLMs) can operationalize it. We introduce a reproducible, provider-agnostic pipeline that scores a country period by period using chain-of-thought (events first, then score) and in-context anchoring on prior periods, against an explicit rubric with schema-validated output. As a proof of concept we produce a twelve-country trajectory atlas (Iran, France, the United Kingdom, the United States, China, Chile, Colombia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Lebanon, Zambia, Somalia, and India), chosen to place at least two countries in each of the book's four Leviathan types, and compare four models. We assess the scores for consistency with an expert index (V-Dem) and for inter-model agreement, reading agreement as concurrent consistency rather than accuracy, since such indices likely appear in the models' training data, and discuss conceptually how the biases of an LLM annotator and a human expert differ. Code, prompts, runs, and an interactive gallery of the animated trajectories are released.
tldr: This paper uses LLMs to quantify state and society power from historical narratives, mapping countries onto a two-dimensional political framework.
motivation: Acemoglu and Robinson's 'Narrow Corridor' framework is qualitative; the authors aim to operationalize it by using LLMs to score historical periods on state and society power.
method: A reproducible pipeline uses chain-of-thought prompting and in-context anchoring to score country-periods against a rubric, with schema-validated output; four LLMs are compared.
result: A twelve-country trajectory atlas is produced; scores are compared with V-Dem expert indices and inter-model agreement is assessed.
conclusion: LLMs can operationalize the framework, but biases differ from human experts; the approach is reproducible and provider-agnostic.

title: A Converse To Generalized Runcorn's Theorem
authors: Ivica Smoli\'c Vjekoslav Kova\v{c}
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an inverse problem for generalized Runcorn's theorem motivated by an apparent paradox of lunar magnetism. In mathematical terms, we characterize square-integrable complex functions [MATH] such that $[MATH][MATH]u[MATH]|x|r_-[MATH]a[MATH]b[MATH]r_-<a><b><r_+[MATH]f$ into spherical harmonics, and explicit representations are provided.
tldr: This paper studies an inverse problem for generalized Runcorn's theorem related to lunar magnetism, using spherical harmonic analysis.
motivation: The work is motivated by an apparent paradox in lunar magnetism, aiming to characterize functions satisfying certain integral conditions.
method: The authors decompose square-integrable complex functions into spherical harmonics and provide explicit representations.
result: A characterization of functions satisfying the generalized Runcorn condition is obtained.
conclusion: The results contribute to the mathematical theory of inverse problems in geophysics, but have no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Finite Element Exponential Integration For Rough Solutions Of Nonlinear Wave Equations. Part Ii: Dynamic Boundary Conditions On Curved Domains
authors: Jiachuan Cao, Benjamin D\"orich, Buyang Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study nonlinear wave equations with dynamic boundary conditions on smooth bounded domains and analyze a fully discrete approximation in the low-regularity regime. The method combines isoparametric bulk--surface finite elements of degree [MATH] with an exponential integrator in time. Assuming only bounded energy of the exact solution, we prove convergence of the displacement--velocity pair in the weak norm [MATH]. The scheme achieves first-order convergence in time and spatial convergence of order [MATH] for [MATH] and [MATH] for [MATH]. In particular, these rates show that higher-order finite elements retain a provable asymptotic advantage even at low regularity. A central difficulty is that the continuous and discrete bulk--surface problems are posed on different geometries and must therefore be compared directly in weak norms. To address this, we develop a weak-norm framework for non-conforming geometries based on lift and adjoint-lift operators, combined with a frequency-decomposition argument. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first fully discrete low-regularity convergence result for nonlinear wave equations with dynamic boundary conditions in a non-conforming bulk--surface finite element setting. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted rates and illustrate the improved efficiency of higher-order methods.
tldr: This paper develops a finite element exponential integration method for nonlinear wave equations with dynamic boundary conditions on curved domains, focusing on low-regularity convergence.
motivation: Nonlinear wave equations with dynamic boundary conditions on curved domains are challenging to solve numerically, especially when the solution has low regularity. Existing methods lack rigorous convergence guarantees in this setting.
method: The method combines isoparametric bulk-surface finite elements with an exponential integrator in time. A weak-norm framework using lift and adjoint-lift operators handles the non-conforming geometry.
result: First-order convergence in time and spatial convergence of order h^{r+1/2} for r≥1 and h^{3/2} for r=0 are proved, showing higher-order elements retain advantage even at low regularity.
conclusion: This is the first fully discrete low-regularity convergence result for such problems, and numerical experiments confirm the predicted rates and efficiency of higher-order methods.

title: Convergence And Almost Sure Exponential Stability Of Compensated Split-step Theta Scheme For Stochastic Pantograph Models With Poisson Random Measure
authors: Amr Abosenna, Yongchun Zhou, Boping Tian
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, stochastic pantograph models have gained an intensive attention and have been used in different fields such as finance, biology, control and stochastic neural networks. It is also more preferable to incorporate jumps during the study of stochastic differential equations. In this paper, stochastic pantograph model with Poisson random measure is studied. The compensated split-step theta technique is applied to the considered model. The numerical scheme exhibits a non divergent attitude and converges to the solution of our model under assumptions addressed later on. Furthermore, the almost sure exponential stability of the numerical scheme is investigated via utilizing the discrete semi-martingale convergence theorem. Finally, theoretical findings are manifested via some numerical examples.
tldr: This paper studies the convergence and stability of a numerical scheme for stochastic pantograph models with jumps, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Stochastic pantograph models with Poisson jumps are used in finance, biology, and neural networks, but the paper focuses on numerical analysis rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The compensated split-step theta scheme is applied to the stochastic pantograph model, and the discrete semi-martingale convergence theorem is used to prove almost sure exponential stability.
result: The numerical scheme converges to the solution under certain assumptions and is almost surely exponentially stable.
conclusion: The theoretical findings are supported by numerical examples, but the work has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Harq For Slow Fluid Antenna Multiple Access
authors: Sixu Han, Kai-Kit Wong, Hanjiang Hong, Hyundong Shin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Slow fluid antenna multiple access (sFAMA), enabled by the fluid antenna system (FAS), has recently emerged as a practical and low-complexity paradigm for supporting massive wireless connectivity. While existing studies have characterized its physical-layer performance under one-shot transmission, its interaction with retransmission protocols and the resulting networking performance remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we study a downlink hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ)-assisted sFAMA framework, termed HARQ-sFAMA, in which each user performs distinguished port selection in every HARQ round and combines the received signals across multiple rounds to improve decoding reliability. We develop a comprehensive analytical framework to characterize the outage probability, average packet waiting time, and energy efficiency of the proposed system. The analysis reveals how HARQ exploits the spatial reconfigurability of FAS to simultaneously enhance reliability and improve queueing performance. Numerical results corroborate the theoretical analysis and demonstrate that the HARQ-sFAMA system significantly outperforms conventional one-shot sFAMA in terms of reliability, delay, and energy efficiency. These findings suggest that the integration of HARQ and sFAMA provides a promising pathway toward a practical and standards-compatible massive access solution for future wireless networks.
tldr: This paper studies a hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) protocol for slow fluid antenna multiple access (sFAMA) in wireless communications.
motivation: The interaction between retransmission protocols and sFAMA has not been explored, and the networking performance of sFAMA under HARQ is unknown.
method: The authors develop an analytical framework to characterize outage probability, average packet waiting time, and energy efficiency for the proposed HARQ-sFAMA system.
result: HARQ-sFAMA significantly outperforms conventional one-shot sFAMA in reliability, delay, and energy efficiency.
conclusion: Integrating HARQ with sFAMA provides a promising pathway toward practical massive access solutions for future wireless networks.

title: A National-Scale Ev Charging Scheduling Framework: Optimal Detour Routing Under Infrastructure Capacity Constraints
authors: Taner Cokyasar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As electric vehicle (EV) adoption grows, quantifying the scheduling burden and economic cost of long-distance travel under the existing charging infrastructure becomes increasingly important for infrastructure planning and policy. This paper presents a scalable, optimization-based framework for scheduling EV charging stops along real-world charging stations and simulated long-distance personal vehicle trajectories across the United States using POLARIS. Taking the existing charging network as fixed input, the framework minimizes total detour and queuing costs for each vehicle while respecting plug capacity constraints at each station. The methodology proceeds in three phases: (i) infeasibility pruning via a forward-pass reachability heuristic, (ii) per-vehicle optimal charging schedule computation via dynamic programming on a directed acyclic graph, and (iii) capacity-aware iterative congestion resolution through a penalty-based heuristic that augments detour costs at congested stations, with a first-in, first-out queue fallback. Applied to approximately 2.7M origin--destination vehicle trajectories derived from a 1\% sample of national personal travel demand within the POLARIS agent-based transportation simulation framework and covering 14,260 DC fast charging stations with 68,641 plugs from the Alternative Fuels Station Locator, the framework produces capacity-feasible schedules in under 1.3 hours on a 128-core high-performance computing cluster without requiring any commercial optimization solver. A three-tier economic analysis spanning operational costs, total cost of ownership, and amortized infrastructure investment is conducted to evaluate EV cost competitiveness relative to internal combustion engine vehicles across scenarios.
tldr: This paper presents an optimization framework for scheduling electric vehicle charging stops on long-distance trips, considering detour and queuing costs under infrastructure capacity constraints.
motivation: As EV adoption grows, there is a need to quantify the scheduling burden and economic cost of long-distance travel under existing charging infrastructure to inform planning and policy.
method: The framework uses a three-phase approach: infeasibility pruning via reachability heuristic, per-vehicle optimal scheduling via dynamic programming on a DAG, and capacity-aware iterative congestion resolution with penalty-based heuristics and FIFO queue fallback.
result: Applied to 2.7M trajectories and 14,260 stations, the framework produces capacity-feasible schedules in under 1.3 hours on a 128-core cluster without commercial solvers.
conclusion: The framework enables large-scale EV charging scheduling and economic analysis, demonstrating feasibility for national-scale infrastructure planning.

title: Block Diagonal Carleson Frames
authors: Brendan Miller Ilya Krishtal
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce , i.e. singly generated dynamical frames in which the generating operator is block diagonal. We classify all such frames when the generating operator is a direct sum of Jordan blocks, the sizes of which are uniformly bounded. Furthermore, block diagonal Carleson frames are shown to enjoy the high redundancy properties observed for Carleson frames. When the generating operator has nonnegative spectrum, we provide a complete description of the redundancy of such frames under the assumption of the existence of natural density.
tldr: This paper introduces block diagonal Carleson frames, a class of dynamical frames with block diagonal generating operators, and studies their classification and redundancy properties.
motivation: The authors aim to extend the theory of Carleson frames to a more general setting where the generating operator is block diagonal, which includes direct sums of Jordan blocks.
method: The paper provides a classification of all such frames when the generating operator is a direct sum of Jordan blocks with uniformly bounded sizes, and analyzes redundancy under nonnegative spectrum assumptions using natural density.
result: Block diagonal Carleson frames are shown to retain the high redundancy properties of standard Carleson frames, and a complete description of redundancy is given for operators with nonnegative spectrum.
conclusion: The work contributes to frame theory but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Revisit Escape Path For Infinite Unit Strip Forest And Unit Broadworm
authors: Zhipeng Deng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on our previous general computational solution to Bellman's Lost-in-a-Forest Problem, we present a new approach and analytical formulas for the previously well-known escape path for the infinite unit-strip forest and unit broadworm by Zalgaller. Earlier studies addressed these problems exclusively through geometric methods. We reformulated the problem as an interval-cover problem and then formulated it as a constrained functional minimization problem. This constrained functional minimization can be directly discretized and subsequently solved as a convex optimization. Furthermore, we extend the analysis of various line segment. Finally, we show that, in the case of a closed escape path for the unit strip, the optimal solution is a curve of constant unit width.
tldr: This paper solves a geometric optimization problem related to Bellman's Lost-in-a-Forest Problem, specifically the escape path for an infinite unit-strip forest and unit broadworm.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a new computational approach to a classic geometric problem that was previously solved only by geometric methods.
method: The problem is reformulated as an interval-cover problem and then as a constrained functional minimization problem, which is discretized and solved via convex optimization.
result: Analytical formulas for the escape path are derived, and it is shown that the optimal solution for a closed escape path in the unit strip is a curve of constant unit width.
conclusion: The work extends previous geometric solutions with a computational framework, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fragility Of Minimum-Variance Portfolios
authors: Daniel Ovalle, Carl D. Laird, Ignacio E. Grossmann, Javier Pe\~na
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Minimum-variance portfolios are well known to be highly sensitive to covariance estimation error. In this paper, we show that by imposing a block diagonal correlation structure, we can derive closed-form expressions for long-only minimum-variance portfolios that make this fragility explicit. These analytical solutions reveal that fragility is driven by threshold effects arising from the interaction between correlation structure and the assets' volatilities. Motivated by the latter insight, we propose robustification approaches that can be interpreted as structured shrinkage schemes that selectively attenuate unstable coupling while preserving the dominant risk structure. Unlike global shrinkage techniques, the proposed corrections are analytically grounded, require minimal tuning, and remain closely aligned with the minimum-variance solution. The framework extends naturally to general covariance matrices through clustering-based approximations. Empirical results on controlled simulations highlight a clear regime dependence. In homogeneous volatility settings, correlation-oblivious shrinkage achieves the best trade-off between risk and stability. In contrast, under heterogeneous volatility, correlation-aware shrinkage performs best by inducing sparsity and avoiding exposure to high-risk assets. Across regimes, the proposed methods consistently reduce out-of-sample variance and turnover relative to classical and clustering-based benchmarks, providing a principled and practical approach to robust portfolio construction.
tldr: This paper studies fragility of minimum-variance portfolios in finance, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Minimum-variance portfolios are sensitive to covariance estimation error, and the authors aim to understand and mitigate this fragility.
method: Closed-form expressions for long-only minimum-variance portfolios under block diagonal correlation structure are derived, and robustification approaches based on structured shrinkage are proposed.
result: Analytical solutions reveal threshold effects; correlation-aware shrinkage performs best under heterogeneous volatility, while correlation-oblivious shrinkage works in homogeneous settings.
conclusion: The proposed methods reduce out-of-sample variance and turnover, providing a principled approach to robust portfolio construction.

title: Gaffke's Confidence Interval For The Mean Of Bounded Data Is Inadmissible But Asymptotically Efficient
authors: Jiahao Ming, Aaditya Ramdas, Yi Shen, Ruodu Wang, Ian Waudby-Smith
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given observations [MATH], Gaffke (2005) defined \[ K_n(\mathbf x)=_{\mathbf D}\!\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n x_iD_i\le 1\right\}, \qquad (D_0,D_1,\ldots,D_n)\sim(1,\ldots,1), \] and conjectured that it is a [MATH]-value whenever the inputs are independent e-values. Recently, Vlassis and Thomas (2026) proved this conjecture. Inverting the tests for observations in [MATH] gives the confidence interval studied by Learned-Miller and Thomas (2020), which reduces to Clopper--Pearson for Bernoulli data. We give a finite- and large-sample account of Gaffke's test and interval. First, for every [MATH] and every elementary symmetric polynomial [MATH], \( K_n(\mathbf x)e_k(\mathbf x)\le {n\choose k}, \) so the Gaffke [MATH]-value never larger than the SymPol [MATH]-value of Ming et al. (2026). However, Gaffke's p-value is inadmissible. For [MATH], we construct a valid rule that is strictly smaller on mixed configurations and is the unique admissible rule that dominates [MATH]. A neutral-face extension proves inadmissibility of [MATH] for every [MATH]. If one independent uniform random variable is allowed, there is an even simpler full-dimensional improvement: on the upper orthant, where [MATH], replace it by [MATH]. The equal-tail Gaffke confidence interval [MATH] is nevertheless first-order asymptotically efficient: for iid observations on [MATH] with unknown variance [MATH], \[ \sqrt n\,(I_n)\longrightarrow 2\sigma z_{1-\alpha/2}\qquad. \] Our simulations also find that, among a variety of bounded-mean intervals considered, the Gaffke interval is the shortest, including comparisons with a recent empirical Berry--Esseen procedure having the same first-order Gaussian target.
tldr: This paper studies Gaffke's confidence interval for the mean of bounded data, proving its inadmissibility but asymptotic efficiency.
motivation: To provide a finite- and large-sample analysis of Gaffke's test and confidence interval, which is based on e-values and has applications in bounded-mean estimation.
method: The authors derive inequalities relating Gaffke's e-value to elementary symmetric polynomials, construct admissible dominating rules, and prove asymptotic normality of the interval width.
result: Gaffke's p-value is inadmissible for all n, but the equal-tail confidence interval is first-order asymptotically efficient with width converging to 2σ z_{1-α/2}/√n.
conclusion: Despite inadmissibility, Gaffke's interval is the shortest among bounded-mean intervals in simulations, making it practically useful.

title: Directional Derivatives And Error Bounds Of Merit Functions In Vector Optimization
authors: Yu Han
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of directional derivatives and error bounds for the merit function [MATH] associated with the vector optimization problem [MATH], where [MATH] is the oriented distance function. We first prove that [MATH] is concave and Lipschitz continuous on the whole space and derive its dual representation via the weak[MATH] compact convex set [MATH]. At a weakly efficient solution [MATH], we obtain the explicit formula [MATH] with [MATH], characterize the zero-directional-derivative cone, and prove that, under a local error bound condition, the tangent cone to the solution set is [MATH]. We establish the equivalence of thirteen distinct global error bound conditions, including characterizations via linear regularity, the global slope, an asymptotic condition, and perturbation stability. A central result shows that the global error bound property for [MATH] on the feasible set [MATH] is characterized by a uniform negativity condition on the unit-sphere minimal directional derivative, namely [MATH]. We also determine the optimal local error bound constant precisely as [MATH] when [MATH], and provide a counterexample demonstrating that an additional directional condition is essential when [MATH]. These results provide a complete bridge between the directional derivative of the merit function and the geometry of the solution set, offering fundamental tools for the convergence analysis of algorithms in vector optimization.
tldr: This paper studies directional derivatives and error bounds for merit functions in vector optimization, a topic in mathematical optimization.
motivation: To provide a complete bridge between directional derivatives of merit functions and the geometry of solution sets in vector optimization, offering tools for algorithm convergence analysis.
method: The paper proves concavity and Lipschitz continuity of the merit function, derives dual representations, characterizes zero-directional-derivative cones, and establishes equivalence of global error bound conditions.
result: Key results include explicit formulas for directional derivatives at weakly efficient solutions, characterization of global error bounds via uniform negativity conditions, and determination of optimal local error bound constants.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental tools for convergence analysis of algorithms in vector optimization, but the topic is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: On Free Generators In The Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller Lie Algebra
authors: Thomas Willwacher
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that any homogeneous family [MATH] in [MATH] with nonzero coefficients of [MATH] in [MATH] generates a free Lie subalgebra, building on the work of Brown.
tldr: This paper proves that certain homogeneous families in the Grothendieck-Teichmüller Lie algebra generate free Lie subalgebras.
motivation: The Grothendieck-Teichmüller Lie algebra is a fundamental object in number theory and algebraic geometry; understanding its structure is important for the study of the absolute Galois group.
method: The proof builds on the work of Brown and uses combinatorial and algebraic techniques to analyze the Lie algebra structure.
result: Any homogeneous family with nonzero coefficients of a specific element generates a free Lie subalgebra.
conclusion: The result provides new insight into the structure of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller Lie algebra.

title: A Lecture On Navier-Stokes Equations
authors: Sylvie Monniaux
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The content of the following pages was part of a special topics lecture given at the Australian National University during the first semester of 2026. That was a very nice expericence, I really enjoyed giving this 12 weeks (2 hours a week) lecture. It is meant to be self contained, starting with results on Fourier transform and Sobolev spaces. As a toy model, before treating the Navier-Stokes system, we focus on the non linear heat equation where the non linearity is polynomial. Ultimately, we prove existence and uniqueness of mild solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations in critical spaces. This script contains some exercises and the text of the mid-semester exam as well as the final exam.
tldr: This paper is a lecture series on the Navier-Stokes equations, focusing on existence and uniqueness of mild solutions in critical spaces.
motivation: The author aims to provide a self-contained introduction to the Navier-Stokes equations, starting from basic Fourier analysis and Sobolev spaces.
method: The lecture covers Fourier transform, Sobolev spaces, nonlinear heat equation as a toy model, and then proves existence and uniqueness of mild solutions for Navier-Stokes in critical spaces.
result: The paper presents a pedagogical exposition with exercises and exams, culminating in a proof of existence and uniqueness of mild solutions.
conclusion: The lecture successfully introduces key analytical tools and results for the Navier-Stokes equations, but does not contribute to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Learning Sufficient Low-dimensional Structures Through Conditional Optimal Transport
authors: Efstathia Bura Kaiqiang Alan Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sufficient dimension reduction seeks a low-dimensional covariate representation that preserves the conditional law of a response. We introduce SDR-COT, which represents that law by conditional optimal transport from an independent reference response. On separable Hilbert spaces, sufficiency forces the response component of the optimal triangular map to factor through the reduction. For quadratic cost, the induced interpolation has a Borel current-state velocity on every truncated time interval, without global injectivity of the terminal map, and this velocity has the same factorisation. These results motivate a conditional-flow-matching criterion. For linear reductions, we prove consistency using a suitably tuned relaxed empirical coupling. Euclidean responses are treated through slicewise Caffarelli bounds; Hilbert-valued responses are treated through Gaussian Sobolev regularity, interpolation compression and uniqueness of a Gaussian continuity equation. Numerical studies with Euclidean and functional data show competitive performance, especially when sufficient information is not solely contained in the conditional mean.
tldr: This paper introduces a method for sufficient dimension reduction using conditional optimal transport, with theoretical guarantees on Hilbert spaces.
motivation: To find low-dimensional representations of covariates that preserve the conditional distribution of a response, which is a classical problem in statistics.
method: The authors propose SDR-COT, which represents the conditional law via optimal transport from an independent reference, and use a conditional flow matching criterion for estimation.
result: They prove that sufficiency forces factorization through the reduction, and establish consistency for linear reductions using relaxed empirical coupling.
conclusion: The method shows competitive performance on Euclidean and functional data, especially when sufficient information is not solely in the conditional mean.

title: Flexible Intelligent Metasurface-Aided Isac: User Fairness Optimization And Performance Evaluation
authors: Hailun Huang, Yuwen Cao, Jiguang He, Tomoaki Ohtsuki
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates max-min user fairness optimization for flexible intelligent metasurface (FIM) and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems with active self-localization. To tackle the multi-user interference, performance imbalance, and neglected sensing accuracy problems encountered in conventional ISAC designs, we derive the closed-form Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) for angle-of-departure (AoD) estimation in target sensing and embed it into a max-min fairness optimization framework. The optimization problem, which jointly designs the base station transmit beamforming, FIM reflection coefficients, and surface deformation, is non-convex and solved by an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm. Notably, the devised optimization framework facilitates superior performance trade-off in terms of spectrum resource utilization between communication and sensing tasks. Simulation results validate that the proposed scheme significantly improves user fairness, balances communication performance and sensing precision effectively, and reveals the coupling characteristic between signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) and sensing CRLB. This work provides a feasible solution for FIM-aided ISAC system optimization in 6G networks.
tldr: This paper optimizes user fairness in FIM-NOMA-ISAC systems for 6G networks using alternating optimization.
motivation: Conventional ISAC designs suffer from multi-user interference, performance imbalance, and neglected sensing accuracy.
method: Derives closed-form CRLB for AoD estimation and embeds it into a max-min fairness optimization framework solved by alternating optimization.
result: The proposed scheme significantly improves user fairness and balances communication performance with sensing precision.
conclusion: Provides a feasible solution for FIM-aided ISAC system optimization in 6G networks.

title: A Frugal Primal-dual Splitting With Minimal Lifting Over Arbitrary Rooted Trees
authors: Hui Zhang Feng Xue
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a frugal primal-dual splitting with minimal lifting for solving structured monotone inclusions, involving cocoercive operators, linear compositions and parallel sums. This is established by defining hierarchical nodes and edges between them over a tree-structured graph, with arbitrary assignments of dual variables and cocoercive elements to primal nodes. This arbitrariness allows a great flexibility in terms of level-synchronous distributed computing, such as centralized or decentralized. The particular instances naturally extend the Douglas--Rachford splitting on various graphs, recover the parallel Chambolle--Pock, and solve a class of structured convex minimization problems with O(1/k) ergodic rate for its primal-dual gap function. Furthermore, we introduce a reformulation technique in a product Hilbert space to facilitate the convergence analysis, specifically to derive the o(1/k)-rate of asymptotic regularity.
tldr: This paper develops a frugal primal-dual splitting algorithm for solving structured monotone inclusions on tree-structured graphs.
motivation: To design a flexible distributed optimization algorithm with minimal lifting that can handle cocoercive operators and linear compositions.
method: The authors define hierarchical nodes and edges over a tree graph, assign dual variables and cocoercive elements arbitrarily to primal nodes, and use a reformulation in product Hilbert space for convergence analysis.
result: The algorithm achieves O(1/k) ergodic rate for the primal-dual gap and o(1/k) asymptotic regularity, generalizing Douglas-Rachford splitting and Chambolle-Pock.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a flexible framework for distributed convex optimization with proven convergence rates.

title: Characterizing The Dynamics Of Muscle Regeneration In The Mdx Mouse Model
authors: Elena Scibona, Davide Carbone, Lamberto Rondoni, Abramo Agosti
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we explore a model of immune response in the skeletal muscle of the mdx mouse, the preferred animal model for studying Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy. The system studied is based on existing literature and describes the reaction of the tissue, and of the immune cells within it, to external damage, focusing specifically on the regeneration process. This work extends the analysis conducted by the authors of the original paper, highlighting interesting dynamical properties of the system, particularly in terms of longterm behavior and dependence on initial conditions. A modification is then introduced to the original equations, incorporating a diffusion term for immune cells. The dynamics of the system is numerically investigated in both the one-dimensional and two-dimensional cases. Specifically, we investigate the effect of diffusion under various boundary conditions, and the system's response to localized damage.
tldr: This paper models immune response and muscle regeneration in the mdx mouse model of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy, focusing on dynamical properties and diffusion effects.
motivation: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy is a severe muscle-wasting disease, and understanding the dynamics of muscle regeneration in the mdx mouse model can inform therapeutic strategies.
method: The authors extend an existing model by adding a diffusion term for immune cells and numerically investigate the system's dynamics in 1D and 2D under various boundary conditions and localized damage.
result: The study reveals interesting long-term behavior and dependence on initial conditions, and shows how diffusion affects the regeneration process.
conclusion: The modified model captures key aspects of muscle regeneration dynamics, providing insights that could guide future experimental and theoretical work.

title: A Refined Structure Theorem For Polynomial Return-time Sets In Minimal Systems
authors: Ioannis Kousek
abstract: ArXiv:2607.18987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a refinement of a recent structural result in topological dynamics due to Glasscock, Koutsogiannis, Le, Moreira, Richter, and Robertson, who showed that in a minimal system, polynomial return-times differ by non-piecewise syndetic sets from those in its maximal infinite-step pronilfactor. In particular, we prove that the infinite-step pronilfactor can be replaced by the maximal [MATH]-step pronilfactor of the system, where [MATH] depends only on the given polynomials, with [MATH] equal to the Host-Kra complexity of the polynomials.
tldr: This paper refines a structural result in topological dynamics about polynomial return-time sets in minimal systems, replacing the infinite-step pronilfactor with a finite-step one depending on polynomial complexity.
motivation: To improve the understanding of polynomial return-time sets in minimal dynamical systems by reducing the required pronilfactor to a finite step.
method: The author proves a refinement of a theorem by Glasscock et al., showing that the infinite-step pronilfactor can be replaced by the maximal M-step pronilfactor where M is the Host-Kra complexity of the polynomials.
result: The polynomial return-time sets differ from those in the maximal M-step pronilfactor by non-piecewise syndetic sets, with M determined by the polynomials' Host-Kra complexity.
conclusion: This provides a more precise structural description of polynomial return-time sets in minimal systems, advancing topological dynamics.

title: Graphical Stability Of Set-valued Integrals Under Measure Perturbations
authors: Tam Le
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by sampling and approximation schemes arising in nonsmooth optimization, we study the stability of parameterized set-valued integrals under weak perturbations of the underlying probability distribution. For a compact parameter set, we show that compact convex-valued and jointly outer semicontinuous integrands induce set-valued integral maps that converge graphically in excess distance along any weakly convergent sequence of probability measures. The result holds under a superlinear integrability condition and provides a unified stability principle for measure approximations of set-valued expectations. We discuss the sharpness of the assumptions through examples. In particular, we emphasize that joint outer semicontinuity is required in general and that the superlinear envelope condition is tight relative to the classical i.i.d. empirical setting. As a consequence, we obtain outer stability of solution sets for stochastic generalized equations. We illustrate the stability result in several settings, including stochastic nonsmooth optimization with Markovian sampling, smoothing by mollifiers, and parameter-dependent distributional dynamics.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of set-valued integrals under measure perturbations, with applications in nonsmooth optimization.
motivation: To provide a unified stability principle for measure approximations of set-valued expectations, motivated by sampling and approximation schemes in nonsmooth optimization.
method: The authors prove that compact convex-valued and jointly outer semicontinuous integrands induce set-valued integral maps that converge graphically in excess distance along weakly convergent sequences of probability measures, under a superlinear integrability condition.
result: The result holds under a superlinear integrability condition and is sharp; it yields outer stability of solution sets for stochastic generalized equations.
conclusion: The stability result is illustrated in stochastic nonsmooth optimization with Markovian sampling, smoothing by mollifiers, and parameter-dependent distributional dynamics.

title: On The Performance Of Fluid Antenna Systems Under Block-Diagonal Correlation Model
authors: Jiangsheng Huangfu, Zhengyu Song, Tianwei Hou, Anna Li, Kai Kit Wong
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FASs) have recently emerged as a promising reconfigurable antenna technology for future wireless networks, owing to their unique ability to exploit fine-grained spatial channel variations within a compact aperture. In this paper, a single-input multiple-output (SIMO) FAS employing maximum-ratio combining (MRC) is investigated under the block-diagonal correlation model, where the ports of FAS are partitioned into independent blocks and the strongest port within each block is selected for MRC combining. Exact outage probability (OP) expressions are first derived in both convolution and characteristic-function forms. To gain further insights, closed-form high-SNR asymptotic expressions are developed, from which the diversity order is shown to approximate the number of ports. This result reveals that block partitioning influences only the coding gain and can therefore be optimized without compromising the diversity performance. For the ergodic rate (ER), a Gamma-matching approximation together with a tighter Jensen-based approximation is derived in closed form. Simulation results corroborate the analytical framework and demonstrate that: i) increasing either the number of ports or the number of blocks improves the system performance; ii) the diversity order depends solely on the number of ports; and iii) the proposed SIMO-FAS achieves comparable or superior outage performance to conventional MRC receivers despite employing fewer combining branches.
tldr: This paper analyzes the performance of fluid antenna systems under a block-diagonal correlation model for wireless communications.
motivation: Fluid antenna systems are a promising reconfigurable antenna technology for future wireless networks, and understanding their performance under realistic correlation models is important.
method: The authors derive exact outage probability expressions and closed-form high-SNR asymptotic expressions for a SIMO-FAS with MRC, and also derive Gamma-matching and Jensen-based approximations for ergodic rate.
result: The diversity order approximates the number of ports, block partitioning affects only coding gain, and increasing ports or blocks improves performance.
conclusion: The proposed SIMO-FAS achieves comparable or superior outage performance to conventional MRC receivers with fewer combining branches.

title: Industrial Application Of A Multi-Disciplinary Design Optimization With Uncertainties To A Pair Of Telecommunication Satellites
authors: Olivier Sapin (ADS), Lo\"ic Cousin (ADS), Nicolas Roussouly (ADS), Anne Gazaix (ADS), Fran\c{c}ois Gallard (ADS), Matthias de Lozzo (ADS), Xavier Fosse (ADS), Nicolas Sarda (ADS), Gaspard Berthelin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In satellite design, it is common practice to add safety margins to the constraints to achieve conservative solutions that are robust to uncertainties. This robustness often comes at the expense of performance and it may be more appropriate to include uncertainties in the definition of the design problem. This work addresses such a challenge by applying techniques of multidisciplinary design optimization under uncertainty to an industrial use case. The latter is a pair of telecommunication satellites launched together in a stacked configuration. Each satellite is a strongly coupled multidisciplinary system while the two satellites are not coupled at all. This use case can be extended to an arbitrary number of satellites. By considering uncertainty quantification techniques such as sensitivity analysis and reliability-based design optimization, this study demonstrates that accounting for uncertainties in the design problem results in a 66% reduction in performance loss compared to the adding of a predefined safety margins, while guaranteeing the feasibility of constraints with high probability.
tldr: This paper applies multidisciplinary design optimization under uncertainty to telecommunication satellite design, demonstrating a 66% reduction in performance loss compared to traditional safety margins.
motivation: In satellite design, safety margins are commonly used to ensure robustness against uncertainties, but this often sacrifices performance. The authors aim to incorporate uncertainties directly into the design optimization to achieve better performance while maintaining reliability.
method: The authors employ uncertainty quantification techniques including sensitivity analysis and reliability-based design optimization on a pair of telecommunication satellites launched in a stacked configuration, treating each satellite as a strongly coupled multidisciplinary system.
result: The proposed approach reduces performance loss by 66% compared to using predefined safety margins, while still guaranteeing constraint feasibility with high probability.
conclusion: Accounting for uncertainties in the design problem can significantly improve performance over traditional safety margin approaches, and the methodology can be extended to an arbitrary number of satellites.

title: Decentralized Linearized Consensus Admm With Efficient Quantized Communication
authors: Boyu Han, Xu Du, Karl H. Johansson, Apostolos I. Rikos
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed optimization offers significant advantages over centralized methods in terms of scalability and robustness when solving large-scale problems. In this paper, we propose a novel decentralized optimization algorithm that integrates Inexact Consensus ADMM (IC-ADMM) with a finite-time decentralized quantized communication algorithm. The proposed method enjoys three main benefits: (i) it operates on directed communication graphs, (ii) it requires only quantized local information instead of exact values, and (iii) it does not rely on solving the local subproblems exactly. Under the assumption that each node's local objective is strongly convex and L-smooth, the algorithm is guaranteed to achieve global linear convergence to a neighborhood of the optimal solution. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate its advantages over existing methods in terms of convergence speed and communication efficiency.
tldr: This paper proposes a decentralized optimization algorithm using quantized communication and inexact consensus ADMM for directed graphs.
motivation: Distributed optimization faces challenges in communication efficiency and robustness; existing methods often require exact information or undirected graphs.
method: The algorithm integrates Inexact Consensus ADMM with a finite-time decentralized quantized communication scheme, allowing directed graphs and quantized local information.
result: Under strong convexity and L-smoothness assumptions, the algorithm achieves global linear convergence to a neighborhood of the optimal solution.
conclusion: The proposed method improves convergence speed and communication efficiency over existing approaches, as demonstrated by numerical experiments.

title: The Influence Function Of Transport-based Quantiles
authors: Alberto Gonz\'alez-Sanz, Shunan Sheng, Bohan Wu, Marco Avella Medina
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transport-based quantiles extend univariate quantiles to multivariate distributions via optimal transport. We study the influence function of the transport quantile map [MATH], defined as the optimal transport map pushing a fixed reference measure [MATH] forward to a target distribution [MATH]. For the Huber contamination [MATH], we prove that the first-order limit [MATH] exists whenever [MATH] and characterize it uniquely. Specifically, [MATH], where [MATH] is characterized by a uniformly elliptic equation with a Dirac source and a Neumann boundary condition. In every dimension [MATH], this influence function has a pole-type singularity. For fixed [MATH], it remains bounded when [MATH] stays away from [MATH], where [MATH] is the transport-based distribution function, but diverges as [MATH], equivalently as [MATH]. In fact, [MATH]. This contrasts with the bounded influence function of univariate quantiles and implies that [MATH], for [MATH], has infinite second moment. Numerical experiments further suggest that empirical transport quantiles may exhibit stable-type non-Gaussian fluctuations.
tldr: This paper studies the influence function of transport-based quantiles for multivariate distributions, revealing a pole-type singularity and infinite second moment.
motivation: To understand the robustness properties of transport-based quantiles, which extend univariate quantiles to multivariate settings via optimal transport.
method: The authors analyze the first-order limit of the transport quantile map under Huber contamination, characterizing it via a uniformly elliptic PDE with a Dirac source and Neumann boundary condition.
result: The influence function has a pole-type singularity in any dimension, diverging as the contamination point approaches the quantile level, leading to infinite second moment of the influence function.
conclusion: Transport-based quantiles are not robust in the classical sense, unlike univariate quantiles, and empirical transport quantiles may exhibit non-Gaussian fluctuations.

title: Identifiability, Convergence And Nonparametric Estimation Of Bivariate Archimax Copulas
authors: Wolfgang Trutschnig Nicolas Dietrich
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Considering that the family of bivariate Archimax copulas contains both the Archimedean and the extreme-value class, Archimax copulas constitute a flexible family allowing to model extreme and moderate levels of dependence. Despite their appeal, no fully nonparametric, consistent estimator that is itself an element of the Archimax family [MATH] has been established yet, mainly because Archimedean generators and Pickands dependence functions alone do not identify Archimax copulas. We resolve this identifiability issue by working with transformed generators and transformed Pickands dependence functions, and show that these functions do identify the Archimax copula uniquely. Building upon this result, we prove that uniform convergence of Archimax copulas is equivalent to uniform convergence of the corresponding transformed generators and Pickands dependence functions. Moreover, as for Archimedean and extreme-value copulas, uniform convergence in [MATH] is equivalent to weak convergence of almost all conditional distributions. Exploiting these equivalences, we construct two nonparametric estimators for Archimax copulas (a Pickands and a CFG type estimator, both elements of [MATH]) and show that they are strongly consistent under mild regularity conditions. As a further consequence of the aforementioned weak conditional convergence, we obtain strongly consistent plug-in estimators for measures of directed dependence such as Chatterjee's [MATH] and Trutschnig's [MATH]. A large-scale simulation study shows that the proposed CFG type estimator outperforms both the standard empirical copula estimator and the Pickands type estimator; an application to precipitation data from Bregenz and Dornbirn (Austria) illustrates the practical use of our estimators on real data.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Space-time Tensor-product Finite Element Methods For Parabolic Problems
authors: Richard L\"oscher, Michael Reichelt, Olaf Steinbach
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19107v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study space-time Galerkin--Petrov formulations for parabolic evolution problems and their relation to classical implicit time-stepping schemes. Although such schemes are stable in the usual time-stepping sense, their interpretation as space-time operator equations may lead to conditional stability, with constants depending on the relation between temporal and spatial mesh sizes. We revisit this phenomenon for the continuous Galerkin method of Aziz and Monk, which yields the Crank--Nicolson scheme in the lowest-order case, and provide a detailed space-time error analysis for solutions of both high and low regularity. In particular, the space-time framework allows us to analyze the deteriorated behaviour of classical time-stepping methods for nonsmooth initial data. By applying integration by parts in time, we derive an adjoint space-time formulation that incorporates the initial condition in a natural variational way. In the lowest-order case, this formulation leads to a Rannacher-type smoothing of the initial data. The theoretical results are complemented by numerical experiments.
tldr: This paper develops space-time finite element methods for parabolic PDEs, focusing on stability and error analysis.
motivation: Classical time-stepping schemes for parabolic problems can exhibit conditional stability when interpreted as space-time operator equations, motivating a unified space-time framework.
method: The authors study Galerkin-Petrov formulations, derive an adjoint formulation with natural initial condition incorporation, and analyze the continuous Galerkin method of Aziz and Monk.
result: The space-time framework reveals deteriorated behavior for nonsmooth initial data and leads to a Rannacher-type smoothing in the lowest-order case.
conclusion: Space-time formulations provide a rigorous error analysis and can improve the treatment of initial conditions in parabolic problems.

title: Invariants Of The Extended Twisted $h$-Yangian
authors: Lucia Bagnoli, Slaven Ko\v{z}i\'c, Jian Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the extended twisted [MATH]-Yangian [MATH], a certain algebra which admits both the orthogonal and the symplectic [MATH]-Yangian as its quotients. We show that [MATH] is naturally equipped with the structure of restricted module for a certain algebra [MATH], which resembles the quantum double, as well as with the structure of [MATH]-coordinated quasi module for the Etingof-Kazhdan quantum affine vertex algebra associated with the trigonometric [MATH]-matrix of type [MATH]. Finally, we demonstrate how the elements of the quantum Feigin--Frenkel center give rise to explicit formulas for central elements of [MATH] and invariants of [MATH] at the critical level, as well as to commutative families in the orthogonal and symplectic [MATH]-Yangians.
tldr: This paper studies the algebraic structure of extended twisted h-Yangians and their invariants, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the structure of extended twisted h-Yangians and their relationship to quantum affine vertex algebras.
method: They show the algebra is a restricted module for a quantum-double-like algebra and a quasi module for the Etingof-Kazhdan quantum affine vertex algebra, then derive central elements and invariants.
result: Explicit formulas for central elements and invariants at the critical level are obtained, along with commutative families in orthogonal and symplectic Yangians.
conclusion: The work contributes to representation theory and algebraic structures, but does not address any topics in the user's research interests.

title: Active Disturbance Rejection For Boundary Control Systems
authors: Lassi Paunonen Jukka-Pekka Humaloja
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider stabilisation of abstract boundary control systems and controlled partial differential equations with general unknown input disturbances and unmodeled nonlinearities at the input. We utilise the active disturbance rejection control approach to design a controller which rejects the input disturbance and achieves stability and external well-posedness of the closed-loop system for a class of boundary control systems with collocated inputs and outputs. We apply our main results to design controllers for one-dimensional wave and heat equations.
tldr: This paper applies active disturbance rejection control to stabilize boundary control systems with unknown input disturbances.
motivation: Boundary control systems are susceptible to unknown disturbances and nonlinearities that degrade performance; a robust controller is needed.
method: The authors design an active disturbance rejection controller that estimates and cancels disturbances, proving stability and well-posedness for collocated input-output systems.
result: The controller achieves asymptotic stability and external well-posedness for a class of boundary control systems, demonstrated on wave and heat equations.
conclusion: Active disturbance rejection control is effective for stabilizing boundary control systems under unknown disturbances.

title: A Relaxed-inertial Proximal Point Algorithm For Strongly Quasiconvex Equilibrium Problems On Hadamard Manifolds
authors: Nicholas Pischke Luisa Marie Despr\'es
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19164v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a proximal point type method for approximating solutions to equilibrium problems generated by pseudomonotone and strongly quasiconvex bifunctions over Hadamard manifolds, that is complete simply connected Riemannian manifolds of nonpositive sectional curvature. Next to the usual proximal step, the method we consider also incorporates an inertia step together with a subsequent over-relaxation, the latter of which is treated in the context of Hadamard manifolds, to our knowledge, for the first time. Making use of a quantitative approach towards such proximal methods for strongly quasiconvex optimization developed by the authors in previous work, we in particular provide effective arguments for the convergence of the method, yielding explicit, fast and very uniform rates of convergence for the distance of the iterates towards the solution. These results extend previous work by Grad, Lara and Marcavillaca on such a method over finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces for the first time to a nonlinear setting, with the quantitative estimates already being novel in the Euclidean case. In particular, our effective approach allows for a fine-grained view on the assumptions on the surrounding objects, so that we are able to either weaken or even fully discharge some previous assumptions.
tldr: This paper proposes a relaxed-inertial proximal point algorithm for solving equilibrium problems on Hadamard manifolds, focusing on strongly quasiconvex bifunctions.
motivation: Extend existing proximal point methods from Euclidean spaces to nonlinear Hadamard manifolds, and improve convergence rates for strongly quasiconvex equilibrium problems.
method: Combines a proximal step with an inertia step and over-relaxation, analyzed using quantitative convergence arguments developed by the authors.
result: Provides explicit, fast, and uniform convergence rates for the distance of iterates to the solution, weakening or removing some previous assumptions.
conclusion: The method generalizes previous work to nonlinear settings and offers improved convergence guarantees.

title: Boundary-Adapted PINNs For Elliptic Dirichlet Problems: $H^2(\Omega)$ A Priori Error Bounds With Application To Mean Escape Time Computation
authors: Nathanael Tepakbong, Jun Fan, Xiang Zhou, Ding-Xuan Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the numerical computation of the Mean Escape Time (MET) [MATH] of a stochastic process from a bounded domain [MATH], we study elliptic Dirichlet boundary value problems (BVPs) using boundary-enforced Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), in which the Dirichlet condition is imposed exactly by multiplying the network output with a predefined distance-to-boundary approximation [MATH]. Combining approximation-theoretic and statistical-learning arguments for Rectified Quadratic Unit (ReQU) and hyperbolic tangent (tanh) networks, we derive a priori error bounds that make explicit the dependence on [MATH]. In particular, we show that exact boundary enforcement alone is not enough for [MATH] error bounds, and that a sufficient and essentially necessary condition is for [MATH] to be a smooth distance approximation [MATH], of the kind constructed in arXiv:2104.08426 [math.NA]. We thereby identify this subclass of [MATH] PINNs as the appropriate neural network ansatz for solving Dirichlet BVPs. Numerical experiments support the theory, showing that appropriate choices of [MATH] improve accuracy and convergence, while poorly chosen distance functions can substantially degrade the solution. Our proof also yields new VC-dimension bounds for hypothesis spaces of higher-order derivatives of ReQU and tanh networks, together with new approximation bounds for shallow ReQU networks in higher-order Sobolev norms, all of which are of important independent interest.
tldr: This paper develops boundary-adapted physics-informed neural networks for solving elliptic Dirichlet problems and provides a priori error bounds, with application to mean escape time computation.
motivation: Accurate numerical computation of mean escape times for stochastic processes requires solving elliptic Dirichlet boundary value problems, which motivates the development of improved neural network methods.
method: The authors propose boundary-enforced PINNs that exactly impose Dirichlet conditions using a distance-to-boundary function, and derive a priori error bounds using approximation-theoretic and statistical-learning arguments for ReQU and tanh networks.
result: They show that exact boundary enforcement alone is insufficient for H^2 error bounds; a smooth distance approximation is necessary and sufficient. They also obtain new VC-dimension bounds for higher-order derivatives of ReQU and tanh networks.
conclusion: The identified subclass of boundary-adapted PINNs is appropriate for solving Dirichlet BVPs, with numerical experiments confirming that proper distance functions improve accuracy and convergence.

title: Numerical Methods For Langevin-type Spde: An Implicit Milstein Approach And Multilevel Monte Carlo Techniques
authors: Carlos V\'azquez Sascha Portaro
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19188v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the numerical approximation of degenerate Langevin-type stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) in two spatial dimensions. These SPDEs arise in stochastic dynamics and mathematical finance, among other applications. In order to handle the mixed deterministic-stochastic structure of the equation and the degeneracy of the differential operator, we propose a semi-implicit Milstein finite difference scheme for the numerical solution. Through the Fourier analysis of the mean-square stability and convergence, we derive explicit conditions on the coefficients under which the scheme is stable, jointly with explicit convergence rates in terms of the discretization parameters. We further embed the proposed scheme within a Multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) framework to reduce the computational cost associated with SPDE simulations, and we derive its theoretical computational complexity. Numerical experiments confirm theoretical convergence rates and show that the MLMC strategy achieves an accuracy comparable to standard Monte Carlo at a fraction of the computational cost, reducing the complexity from [MATH] to [MATH] for a target root-mean-square error [MATH]. These results show that combining semi-implicit Milstein schemes with MLMC techniques provides an effective approach for the numerical simulation of Langevin-type SPDEs.
tldr: This paper develops numerical methods for Langevin-type SPDEs, focusing on a semi-implicit Milstein scheme and multilevel Monte Carlo techniques.
motivation: Langevin-type SPDEs arise in stochastic dynamics and mathematical finance, but their numerical approximation is challenging due to degeneracy and mixed deterministic-stochastic structure.
method: A semi-implicit Milstein finite difference scheme is proposed, with stability and convergence analyzed via Fourier analysis. The scheme is embedded in a Multilevel Monte Carlo framework to reduce computational cost.
result: Explicit stability conditions and convergence rates are derived. Numerical experiments show the MLMC strategy achieves comparable accuracy to standard Monte Carlo at reduced computational complexity.
conclusion: Combining semi-implicit Milstein schemes with MLMC provides an effective approach for simulating Langevin-type SPDEs.

title: Squeezing The Most Out Of Preemption For AoI Minimization: Single-source Case
authors: Nail Akar, Mohammad Moltafet, Sennur Ulukus, Marian Codreanu, Roy D. Yates
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study a single-source single-server continuous-time status update system where the updates arrive according to a Poisson process and update service times are generally distributed. In our proposed setting, a preemption policy refers to one where a new update preempts the ongoing one with a probability depending on the age of the update in service. We first propose an analytical method to derive the average age of information (AoI) and average peak AoI (PAoI) for any such preemption policy. This analysis is then utilized to tune two particular preemption policies: (i) probabilistic preemption (PP), in which preemption takes place according to a fixed probability regardless of the update age, (ii) threshold-based preemption (TP), for which preemption is incurred when the update age exceeds a certain threshold, both using one-dimensional line search. The effectiveness of policy tuning for the PP and TP policies is validated using lognormal-distributed update service times.
